courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
Foundations of Diplomatic Protocol and International Conduct
• Understanding the purpose and strategic value of protocol in building trust, facilitating cooperation and protecting organisational reputation in international settings
• Exploring the core principles that underpin effective diplomatic practice across different cultural, political and organisational contexts
• Identifying common protocol challenges and risks faced by professionals and organisations engaging in international activities
• Establishing the direct link between protocol excellence, organisational credibility and successful stakeholders and diplomatic outcomes
• Recognising how protocol supports broader diplomatic, commercial, governmental and strategic objectives
• Mapping the practical development pathway from foundational knowledge to advanced application and sustainable organisational integration

MODULE 02
Principles of International Etiquette and Cross-Cultural Intelligence
• Examining key dimensions of cross-cultural communication that influence professional interactions, trust-building and relationship development
• Developing practical awareness of cultural variations in greetings, forms of address, gift-giving, dining and conversational norms
• Practising techniques for adapting behaviour respectfully while maintaining authenticity and professionalism in diverse international settings
• Understanding the role of non-verbal communication, body language, personal space and timing in international etiquette
• Building capability to interpret cultural signals accurately and respond appropriately during high-stakes professional engagements
• Creating personal and organisational approaches to continuous cross-cultural learning, reflection and adaptation

MODULE 03
Protocol for Official Visits, Summits and High-Level Bilateral Meetings
• Planning and coordinating comprehensive protocol arrangements for incoming and outgoing high-level visits, delegations and official programmes
• Establishing correct order of precedence, seating arrangements and logistical sequences that reflect accepted diplomatic norms
• Managing arrival ceremonies, welcome procedures, bilateral meeting protocols, official photography and departure formalities with precision
• Coordinating effectively with host teams, visiting delegations and multiple internal stakeholders to ensure seamless execution
• Handling national symbols, flags, anthems and sensitive representational elements with accuracy and cultural respect
• Developing detailed checklists, timelines and contingency plans that prevent protocol failures during critical high-level engagements

MODULE 04
State Ceremonial Practice, Flags, Anthems and Order of Precedence
• Understanding the significance, correct display and protocols governing national flags, anthems and other state symbols in official settings
• Applying rules of precedence consistently in seating, processions, toasts, speeches and official documentation
• Designing and managing ceremonial elements for state dinners, receptions, award ceremonies, openings and official events
• Coordinating with security, military, venue and protocol counterparts to deliver dignified, error-free and culturally appropriate ceremonies
• Adapting ceremonial practice to different venue types, event scales, cultural contexts and organisational requirements
• Building internal capability to advise on and oversee ceremonial aspects of major international and organisational events

MODULE 05
Gift Exchange, Hospitality and Social Protocol in International Relations
• Developing clear guidelines for appropriate gift selection, presentation, reciprocity and documentation in diplomatic and international business contexts
• Managing hospitality arrangements including hosting, guest protocols, dietary and religious considerations and cultural sensitivities
• Understanding the strategic role of social events, dinners and informal gatherings in advancing diplomatic, governmental and commercial objectives
• Handling invitations, RSVPs, seating at social functions, thank-you protocols and follow-up communications with professionalism
• Navigating complex situations involving spouses, partners, cultural taboos, dietary restrictions and unexpected protocol challenges
• Establishing organisational policies, training and quality standards that ensure consistent, respectful and effective hospitality practice globally

MODULE 06
Virtual, Hybrid and Digital Diplomatic Protocol
• Adapting traditional protocol principles and standards to virtual summits, hybrid meetings and digital diplomatic engagements
• Managing online platform etiquette, camera presence, virtual seating arrangements, digital flag displays and interpretation protocols
• Handling time zone coordination, recording and documentation standards, and secure communication platform requirements
• Developing best practices for virtual gift exchanges, online toasts, remote ceremonial participation and digital hospitality
• Addressing cybersecurity, data privacy, platform security and confidentiality considerations in digital diplomatic practice
• Building organisational readiness and confidence to conduct high-level international business effectively in hybrid and virtual environments

MODULE 07
Managing Protocol Breaches, Incidents and Sensitive Situations
• Identifying potential protocol risks, early warning signs and cultural sensitivities during the planning and execution of international engagements
• Developing rapid yet diplomatic response protocols for addressing accidental breaches, misunderstandings or deliberate provocations
• Managing media interest, stakeholder communications, internal reporting and reputation protection following protocol incidents
• Conducting structured post-incident reviews that extract lessons and strengthen future practice without assigning personal blame
• Balancing firmness with diplomatic sensitivity when addressing protocol violations or cultural missteps by other parties
• Creating organisational learning systems that convert protocol challenges into improved capability, resilience and preventive practice

MODULE 08
Building Sustainable Protocol Capability and Organisational Excellence
• Designing internal protocol frameworks, manuals, checklists and training programmes tailored to specific organisational needs and risk profiles
• Establishing clear protocol roles, responsibilities and coordination mechanisms within government relations, external affairs or corporate diplomacy functions
• Developing practical approaches to measure protocol effectiveness, gather feedback and drive continuous improvement
• Integrating protocol considerations into broader international strategy, risk management, stakeholder engagement and organisational planning
• Mentoring and developing internal champions who can sustain high standards of diplomatic conduct and etiquette across the organisation
• Positioning protocol and international etiquette excellence as a strategic organisational asset that enhances credibility, trust and influence globally
• Assessment & Evaluation
• Upon successful completion of this programme, an Elevoris Certificate of Training will be awarded to delegates who meet the passing requirements.

sourceRecord.courseSyllabus:
MODULE 01
Foundations of Diplomatic Protocol and International Conduct
• Understanding the purpose and strategic value of protocol in building trust, facilitating cooperation and protecting organisational reputation in international settings
• Exploring the core principles that underpin effective diplomatic practice across different cultural, political and organisational contexts
• Identifying common protocol challenges and risks faced by professionals and organisations engaging in international activities
• Establishing the direct link between protocol excellence, organisational credibility and successful stakeholders and diplomatic outcomes
• Recognising how protocol supports broader diplomatic, commercial, governmental and strategic objectives
• Mapping the practical development pathway from foundational knowledge to advanced application and sustainable organisational integration

MODULE 02
Principles of International Etiquette and Cross-Cultural Intelligence
• Examining key dimensions of cross-cultural communication that influence professional interactions, trust-building and relationship development
• Developing practical awareness of cultural variations in greetings, forms of address, gift-giving, dining and conversational norms
• Practising techniques for adapting behaviour respectfully while maintaining authenticity and professionalism in diverse international settings
• Understanding the role of non-verbal communication, body language, personal space and timing in international etiquette
• Building capability to interpret cultural signals accurately and respond appropriately during high-stakes professional engagements
• Creating personal and organisational approaches to continuous cross-cultural learning, reflection and adaptation

MODULE 03
Protocol for Official Visits, Summits and High-Level Bilateral Meetings
• Planning and coordinating comprehensive protocol arrangements for incoming and outgoing high-level visits, delegations and official programmes
• Establishing correct order of precedence, seating arrangements and logistical sequences that reflect accepted diplomatic norms
• Managing arrival ceremonies, welcome procedures, bilateral meeting protocols, official photography and departure formalities with precision
• Coordinating effectively with host teams, visiting delegations and multiple internal stakeholders to ensure seamless execution
• Handling national symbols, flags, anthems and sensitive representational elements with accuracy and cultural respect
• Developing detailed checklists, timelines and contingency plans that prevent protocol failures during critical high-level engagements

MODULE 04
State Ceremonial Practice, Flags, Anthems and Order of Precedence
• Understanding the significance, correct display and protocols governing national flags, anthems and other state symbols in official settings
• Applying rules of precedence consistently in seating, processions, toasts, speeches and official documentation
• Designing and managing ceremonial elements for state dinners, receptions, award ceremonies, openings and official events
• Coordinating with security, military, venue and protocol counterparts to deliver dignified, error-free and culturally appropriate ceremonies
• Adapting ceremonial practice to different venue types, event scales, cultural contexts and organisational requirements
• Building internal capability to advise on and oversee ceremonial aspects of major international and organisational events

MODULE 05
Gift Exchange, Hospitality and Social Protocol in International Relations
• Developing clear guidelines for appropriate gift selection, presentation, reciprocity and documentation in diplomatic and international business contexts
• Managing hospitality arrangements including hosting, guest protocols, dietary and religious considerations and cultural sensitivities
• Understanding the strategic role of social events, dinners and informal gatherings in advancing diplomatic, governmental and commercial objectives
• Handling invitations, RSVPs, seating at social functions, thank-you protocols and follow-up communications with professionalism
• Navigating complex situations involving spouses, partners, cultural taboos, dietary restrictions and unexpected protocol challenges
• Establishing organisational policies, training and quality standards that ensure consistent, respectful and effective hospitality practice globally

MODULE 06
Virtual, Hybrid and Digital Diplomatic Protocol
• Adapting traditional protocol principles and standards to virtual summits, hybrid meetings and digital diplomatic engagements
• Managing online platform etiquette, camera presence, virtual seating arrangements, digital flag displays and interpretation protocols
• Handling time zone coordination, recording and documentation standards, and secure communication platform requirements
• Developing best practices for virtual gift exchanges, online toasts, remote ceremonial participation and digital hospitality
• Addressing cybersecurity, data privacy, platform security and confidentiality considerations in digital diplomatic practice
• Building organisational readiness and confidence to conduct high-level international business effectively in hybrid and virtual environments

MODULE 07
Managing Protocol Breaches, Incidents and Sensitive Situations
• Identifying potential protocol risks, early warning signs and cultural sensitivities during the planning and execution of international engagements
• Developing rapid yet diplomatic response protocols for addressing accidental breaches, misunderstandings or deliberate provocations
• Managing media interest, stakeholder communications, internal reporting and reputation protection following protocol incidents
• Conducting structured post-incident reviews that extract lessons and strengthen future practice without assigning personal blame
• Balancing firmness with diplomatic sensitivity when addressing protocol violations or cultural missteps by other parties
• Creating organisational learning systems that convert protocol challenges into improved capability, resilience and preventive practice

MODULE 08
Building Sustainable Protocol Capability and Organisational Excellence
• Designing internal protocol frameworks, manuals, checklists and training programmes tailored to specific organisational needs and risk profiles
• Establishing clear protocol roles, responsibilities and coordination mechanisms within government relations, external affairs or corporate diplomacy functions
• Developing practical approaches to measure protocol effectiveness, gather feedback and drive continuous improvement
• Integrating protocol considerations into broader international strategy, risk management, stakeholder engagement and organisational planning
• Mentoring and developing internal champions who can sustain high standards of diplomatic conduct and etiquette across the organisation
• Positioning protocol and international etiquette excellence as a strategic organisational asset that enhances credibility, trust and influence globally
• Assessment & Evaluation
• Upon successful completion of this programme, an Elevoris Certificate of Training will be awarded to delegates who meet the passing requirements.

courses.title: Employee Relations & Labour Law Mastery for Energy & Public Sector
courses.overview: Employee relations challenges in energy and public sector organisations are intensified by regulatory scrutiny, essential service obligations and complex industrial environments that demand proactive, fair and strategically aligned approaches to maintain operational continuity and public trust. This employee relations training develops advanced capabilities to prevent conflict, manage workforce issues and uphold fairness while protecting service delivery and organisational reputation in highly regulated contexts. Participants master diagnostic frameworks, early intervention strategies and governance approaches tailored to unionised and publicly accountable settings. The labour law HR energy public sector emphasis equips HR leaders to build resilient employee relations that balance legal compliance, operational resilience and sustainable workforce relationships. This course can be facilitated in London, Dubai, Kuala Lumpur, Nairobi, and other major business centres on client-preferred dates.

courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
Strategic Foundations of Employee Relations in Regulated and Essential Service Environments
• Examining the distinctive employee relations dynamics in energy, utilities and public sector organisations where service continuity, public accountability and regulatory oversight create heightened complexity
• Understanding how operational criticality, union presence and public scrutiny shape the nature and consequences of workplace conflict
• Identifying common sources of employee relations risk arising from organisational change, operational pressures and workforce expectations in essential services
• Recognising the leadership and governance practices required to maintain fairness, trust and operational resilience in highly regulated environments
• Establishing the strategic case for proactive employee relations that protects both organisational performance and public service obligations
• Developing a personal employee relations philosophy grounded in prevention, fairness and long-term organisational sustainability

MODULE 02
Legal and Regulatory Navigation in Highly Scrutinised Operational Contexts
• Applying structured approaches to interpret and operationalise employment requirements in energy, utilities and public sector settings without creating unnecessary rigidity
• Developing internal frameworks that ensure consistent, defensible decision-making while maintaining operational flexibility
• Managing interfaces with external regulators, oversight bodies and public accountability mechanisms with professionalism and strategic awareness
• Integrating employment considerations into operational planning, risk management and organisational governance processes
• Building organisational capability to anticipate, interpret and respond constructively to evolving regulatory and societal expectations
• Establishing review and assurance processes that maintain legal and regulatory alignment while supporting strategic agility

MODULE 03
Conflict Prevention, Early Intervention and Informal Resolution Strategies
• Developing proactive approaches to identify emerging workplace tensions before they escalate into formal disputes or industrial action
• Applying early intervention techniques, facilitated conversations and mediation principles to resolve issues at the lowest appropriate level
• Building manager and leader capability to handle difficult conversations, address performance concerns and prevent unnecessary formal processes
• Establishing clear escalation pathways and support mechanisms that balance timely resolution with appropriate governance
• Integrating conflict prevention into day-to-day operational leadership, team practices and change management
• Creating measurement and learning processes that track early intervention effectiveness and strengthen organisational capability over time

MODULE 04
Industrial Relations, Collective Bargaining and Partnership in Essential Services
• Developing constructive approaches to industrial relations that balance organisational objectives with workforce representation in unionised environments
• Applying structured preparation, negotiation and partnership-building techniques for collective bargaining and ongoing engagement
• Managing the interface between operational requirements, service continuity obligations and collective processes with strategic clarity
• Building internal capability for effective consultation, information sharing and joint problem-solving with recognised representatives
• Establishing governance and decision-making frameworks that maintain management prerogative while fostering constructive relationships
• Creating review processes that evaluate industrial relations health and adapt engagement approaches to changing organisational and workforce dynamics

MODULE 05
Grievance, Discipline, Investigation and Fair Process Management
• Designing and implementing grievance and discipline frameworks that are fair, timely and defensible in high-scrutiny environments
• Applying structured investigation principles that ensure thoroughness, impartiality and appropriate confidentiality
• Establishing clear roles, responsibilities and decision-making authority for grievance and disciplinary matters across different organisational levels
• Integrating procedural fairness with operational pragmatism to maintain workforce trust while protecting organisational interests
• Building manager and HR capability to handle complex cases with consistency, empathy and legal awareness
• Creating oversight, review and learning mechanisms that strengthen process quality and reduce recurrence of issues

MODULE 06
Managing Workforce Change, Restructuring and Transition with Minimal Disruption
• Applying employee relations considerations into planning and execution of organisational change, restructuring and workforce transitions
• Developing consultation, communication and support strategies that maintain trust and minimise operational disruption during change
• Managing the interface between change processes, collective consultation requirements and individual employee impacts with care and professionalism
• Establishing redeployment, outplacement and wellbeing support mechanisms that protect both individuals and organisational capability
• Integrating employee relations risk assessment into change governance and decision-making processes
• Creating post-change review and learning processes that strengthen future transition capability and organisational resilience

MODULE 07
Psychological Safety, Wellbeing and the Human Dimension of Employee Relations
• Establishing the critical connection between psychological safety, employee wellbeing and effective employee relations outcomes
• Developing approaches to address workplace conflict, bullying, harassment and other behaviours that undermine psychological safety
• Integrating employee relations with broader wellbeing, mental health and employee experience strategies
• Building leadership capability to recognise and respond appropriately to emerging wellbeing and relational issues
• Establishing support mechanisms, escalation pathways and recovery approaches for individuals and teams affected by workplace conflict
• Creating measurement and continuous improvement processes that track psychological safety and relational health alongside traditional ER indicators

MODULE 08
Employee Relations Governance, Risk Management and Organisational Accountability
• Designing robust employee relations governance frameworks that clarify roles, responsibilities and decision rights across the organisation
• Establishing risk identification, assessment and mitigation approaches for employee relations in high-stakes operational environments
• Integrating employee relations considerations into broader organisational risk, compliance and assurance frameworks
• Building internal capability for consistent, high-quality employee relations decision-making at all levels
• Managing external scrutiny, investigations and reputational considerations with strategic awareness and professionalism
• Creating continuous improvement and assurance mechanisms that strengthen employee relations governance maturity over time

MODULE 09
Data-Driven Employee Relations and Proactive Risk Identification
• Defining relevant employee relations metrics and indicators that provide early warning of emerging issues and track organisational health
• Applying data analysis, trend identification and diagnostic approaches to inform proactive interventions
• Integrating employee relations data with broader people analytics and operational performance information
• Establishing reporting, dashboard and escalation mechanisms that enable timely and informed decision-making
• Building organisational capability to use employee relations insights for strategic workforce planning and risk management
• Creating governance and ethical frameworks that support responsible and effective use of employee relations data

MODULE 10
Strategic Employee Relations Leadership and Future Capability Building
• Assessing current employee relations capability and identifying strategic development needs for leaders and HR teams
• Developing targeted capability-building approaches that strengthen proactive, fair and strategically aligned employee relations practice
• Leading cultural and behavioural change that embeds prevention, fairness and constructive resolution into organisational norms
• Establishing coaching, mentoring and knowledge transfer mechanisms that sustain employee relations capability across the organisation
• Anticipating future employee relations challenges arising from technological change, workforce evolution and societal expectations
• Positioning strategic employee relations leadership as a source of organisational resilience, operational continuity and sustainable workforce relationships

• Integrating employee relations risk assessment into change governance and decision-making processes
• Creating post-change review and learning processes that strengthen future transition capability and organisational resilience

Psychological Safety, Wellbeing and the Human Dimension of Employee Relations

• Building leadership capability to recognise and respond appropriately to emerging wellbeing and relational issues
• Establishing support mechanisms, escalation pathways and recovery approaches for individuals and teams affected by workplace conflict

Employee Relations Governance, Risk Management and Organisational Accountability

• Establishing risk identification, assessment and mitigation approaches for employee relations in high-stakes operational environments
• Integrating employee relations considerations into broader organisational risk, compliance and assurance frameworks
• Building internal capability for consistent, high-quality employee relations decision-making at all levels
• Managing external scrutiny, investigations and reputational considerations with strategic awareness and professionalism
• Creating continuous improvement and assurance mechanisms that strengthen employee relations governance maturity over time

MODULE 09
Data-Driven Employee Relations and Proactive Risk Identification

• Applying data analysis, trend identification and diagnostic approaches to inform proactive interventions
• Integrating employee relations data with broader people analytics and operational performance information
• Establishing reporting, dashboard and escalation mechanisms that enable timely and informed decision-making
• Building organisational capability to use employee relations insights for strategic workforce planning and risk management
• Creating governance and ethical frameworks that support responsible and effective use of employee relations data

MODULE 10
Strategic Employee Relations Leadership and Future Capability Building

• Developing targeted capability-building approaches that strengthen proactive, fair and strategically aligned employee relations practice
• Leading cultural and behavioural change that embeds prevention, fairness and constructive resolution into organisational norms
• Establishing coaching, mentoring and knowledge transfer mechanisms that sustain employee relations capability across the organisation
• Anticipating future employee relations challenges arising from technological change, workforce evolution and societal expectations
• Positioning strategic employee relations leadership as a source of organisational resilience, operational continuity and sustainable workforce relationships

courses.title: Energy Sector Strategic Leadership Programme
courses.overview: In an energy sector undergoing profound structural transformation, where energy transition pressures, geopolitical volatility and shifting stakeholder expectations demand leaders who can think and act strategically across the full value chain, many senior professionals remain constrained by functional expertise without the integrated strategic leadership capability required at the highest levels. This energy sector leadership training delivers a rigorous, multi-module programme that develops advanced competence in strategic foresight, organisational transformation, governance oversight and value-creating decision-making in complex energy environments. Participants master frameworks to lead IOCs, NOCs and energy companies through uncertainty while balancing current operational performance with credible transition strategies. The oil gas strategic leadership programme equips leaders to shape direction, influence stakeholders and deliver sustainable results in a rapidly evolving global energy landscape. This course can be facilitated in London, Dubai, Kuala Lumpur, Nairobi, and other major business centres on client-preferred dates.
whyChoose: Avoid the strategic drift and value erosion that occur when energy organisations are led by technically capable executives who lack the integrated strategic perspective needed to navigate energy transition, market volatility and stakeholder complexity simultaneously

Prevent the organisational risk of misaligned investment decisions, weak governance and fragmented responses to decarbonisation pressures that arise when leaders operate within narrow functional or asset silos

Reduce the competitive disadvantage created when energy companies fail to develop coherent strategies that optimise existing hydrocarbon portfolios while building credible positions in new energy and lower-carbon opportunities

Eliminate the leadership capability gap that leaves boards and executive teams exposed when confronting high-stakes decisions on capital allocation, portfolio rationalisation, partnership structures and regulatory positioning

Close the persistent divide between operational excellence and strategic leadership that prevents even high-performing energy organisations from translating strong asset performance into sustainable corporate value

Overcome the personal limitation of remaining a highly effective functional or asset leader without developing the broader strategic, governance and transformation skills increasingly required for appointment to General Manager, Country Manager and C-suite roles

General Manager – E&P Assets and Country Manager responsible for integrated asset performance, commercial outcomes and organisational leadership in complex operating environments
Head of Strategy and Planning Manager – Energy leading strategic planning processes, investment prioritisation and organisational transformation initiatives
Business Development Director and Commercial Strategy Manager responsible for growth strategy, partnership development and new opportunity origination across the energy value chain

Develop and articulate integrated energy sector strategies that align upstream, midstream and downstream activities with corporate purpose, market realities and credible energy transition pathways
Lead strategic investment decision-making processes that optimise capital allocation across portfolios while rigorously assessing transition risk, optionality and long-term value creation
Establish robust corporate governance, risk oversight and ESG integration frameworks that strengthen board effectiveness, stakeholder confidence and organisational resilience
Drive organisational transformation and change leadership that builds capability, culture and agility required for sustained performance in a structurally changing energy sector
Design and execute commercial and partnership strategies that create and protect value through joint ventures, strategic alliances and stakeholder influence in complex multi-party environments
Apply advanced scenario planning, strategic foresight and risk management approaches to navigate geopolitical, regulatory and market uncertainty with greater confidence and preparedness
Build high-performing strategic leadership teams and organisational decision-making processes that improve the quality, speed and alignment of critical choices
Demonstrate strategic leadership excellence through integrated application of learning and apply frameworks to strengthen both personal effectiveness and organisational strategic capability

Comprehensive participant materials, strategic frameworks, governance diagnostics, scenario planning tools and post-programme reference resources provided for sustained application
courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
The Strategic Context and Leadership Imperatives of the Transforming Energy Sector
• Analysing the interplay of energy transition, geopolitical shifts, regulatory evolution and technological disruption that define the strategic environment for energy leaders
• Identifying the specific leadership challenges created by structural demand changes, capital reallocation pressures and evolving stakeholder expectations across the energy value chain
• Understanding the distinct strategic positions and transformation journeys of national oil companies, international oil companies and emerging energy players
• Assessing the implications of net zero commitments, carbon management requirements and policy uncertainty for existing asset portfolios and future investment choices
• Recognising the leadership mindset shifts required to move from operational optimisation to strategic value creation in a fundamentally changing industry
• Establishing clear personal and organisational strategic leadership development objectives aligned with current challenges and future role aspirations

MODULE 02
Strategic Foresight, Scenario Planning and Decision-Making Under Uncertainty
• Applying structured strategic foresight methodologies to identify emerging trends, weak signals and potential disruptions relevant to energy sector strategy
• Developing advanced scenario planning capabilities that enable robust strategy development and stress testing across multiple plausible futures
• Building skills in framing strategic choices, evaluating trade-offs and making high-quality decisions when information is incomplete and outcomes are uncertain
• Managing the tension between long-term strategic intent and short-term performance pressures in capital-intensive, long-cycle energy businesses
• Establishing organisational processes that embed strategic thinking into routine decision-making rather than treating it as a periodic planning exercise
• Creating practical approaches to communicate strategic direction clearly and build organisational alignment around chosen pathways

MODULE 03
Integrated Value Chain Strategy and Portfolio Optimisation
• Mapping strategic interdependencies across upstream, midstream and downstream segments to identify value creation and value leakage opportunities at portfolio level
• Developing approaches to optimise asset portfolios through disciplined capital allocation, divestment, acquisition and partnership decisions
• Building capability to design coherent strategies that capture integration synergies while managing complexity, risk and organisational capability constraints
• Managing the strategic interface between core hydrocarbon operations and emerging lower-carbon and new energy opportunities within a single portfolio framework
• Establishing portfolio-level performance metrics and governance mechanisms that align activities with overall corporate strategic objectives
• Creating frameworks for ongoing portfolio review and strategic adjustment in response to changing market, regulatory and technological conditions

MODULE 04
Energy Transition Leadership and Sustainable Value Creation
• Developing credible and value-accretive energy transition strategies that balance optimisation of existing hydrocarbon assets with disciplined investment in lower-carbon opportunities
• Building capability to assess transition pathways, evaluate strategic options and set realistic yet ambitious decarbonisation and net zero targets aligned with organisational purpose
• Managing the organisational, cultural and capability implications of energy transition, including workforce evolution, new skill requirements and mindset shifts
• Establishing governance and performance frameworks that integrate carbon management, emissions reduction and sustainability metrics into core strategic and investment decision-making
• Leading stakeholder engagement on transition strategy with investors, regulators, partners and civil society in ways that build credibility and maintain social licence
• Creating practical approaches to measure, report and communicate progress on energy transition objectives alongside traditional financial and operational performance

MODULE 05
Corporate Governance, Board Effectiveness and Strategic Risk Oversight
• Establishing robust corporate governance frameworks that ensure clarity of roles, accountability and effective oversight between boards, executive teams and operational leadership
• Developing skills in strategic risk identification, assessment and oversight that go beyond compliance to support informed risk-taking and value protection
• Building capability to integrate ESG considerations, climate risk and sustainability into board-level strategy discussions and decision processes
• Managing the interface between governance requirements, regulatory expectations and commercial realities in increasingly scrutinised energy environments
• Establishing reporting, assurance and escalation mechanisms that provide boards with timely, decision-relevant information on strategic risks and opportunities
• Creating continuous improvement processes that strengthen governance effectiveness and organisational resilience over time

MODULE 06
Strategic Investment Decision-Making and Capital Discipline
• Applying structured investment appraisal frameworks that incorporate strategic fit, risk-adjusted returns, optionality and transition considerations alongside financial metrics
• Developing capability to evaluate and prioritise major capital investments, acquisitions, divestments and partnerships at portfolio and enterprise level
• Building skills in managing the stage-gate investment process, post-investment review and organisational learning from capital decisions
• Balancing the competing demands of short-term cash generation, long-term value creation and energy transition investment requirements
• Establishing governance and approval processes that improve the quality and consistency of strategic investment decisions across the organisation
• Creating approaches to maintain capital discipline while preserving strategic flexibility in volatile and uncertain energy markets

MODULE 07
Commercial Leadership, Partnerships and Stakeholder Influence
• Designing commercial strategies that maximise value from existing positions and create new growth opportunities through effective market positioning and deal structuring
• Developing advanced skills in structuring, negotiating and governing complex commercial arrangements, joint ventures and strategic partnerships
• Building capability to manage partner relationships, align objectives and resolve conflicts constructively in multi-party energy ventures
• Leading stakeholders influence strategies with governments, regulators, investors and communities that protect and enhance organisational interests
• Establishing internal commercial governance processes that ensure decisions are aligned with strategic priorities and risk appetite
• Creating practical frameworks for building and sustaining high-value commercial relationships that support long-term strategic objectives

MODULE 08
Operational Excellence, Asset Performance and Organisational Capability Leadership
• Developing operational strategies that deliver sustained excellence in safety, reliability, cost and environmental performance while supporting strategic objectives
• Building capability to lead asset integrity, maintenance and reliability strategies at a management level that protect long-term value creation
• Managing supply chain strategy, contractor relationships and local content requirements to support operational resilience and strategic priorities
• Establishing performance management systems, benchmarking and continuous improvement cultures that drive organisational capability development
• Integrating digital tools, data analytics and AI-driven decision support into operational leadership in ways that enhance rather than undermine governance and human judgement
• Creating frameworks for aligning operational performance with broader strategic goals including energy transition and stakeholder expectations

MODULE 09
Leading Strategic Transformation and Organisational Change
• Developing structured approaches to diagnose organisational readiness for change and design transformation programmes that deliver sustainable strategic outcomes
• Building skills in leading cultural and behavioural change required to support new strategies, governance standards and energy transition objectives
• Managing the human, structural and process dimensions of major organisational change while maintaining operational performance and stakeholder confidence
• Establishing change governance, communication and capability-building mechanisms that increase the probability of successful strategy execution
• Leading through periods of strategic ambiguity and disruption with clarity, resilience and authenticity that maintain organisational cohesion
• Creating practical approaches to measure transformation progress and adapt plans based on emerging insights and changing circumstances

MODULE 10
Personal Strategic Leadership Mastery and Executive Impact
• Consolidating learning across the programme into a coherent personal strategic leadership philosophy and practical operating model
• Developing advanced self-awareness, strategic thinking habits and leadership practices that enhance personal effectiveness at senior and executive levels
• Building capability to influence at board and C-suite level, communicate strategic direction compellingly and building followership around chosen pathways
• Establishing mechanisms for ongoing strategic learning, reflection and continuous improvement as a senior energy leader
• Creating a detailed personal action plan for immediate application and long-term development in strategic leadership roles
• Committing to ongoing mastery and active contribution to building strategic leadership capability within current and future organisations
expectedOutcomes: Participants will be able to:
Lead strategic thinking and organisational direction-setting with greater clarity, rigour and confidence across complex energy sector environments
Make high-stakes investment, portfolio and partnership decisions grounded in robust analysis, strategic fit and transition-aware judgement
Strengthen corporate governance, risk oversight and ESG integration in ways that enhance board effectiveness and stakeholder trust
Drive credible energy transition strategies that optimise current operations while building sustainable future positions
Lead organisational transformation and capability development that improves both current performance and long-term strategic resilience
Accelerate progression into General Manager, Country Manager, Vice President and C-suite roles through demonstrated strategic leadership excellence
organisationalImpact: Improved quality and coherence of enterprise strategy, capital allocation and portfolio decisions across the energy value chain
Stronger governance, risk oversight and ESG integration that reduces exposure and enhances organisational reputation and resilience
More effective navigation of energy transition challenges with strategies that balance current performance and future positioning
Enhanced organisational capability to execute strategy, manage change and sustain high performance through periods of significant disruption
Better alignment between strategic intent, operational delivery and stakeholder expectations across the organisation
Sustainable competitive advantage through more disciplined, forward-looking and integrated strategic leadership
personalImpact: Clear acceleration in career trajectory as strategic leadership capability becomes a recognised personal strength and differentiator for senior and executive appointments
Greater confidence and influence when engaging boards, executive teams and external stakeholders on complex strategic, commercial and transition matters
A distinctive professional brand as a strategic thinker and organisational leader capable of shaping direction in transforming energy environments
Practical frameworks, diagnostic tools and leadership disciplines that deliver immediate and lasting improvements in current and future roles
Enhanced ability to build and lead high-performing teams and drive organisational alignment around strategic priorities
A sustainable personal approach to strategic leadership that supports long-term effectiveness, resilience and career fulfilment
General Notes
Sector customisation available on request
Training material provided
Elevoris Certificate of Training issued to all participants
Optional post-programme advisory coaching available

In an energy sector where the difference between value creation and value erosion increasingly depends on the quality of strategic leadership, the ability to think systemically, govern effectively and lead transformation with clarity is the defining executive capability. This programme provides the depth, frameworks and personal development required to lead at that level.
Enrol now in the Energy Sector Strategic Leadership Programme to develop the strategic mastery that will distinguish you as an outstanding energy sector leader.

MODULE 02

• Building capability to set realistic yet ambitious decarbonisation targets, milestones and pathways aligned with organisational purpose, risk appetite and stakeholder expectations
• Managing the strategic trade-offs between short-term performance, long-term value creation and credible progress toward net zero commitments

• Establishing carbon accounting, internal carbon pricing and performance management systems that drive accountability and continuous improvement
• Integrating carbon management considerations into operational decision-making, maintenance strategies and supply chain management
• Creating practical frameworks for balancing emissions reduction ambition with operational realities and capital discipline

MODULE 04

• Establishing reporting, assurance and disclosure mechanisms that meet evolving investor, regulatory and stakeholder expectations for transparency
• Creating continuous improvement processes that strengthen ESG performance and organisational resilience over time

MODULE 05

• Managing reputational risk, stakeholder expectations and social licence to operate in increasingly scrutinised energy environments
• Establishing mechanisms for incorporating stakeholder feedback into transition strategy refinement and operational decision-making
• Leading constructive dialogue with host governments, regulators and partners on policy alignment, regulatory compliance and shared value creation
• Creating practical frameworks for turning stakeholder engagement into a source of strategic insight, risk mitigation and competitive advantage

MODULE 06

• Understanding the evolving landscape of sustainable finance, green bonds, sustainability-linked loans and investor expectations for energy transition performance
• Developing approaches to structure transition-related investments, access sustainable capital and demonstrate credible use of proceeds
• Building capability to develop compelling investment cases for decarbonisation and lower-carbon projects that meet both financial return and sustainability criteria
• Managing the interface between traditional project finance, corporate treasury and sustainable finance markets
• Establishing governance, reporting and assurance processes that satisfy lender and investor requirements for transition-related financing
• Creating practical frameworks for optimising the organisation’s position in sustainable finance markets while maintaining financial discipline and strategic flexibility

MODULE 07
Regulatory Navigation, Policy Advocacy and Compliance Leadership
• Developing systematic approaches to monitor, interpret and respond to evolving energy, climate and sustainability regulations across relevant jurisdictions
• Building capability to anticipate regulatory trends, assess compliance implications and integrate policy considerations into strategic and operational planning
• Managing engagement with regulators, industry bodies and policy-makers to shape constructive outcomes and maintain compliance leadership
• Establishing internal compliance frameworks, monitoring systems and reporting mechanisms that ensure ongoing adherence to transition-related obligations
• Leading organisational positioning on policy issues that affect long-term transition strategy and competitive positioning
• Creating practical approaches to turn regulatory requirements into sources of operational improvement and strategic differentiation

MODULE 08
Organisational Change, Culture and Capability Building for Transition
• Diagnosing organisational readiness for energy transition and identifying cultural, structural and capability barriers to successful implementation
• Developing structured approaches to lead the behavioural, process and capability changes required to embed sustainability into routine business practice
• Building skills in designing and delivering transition-related training, communication and leadership development programmes that create genuine organisational ownership
• Managing the human dimensions of change, including workforce evolution, new skill requirements and mindset shifts, while maintaining operational performance
• Establishing change governance, sponsorship and measurement mechanisms that increase the probability of sustainable transformation
• Creating practical frameworks for building long-term organisational capability and cultural alignment around energy transition and sustainability objectives

MODULE 09
Performance Measurement, Reporting and Continuous Improvement
• Designing meaningful key performance indicators, targets and reporting frameworks that track progress on energy transition, carbon reduction and ESG objectives
• Building capability to integrate sustainability metrics into existing performance management, board reporting and external disclosure processes
• Developing approaches to conduct credible assurance, benchmarking and external reporting that enhance stakeholder confidence and organisational learning
• Managing the balance between ambitious target-setting and realistic, evidence-based performance tracking that drives genuine improvement
• Establishing mechanisms for capturing lessons, adapting strategies and continuously improving transition performance over time
• Creating practical approaches to communicate performance transparently while maintaining credibility with increasingly sophisticated stakeholders

MODULE 10
Personal Leadership, Legacy and Sustained Impact in Energy Transition
• Consolidating learning across the programme into a coherent personal leadership approach for driving energy transition and sustainability within complex organisations
• Developing advanced self-awareness, strategic thinking and influencing skills required to lead change at senior and executive levels
• Building capability to articulate a compelling personal and organisational vision for sustainable value creation that inspires followership and sustains momentum
• Establishing mechanisms for ongoing personal development, reflection and continuous improvement as a transition leader
• Creating a detailed personal action plan for immediate application and long-term contribution to organisational and sector-wide sustainability outcomes
• Committing to ongoing mastery and active contribution to building credible, value-accretive energy transition leadership within current and future roles
• Assessment & Evaluation
• Upon successful completion of this programme, an Elevoris Certificate of Training will be awarded to delegates who meet the passing requirements.

courses.title: Enterprise Risk Management Mastery
courses.overview: In increasingly complex and interconnected environments, organisations face strategic vulnerabilities that can erode long-term value when risk is not governed coherently at the highest levels. This enterprise risk management training programme equips Chief Risk Officers, ERM Directors and Board Risk Committee members with frameworks to design integrated risk governance structures, articulate clear risk appetite and embed risk considerations into enterprise strategy and culture. Emphasis is placed on board-level oversight, strategic alignment and risk culture within this ERM masterclass course. This course can be facilitated in London, Dubai, Kuala Lumpur, Nairobi, and other major business centres on client-preferred dates.
whyChoose: Strengthening board and executive oversight through clear enterprise risk governance frameworks that define roles, responsibilities and accountability across the organisation
Enhance strategic decision quality by embedding risk considerations into planning, capital allocation and major business initiatives at the highest level
Improve organisational resilience by establishing risk appetite frameworks that translate strategic objectives into clear tolerance boundaries and guide consistent decision-making
Build a sustainable risk-aware culture that encourages proactive identification of emerging threats and collective responsibility for risk management across all functions
Strengthening stakeholder confidence through transparent risk reporting, assurance mechanisms and demonstrable alignment between risk management and corporate governance expectations
Develop internal capability to anticipate, assess and respond to complex, interconnected risks including climate, technological and geopolitical developments at enterprise level
audience: Chief Risk Officers and ERM Directors accountable for organisation-wide risk governance and strategic oversight
Heads of Risk and Senior Risk Leaders responsible for designing and implementing enterprise risk frameworks
Board Risk Committee Members and Non-Executive Directors overseeing strategic risk at the highest level
Enterprise Risk Managers and Risk Governance Leads driving framework implementation and risk appetite processes
Senior Risk Analysts and Governance Specialists supporting enterprise risk reporting and analysis
Risk Officers and Analysts contributing to enterprise risk identification, escalation and monitoring
objectives: By the end of this programme, participants will be able to:
Design integrated enterprise risk governance frameworks that clearly define roles, responsibilities, escalation protocols and board oversight mechanisms aligned with organisational strategy
Establish risk appetite frameworks that translate strategic objectives into measurable tolerance boundaries and guide consistent decision-making across the enterprise
Integrate risk management considerations into strategic planning, capital allocation and major business initiatives to enhance resilience and value protection
Lead the development of risk culture initiatives that embed proactive risk awareness, ethical behaviour and collective accountability throughout the organisation
Design enterprise-level stress testing and scenario analysis programmes that inform strategic planning and board-level risk oversight under a range of plausible conditions
Establish robust risk reporting, communication and assurance mechanisms that provide the board and executive team with clear, decision-relevant insight into enterprise risk exposure
Oversee the identification and assessment of emerging and interconnected risks, including climate, ESG, technological and geopolitical developments, at strategic level
Lead enterprise risk transformation programmes that strengthen governance, culture and capability while sustaining alignment with evolving strategic priorities and stakeholder expectations
deliveryApproach: Executive masterclass workshops combining strategic framework design, risk appetite development and board-level governance simulations with real organisational scenarios
Practical sessions focused on developing enterprise risk governance structures, risk appetite statements and strategic risk reporting templates with expert facilitation
In-depth examination of successful and challenged enterprise risk management approaches to extract transferable lessons on governance, culture and strategic integration
Collaborative development of organisation-specific risk governance frameworks and implementation roadmaps with structured peer and expert feedback
Reflective practice examining board dynamics, stakeholder influence and opportunities for enhanced strategic risk leadership
Personal and team action planning with expert support to translate learning into immediate improvements in enterprise risk governance and oversight effectiveness
courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
The Strategic Imperative of Enterprise Risk Management in Value Protection
• Examining how enterprise risk management serves as a critical enabler of sustainable organisational performance and long-term value protection in complex environments
• Understanding the distinction between enterprise-level risk governance and operational risk management activities within the three lines of defence model
• Identifying the key challenges in establishing coherent risk oversight across diverse business units, geographies and risk categories
• Aligning enterprise risk management with corporate purpose, strategic objectives and stakeholder expectations at the highest level
• Exploring the board’s role in overseeing enterprise risk and the governance mechanisms that support effective strategic oversight
• Establishing criteria for evaluating the effectiveness of enterprise risk management in contributing to organisational resilience and strategic success

MODULE 02
Designing Enterprise Risk Governance Frameworks and Board Oversight
• Establishing comprehensive enterprise risk governance structures that define roles, responsibilities, decision rights and escalation protocols across the organisation
• Designing board and executive risk oversight mechanisms that provide strategic insight without operational interference
• Integrating enterprise risk governance with corporate governance codes, regulatory expectations and stakeholder requirements
• Developing clear reporting lines, committee structures and information flows that support effective board-level risk oversight
• Addressing independence, conflict management and accountability considerations in enterprise risk governance design
• Creating processes for regular review and enhancement of governance effectiveness in response to organisational or environmental changes

MODULE 03
Developing and Implementing Risk Appetite Frameworks at Enterprise Level
• Defining the components of robust risk appetite frameworks that articulate the level and type of risk the organisation is willing to accept in pursuit of its objectives
• Establishing quantitative and qualitative risk tolerance measures that guide decision-making across strategic, financial and operational dimensions
• Aligning risk appetite with corporate strategy, capital planning and performance management processes
• Creating clear linkages between risk appetite, risk capacity and actual risk exposure to support informed strategic choices
• Developing processes for cascading risk appetite throughout the organisation while maintaining coherence and strategic alignment
• Establishing review and update mechanisms that ensure risk appetite remains relevant in changing internal and external environments

MODULE 04
Integrating Risk Management into Strategic Planning and Decision-Making
• Establishing structured processes that embed risk considerations into strategic planning, scenario development and major investment decisions
• Creating mechanisms for risk-informed capital allocation that balance opportunity, risk and strategic ambition
• Developing approaches to assess the risk implications of strategic initiatives, market expansion and significant organisational change
• Integrating stress testing and scenario analysis outcomes into strategic planning and board decision-making processes
• Building cross-functional collaboration between risk, strategy, finance and business units to support coherent enterprise decision-making
• Establishing feedback loops that enable strategy to adapt in response to emerging risk insights and changing risk profiles

MODULE 05
Building and Sustaining a Risk-Aware Organisational Culture
• Understanding the critical role of risk culture in enabling effective enterprise risk management and preventing governance failures
• Designing cultural change initiatives that strengthen risk awareness, ethical behaviour and proactive risk identification across all levels
• Establishing leadership behaviours, tone from the top and accountability mechanisms that reinforce desired risk culture norms
• Integrating risk culture considerations into recruitment, induction, training and performance management systems
• Measuring and monitoring cultural indicators through surveys, behavioural metrics and incident analysis
• Addressing cultural barriers and resistance that may undermine enterprise risk management effectiveness

MODULE 06
Enterprise-Level Risk Identification, Prioritisation and Interconnectedness
• Developing systematic approaches to identify strategic, emerging and interconnected risks across the enterprise
• Establishing processes for prioritising risks based on potential impact on strategic objectives, stakeholder value and organisational resilience
• Mapping risk interdependencies and concentrations that may amplify impact across business units, risk categories and external environments
• Integrating risk identification into strategic planning, horizon scanning and environmental analysis processes
• Creating mechanisms for regular refresh of the enterprise risk profile in response to internal developments and external changes
• Ensuring that risk identification processes remain forward-looking and capture both known and emerging threat landscapes

MODULE 07
Institutional Stress Testing, Scenario Analysis and Forward-Looking Assessment
• Designing enterprise-level stress testing and scenario analysis programmes that evaluate resilience under severe but plausible conditions
• Establishing governance processes for scenario selection, assumption setting and interpretation of results at strategic level
• Integrating stress testing outcomes into capital planning, liquidity management and strategic decision-making
• Developing reverse stress testing approaches that identify scenarios which could threaten organisational viability
• Creating clear linkages between stress testing results and risk appetite, contingency planning and board risk oversight
• Ensuring that stress testing and scenario analysis remain relevant through regular review and adaptation to changing risk environments

MODULE 08
Oversight of Emerging and Strategic Risks including Climate and ESG Factors
• Identifying and assessing emerging risks arising from technological change, geopolitical shifts, climate developments and evolving societal expectations
• Developing frameworks for integrating climate and ESG risk considerations into enterprise risk governance and strategic planning
• Establishing processes for evaluating the strategic implications of emerging risks on business model resilience and long-term value creation
• Creating governance mechanisms that ensure emerging risks receive appropriate attention at board and executive level
• Integrating horizon scanning and external intelligence into enterprise risk identification and assessment processes
• Building organisational capability to anticipate, assess and respond to novel and interconnected risk developments

MODULE 09
Enterprise Risk Reporting, Communication and Stakeholder Assurance
• Designing risk reporting frameworks that provide the board and executive team with clear, decision-relevant insight into enterprise risk exposure and management
• Establishing key risk indicators and early warning mechanisms that support proactive oversight and timely intervention
• Developing communication strategies that convey risk information effectively to different stakeholder groups while maintaining appropriate context and balance
• Creating assurance processes, including internal audit and independent review, that provide confidence in the effectiveness of enterprise risk management
• Managing the interface between management reporting, board reporting and external disclosure requirements
• Ensuring that risk reporting evolves in line with organisational complexity, stakeholder expectations and regulatory developments

MODULE 10
Leading Enterprise Risk Transformation and Sustaining Strategic Excellence
• Defining the target operating model for a strategically effective enterprise risk management function that supports organisational objectives
• Leading change initiatives that strengthen risk governance, culture and capability across the enterprise
• Establishing sponsorship, accountability and governance mechanisms that sustain long-term commitment to enterprise risk management excellence
• Developing talent, skills and succession processes that ensure the organisation has the capability to manage evolving risk landscapes
• Creating mechanisms for ongoing environmental scanning, strategic adaptation and continuous improvement in enterprise risk management
• Building a legacy of enterprise risk leadership that protects organisational value and contributes to sustainable strategic success

Design and implement enterprise risk governance frameworks that strengthen board oversight and strategic risk alignment across the organisation
Establish clear risk appetite frameworks that guide consistent, risk-informed decision-making at all levels while supporting strategic objectives
Achieving stronger integration of risk considerations into strategic planning, capital allocation and major business decisions
Building sustainable risk culture and capability that reduces reliance on reactive approaches and enhances organisational resilience
Delivery improved board-level risk reporting and assurance that enhances stakeholder confidence and governance effectiveness
Lead enterprise risk transformation that positions risk management as a strategic enabler of long-term value protection and organisational agility

sourceRecord.courseSyllabus:
MODULE 01
The Strategic Imperative of Enterprise Risk Management in Value Protection
• Examining how enterprise risk management serves as a critical enabler of sustainable organisational performance and long-term value protection in complex environments
• Understanding the distinction between enterprise-level risk governance and operational risk management activities within the three lines of defence model
• Identifying the key challenges in establishing coherent risk oversight across diverse business units, geographies and risk categories
• Aligning enterprise risk management with corporate purpose, strategic objectives and stakeholder expectations at the highest level
• Exploring the board’s role in overseeing enterprise risk and the governance mechanisms that support effective strategic oversight
• Establishing criteria for evaluating the effectiveness of enterprise risk management in contributing to organisational resilience and strategic success

MODULE 02
Designing Enterprise Risk Governance Frameworks and Board Oversight
• Establishing comprehensive enterprise risk governance structures that define roles, responsibilities, decision rights and escalation protocols across the organisation
• Designing board and executive risk oversight mechanisms that provide strategic insight without operational interference
• Integrating enterprise risk governance with corporate governance codes, regulatory expectations and stakeholder requirements
• Developing clear reporting lines, committee structures and information flows that support effective board-level risk oversight
• Addressing independence, conflict management and accountability considerations in enterprise risk governance design
• Creating processes for regular review and enhancement of governance effectiveness in response to organisational or environmental changes

MODULE 03
Developing and Implementing Risk Appetite Frameworks at Enterprise Level
• Defining the components of robust risk appetite frameworks that articulate the level and type of risk the organisation is willing to accept in pursuit of its objectives
• Establishing quantitative and qualitative risk tolerance measures that guide decision-making across strategic, financial and operational dimensions
• Aligning risk appetite with corporate strategy, capital planning and performance management processes
• Creating clear linkages between risk appetite, risk capacity and actual risk exposure to support informed strategic choices
• Developing processes for cascading risk appetite throughout the organisation while maintaining coherence and strategic alignment
• Establishing review and update mechanisms that ensure risk appetite remains relevant in changing internal and external environments

MODULE 04
Integrating Risk Management into Strategic Planning and Decision-Making
• Establishing structured processes that embed risk considerations into strategic planning, scenario development and major investment decisions
• Creating mechanisms for risk-informed capital allocation that balance opportunity, risk and strategic ambition
• Developing approaches to assess the risk implications of strategic initiatives, market expansion and significant organisational change
• Integrating stress testing and scenario analysis outcomes into strategic planning and board decision-making processes
• Building cross-functional collaboration between risk, strategy, finance and business units to support coherent enterprise decision-making
• Establishing feedback loops that enable strategy to adapt in response to emerging risk insights and changing risk profiles

MODULE 05
Building and Sustaining a Risk-Aware Organisational Culture
• Understanding the critical role of risk culture in enabling effective enterprise risk management and preventing governance failures
• Designing cultural change initiatives that strengthen risk awareness, ethical behaviour and proactive risk identification across all levels
• Establishing leadership behaviours, tone from the top and accountability mechanisms that reinforce desired risk culture norms
• Integrating risk culture considerations into recruitment, induction, training and performance management systems
• Measuring and monitoring cultural indicators through surveys, behavioural metrics and incident analysis
• Addressing cultural barriers and resistance that may undermine enterprise risk management effectiveness

MODULE 06
Enterprise-Level Risk Identification, Prioritisation and Interconnectedness
• Developing systematic approaches to identify strategic, emerging and interconnected risks across the enterprise
• Establishing processes for prioritising risks based on potential impact on strategic objectives, stakeholder value and organisational resilience
• Mapping risk interdependencies and concentrations that may amplify impact across business units, risk categories and external environments
• Integrating risk identification into strategic planning, horizon scanning and environmental analysis processes
• Creating mechanisms for regular refresh of the enterprise risk profile in response to internal developments and external changes
• Ensuring that risk identification processes remain forward-looking and capture both known and emerging threat landscapes

MODULE 07
Institutional Stress Testing, Scenario Analysis and Forward-Looking Assessment
• Designing enterprise-level stress testing and scenario analysis programmes that evaluate resilience under severe but plausible conditions
• Establishing governance processes for scenario selection, assumption setting and interpretation of results at strategic level
• Integrating stress testing outcomes into capital planning, liquidity management and strategic decision-making
• Developing reverse stress testing approaches that identify scenarios which could threaten organisational viability
• Creating clear linkages between stress testing results and risk appetite, contingency planning and board risk oversight
• Ensuring that stress testing and scenario analysis remain relevant through regular review and adaptation to changing risk environments

MODULE 08
Oversight of Emerging and Strategic Risks including Climate and ESG Factors
• Identifying and assessing emerging risks arising from technological change, geopolitical shifts, climate developments and evolving societal expectations
• Developing frameworks for integrating climate and ESG risk considerations into enterprise risk governance and strategic planning
• Establishing processes for evaluating the strategic implications of emerging risks on business model resilience and long-term value creation
• Creating governance mechanisms that ensure emerging risks receive appropriate attention at board and executive level
• Integrating horizon scanning and external intelligence into enterprise risk identification and assessment processes
• Building organisational capability to anticipate, assess and respond to novel and interconnected risk developments

MODULE 09
Enterprise Risk Reporting, Communication and Stakeholder Assurance
• Designing risk reporting frameworks that provide the board and executive team with clear, decision-relevant insight into enterprise risk exposure and management
• Establishing key risk indicators and early warning mechanisms that support proactive oversight and timely intervention
• Developing communication strategies that convey risk information effectively to different stakeholder groups while maintaining appropriate context and balance
• Creating assurance processes, including internal audit and independent review, that provide confidence in the effectiveness of enterprise risk management
• Managing the interface between management reporting, board reporting and external disclosure requirements
• Ensuring that risk reporting evolves in line with organisational complexity, stakeholder expectations and regulatory developments

MODULE 10
Leading Enterprise Risk Transformation and Sustaining Strategic Excellence
• Defining the target operating model for a strategically effective enterprise risk management function that supports organisational objectives
• Leading change initiatives that strengthen risk governance, culture and capability across the enterprise
• Establishing sponsorship, accountability and governance mechanisms that sustain long-term commitment to enterprise risk management excellence
• Developing talent, skills and succession processes that ensure the organisation has the capability to manage evolving risk landscapes
• Creating mechanisms for ongoing environmental scanning, strategic adaptation and continuous improvement in enterprise risk management
• Building a legacy of enterprise risk leadership that protects organisational value and contributes to sustainable strategic success
