sourceRecord.courseSyllabus:
MODULE 01
Foundations of Quantitative Risk Measurement and Data Analytics
• Establishing the principles of rigorous quantitative analysis that underpin reliable risk measurement and decision support in financial institutions
• Understanding the role of data quality, statistical assumptions and model limitations in producing credible risk estimates
• Defining the key categories of financial risk and the quantitative approaches commonly applied to each
• Recognising the distinction between model development for measurement, forecasting and decision support purposes
• Setting professional standards for analytical rigour, documentation and reproducibility that support model governance
• Mapping the end-to-end analytics lifecycle from data preparation through to model implementation and ongoing monitoring

MODULE 02
Advanced Statistical and Econometric Techniques for Risk Modelling
• Applying descriptive and inferential statistical methods to explore, clean and transform financial and risk-related datasets
• Conducting correlation, regression and time-series analysis to identify relationships and patterns relevant to risk measurement
• Managing data challenges including missing values, outliers, non-stationarity and structural breaks in financial time series
• Establishing robust data preparation and feature engineering processes that improve model performance and interpretability
• Applying exploratory data analysis techniques to generate hypotheses and inform model specification decisions
• Documenting data analysis processes to support reproducibility, auditability and model validation activities

MODULE 03
Market Risk Modelling: Value-at-Risk and Expected Shortfall Approaches
• Constructing parametric, historical simulation and Monte Carlo approaches to estimate Value-at-Risk for portfolios and trading books
• Calculating and interpreting expected shortfall and other tail-risk measures that complement Value-at-Risk in stressed market conditions
• Incorporating volatility clustering, fat tails and correlation dynamics into market risk models using appropriate statistical techniques
• Conducting backtesting and model performance evaluation to assess the accuracy and reliability of market risk estimates
• Addressing practical challenges in market risk modelling including liquidity risk, basis risk and model risk in complex instruments
• Integrating market risk models into daily risk management, limit setting and capital allocation processes

MODULE 04
Credit Risk Parameter Estimation: PD, LGD and EAD Modelling
• Developing statistical models to estimate probability of default using logistic regression, survival analysis and machine learning techniques
• Constructing models for loss given default that account for recovery rates, collateral and economic conditions
• Estimating exposure at default for different product types including revolving credit facilities and derivatives
• Validating credit risk models through discrimination, calibration and stability testing using appropriate statistical metrics
• Addressing data challenges in credit risk modelling including low default portfolios, cyclicality and structural changes
• Integrating credit risk parameter estimates into pricing, provisioning and capital calculation processes

MODULE 05
Operational Risk Modelling and Loss Distribution Analysis
• Applying loss distribution approaches to model operational risk frequency and severity using internal and external loss data
• Incorporating scenario analysis and expert judgement into operational risk models where historical data is limited
• Developing models for specific operational risk categories including fraud, conduct, cyber and third-party risk
• Conducting model validation and sensitivity analysis to assess the robustness of operational risk capital estimates
• Integrating operational risk models with other risk categories to support enterprise-wide capital and risk aggregation
• Establishing processes for updating operational risk models in response to new loss experience and changing risk profiles

MODULE 06
Model Validation, Testing and Performance Evaluation Frameworks
• Establishing structured model development processes that include clear objectives, data requirements, methodology selection and documentation standards
• Designing independent validation frameworks that assess conceptual soundness, data quality, statistical performance and implementation integrity
• Developing model governance policies that define roles, approval processes, change management and ongoing monitoring requirements
• Conducting model risk assessment to identify, measure and mitigate risks arising from model use and potential errors
• Establishing model inventory, tiering and reporting mechanisms that support oversight by senior management and the board
• Creating feedback loops between model performance monitoring, validation findings and model enhancement activities

MODULE 07
Stress Testing, Scenario Analysis and Sensitivity Modelling
• Designing comprehensive stress testing programmes that evaluate portfolio and institutional resilience under severe but plausible scenarios
• Developing scenario generation processes that incorporate macroeconomic, market and idiosyncratic risk factors in a coherent manner
• Conducting sensitivity analysis to understand how changes in key assumptions and inputs affect model outputs and risk estimates
• Integrating stress testing results into capital planning, liquidity management and strategic decision-making processes
• Validating stress testing models and scenarios through backtesting against historical stress events where appropriate
• Communicating stress testing outcomes clearly to support risk appetite calibration and contingency planning

MODULE 08
Machine Learning Applications in Financial Risk Analytics
• Applying machine learning techniques including decision trees, random forests and neural networks to risk classification and prediction problems
• Addressing challenges of interpretability, overfitting and regulatory acceptance when applying advanced analytical methods to risk modelling
• Integrating alternative data sources and unstructured data into risk models while maintaining robustness and governance standards
• Conducting comparative analysis between traditional statistical models and machine learning approaches to inform methodology selection
• Establishing governance and validation processes specific to machine learning models that address bias, drift and explainability requirements
• Building organisational capability to deploy, monitor and maintain advanced analytical models in production risk environments

MODULE 09
Model Risk Management, Governance and Regulatory Compliance
• Identifying sources of model risk arising from data, methodology, implementation and usage across the model lifecycle
• Developing frameworks to measure, monitor and mitigate model risk in a manner proportionate to model materiality and complexity
• Establishing model risk appetite and tolerance levels that guide model approval, usage restrictions and remediation priorities
• Integrating model risk management into broader enterprise risk governance and regulatory compliance processes
• Conducting regular model risk reporting to senior management and the board on model inventory, performance and remediation status
• Creating processes for managing model changes, version control and decommissioning in a controlled and auditable manner

MODULE 10
Implementing Analytics-Driven Risk Reporting and Decision Support
• Designing risk analytics platforms and dashboards that translate complex model outputs into clear, actionable insight for decision-makers
• Establishing automated reporting processes that deliver timely risk information while maintaining appropriate controls and audit trails
• Integrating risk analytics into business processes including pricing, limit setting, capital allocation and performance measurement
• Developing training and changing management initiatives that build user understanding and appropriate reliance on model outputs
• Creating feedback mechanisms that capture user experience and decision outcomes to inform model refinement
• Building sustainable analytical capability that supports continuous improvement in risk measurement and decision support

Foundations of Fintech Strategy and Digital Transformation Leadership
• Examining the evolution of banking from product-centric models to ecosystem-enabled, technology-driven and customer-centric organisations
• Defining the scope of fintech strategy and digital transformation including technology adoption, ecosystem development, organisational change and value creation
• Identifying the key interfaces between fintech strategy, corporate strategy, risk appetite, regulatory expectations and competitive positioning
• Establishing principles of effective digital leadership including clarity of vision, disciplined innovation governance and alignment of technology investments with institutional objectives
• Recognising the impact of open banking, embedded finance, generative AI and shifting customer behaviours on strategic priorities and transformation requirements

MODULE 02

• Establishing governance processes for prioritising digital initiatives and allocating resources across competing transformation opportunities
• Communicating strategic analysis and recommended digital directions clearly to boards and executive teams

MODULE 03

• Managing the strategic, operational and regulatory implications of sharing data and capabilities through open APIs
• Evaluating the risks, opportunities and governance requirements of participating in or building digital ecosystems
• Aligning ecosystem strategies with institutional risk appetite, regulatory expectations and long-term competitive objectives

MODULE 04
Integrating Generative AI, Analytics and Automation into Core Operations

• Designing governance frameworks for evaluating, piloting and scaling AI and automation solutions with appropriate risk oversight and ethical considerations
• Integrating AI-driven decisioning, process automation and predictive analytics into credit, fraud, operations and customer service functions
• Establishing data, model risk and change management requirements that support responsible and effective technology adoption
• Measuring and realising the benefits of AI and automation investments through clear business cases and performance metrics
• Building organisational capability to govern, maintain and continuously improve AI-enabled processes and decision systems

MODULE 05
Innovation Portfolio Management and Fintech Partnership Governance
• Designing innovation portfolio management frameworks that balance incremental improvement, adjacent innovation and transformative bets
• Establishing governance processes for evaluating, selecting and managing fintech partnerships, investments and acquisitions
• Managing the strategic, operational and cultural implications of integrating external technologies, platforms and talent into the organisation
• Aligning innovation activities with institutional strategy, risk appetite and regulatory requirements through clear prioritisation and oversight mechanisms
• Developing performance measurement and stage-gate processes that enable disciplined scaling or termination of innovation initiatives
• Building organisational capability to source, evaluate and integrate external innovation while protecting core capabilities and franchise value

MODULE 06
Regulatory Alignment, Risk Integration and Governance of Digital Initiatives
• Integrating regulatory expectations including open banking, data protection, AI governance and conduct requirements into fintech strategy and digital transformation programmes
• Designing governance frameworks that ensure digital initiatives maintain appropriate risk oversight, model validation and compliance controls
• Establishing board-level reporting and assurance mechanisms for digital transformation progress, risks and outcomes
• Managing the interface between digital strategy, risk, compliance, legal and technology functions to ensure coordinated execution
• Anticipating and responding to evolving regulatory expectations for fintech, embedded finance and AI in banking
• Building organisational capability to innovate responsibly while maintaining supervisory confidence and regulatory alignment

MODULE 07
Leading Organisational Change, Culture and Agile Transformation
• Designing and leading large-scale organisational change programmes that embed digital mindsets, agile ways of working and customer-centric cultures
• Establishing change leadership frameworks, communication strategies and capability development programmes that accelerate adoption of new technologies and processes
• Managing the human, structural and cultural dimensions of digital transformation to reduce resistance and build sustainable new behaviours
• Integrating agile methodologies, design thinking and cross-functional collaboration into operational and strategic decision-making processes
• Measuring and monitoring cultural and behavioural indicators that support digital transformation and innovation outcomes
• Building leadership capability to model digital behaviours and sustain momentum through the multi-year journey of transformation

MODULE 08
Performance Measurement, Value Realisation and Continuous Improvement
• Defining key performance indicators and value metrics that link digital initiatives to strategic objectives, financial outcomes and customer impact
• Designing governance processes for tracking, reporting and realising benefits from fintech strategy and digital transformation investments
• Establishing feedback loops, stage-gate reviews and continuous improvement mechanisms that enable adaptive strategy execution
• Integrating digital performance into broader organisational performance management, capital allocation and incentive frameworks
• Benchmarking digital transformation progress and outcomes against relevant peers and industry standards to identify enhancement opportunities
• Building organisational capability to use data, analytics and insights to drive ongoing optimisation of digital strategies and initiatives

MODULE 09
Risk, Resilience and Cybersecurity in Digital Transformation
• Integrating cybersecurity, operational resilience and technology risk considerations into fintech strategy and digital transformation governance
• Designing risk frameworks that address new and amplified risks arising from open APIs, cloud adoption, AI systems and ecosystem partnerships
• Establishing governance processes for managing third-party technology risks, data sharing risks and concentration risks in digital ecosystems
• Aligning digital transformation initiatives with operational resilience requirements and regulatory expectations for critical functions
• Building organisational awareness and capability to maintain security, privacy and resilience as digital footprints expand
• Developing incident response and recovery capabilities that protect institutional reputation and customer trust during digital disruptions

MODULE 10
Executive Leadership, Legacy and Future-Proofing Digital Capability
• Defining the evolving role of digital and fintech leadership in shaping institutional competitiveness, resilience and stakeholder value
• Developing personal leadership practices, executive presence and influence skills required to lead digital transformation at board and C-suite level
• Building high-performing digital, innovation and transformation teams through talent strategy, capability development and succession planning
• Anticipating future trends in technology, regulation, customer behaviour and competitive dynamics to future-proof digital strategies and capabilities
• Creating organisational legacy through governance discipline, knowledge transfer and cultural change that sustains digital excellence beyond individual tenures
• Positioning fintech strategy and digital transformation as strategic assets that protect value, enable innovation and drive long-term institutional success

courses.title: Forensic Accounting & Fraud Investigation
courses.overview: When fraud or financial misconduct occurs, organisations require skilled professionals who can conduct thorough, defensible investigations that establish facts, preserve evidence integrity and support appropriate legal, disciplinary or regulatory outcomes. This forensic accounting training programme equips Forensic Accountants and Fraud Investigators with structured methodologies for evidence identification, digital forensics, witness interviewing and expert reporting that withstands scrutiny. Emphasis is placed on maintaining chain of custody, ensuring procedural rigour and delivering clear, objective findings that inform decision-making in complex post-event scenarios. This fraud investigation course can be facilitated in London, Dubai, Kuala Lumpur, Nairobi, and other major business centres on client-preferred dates.
whyChoose: Strengthen investigative capability by applying structured forensic methodologies that ensure evidence is identified, collected and preserved in a manner that maintains integrity and supports subsequent proceedings
Improve the quality and defensibility of investigation outcomes through rigorous documentation, chain of custody protocols and clear expert reporting that withstands internal and external challenge
Enhance organisational capacity to respond effectively to fraud incidents by building internal expertise in evidence handling, digital forensics and witness interviewing
Reduce the risk of compromised investigations through consistent application of professional standards for evidence management, interview technique and report preparation
Build stakeholder confidence in investigation findings by producing objective, well-supported conclusions that inform disciplinary, legal or recovery actions
Develop sustainable internal forensic capability that reduces reliance on external investigators and positions the organisation to manage complex cases with greater control and consistency
audience: Forensic Accountants and Fraud Investigators responsible for conducting detailed investigations into financial misconduct and fraud incidents
Internal Auditors and Risk Officers who support or lead fraud investigations and require deeper forensic skills
Compliance Officers and Financial Crime Specialists involved in post-incident investigations and evidence gathering
Legal and Governance Professionals who oversee or rely on forensic findings for disciplinary, regulatory or litigation purposes
Finance and Controls Managers who may be required to support or participate in internal fraud investigations
Senior Managers and Heads of Function accountable for incident response, investigation oversight and organisational learning from fraud events
objectives: By the end of this programme, participants will be able to:
Plan and scope forensic investigations in a structured manner that defines objectives, resource requirements and procedural safeguards from the outset
Identify, collect and preserve physical, documentary and electronic evidence while maintaining chain of custody and ensuring admissibility for subsequent proceedings
Conduct structured interviews and information-gathering activities that elicit reliable information while respecting legal and ethical boundaries
Apply digital forensics techniques to identify, recover and analyse electronic evidence in a forensically sound manner that preserves integrity
Perform detailed financial analysis and transaction tracing to establish the nature, extent and impact of fraudulent activity
Prepare clear, defensible expert reports that communicate complex financial findings, methodology and conclusions to non-specialist audiences
Manage the legal, ethical and professional considerations that arise during investigations, including confidentiality, conflicts of interest and disclosure obligations
Present findings effectively in formal settings and support post-investigation actions including disciplinary processes, recovery efforts and organisational learning
deliveryApproach: Intensive practitioner workshops combining evidence handling exercises, digital forensics simulations and structured interview role-plays with realistic case materials
Hands-on sessions focused on planning investigations, preserving evidence and preparing expert reports with expert facilitation and peer review
Detailed examination of real investigation cases to extract practical lessons on evidence management, interviewing challenges and reporting standards
Collaborative group exercises addressing complex, multi-issue investigations that require integrated evidence gathering, analysis and reporting
Expert-led discussions on emerging challenges in digital evidence, cross-border considerations and evolving investigative practice
Personal and team action planning with structured support to translate learning into immediate improvements in participants’ investigative practice
courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
Foundations of Forensic Investigation Methodology and Professional Standards
• Defining the scope, objectives and distinguishing characteristics of forensic accounting and fraud investigation compared to routine audit or compliance work
• Establishing the core principles of objectivity, independence and professional scepticism that underpin all forensic work
• Understanding the legal and procedural context in which forensic findings may be used, including disciplinary, civil and criminal proceedings
• Mapping the typical phases of a forensic investigation from initial referral through to reporting and post-investigation support
• Recognising the ethical obligations and professional boundaries that govern forensic practitioners throughout an engagement
• Setting expectations for rigour, documentation and defensibility that distinguish forensic work from other forms of financial review

MODULE 02
Planning, Scoping and Managing Forensic Investigations
• Developing structured investigation plans that define objectives, scope, hypotheses, resource needs and key milestones
• Assessing initial allegations or referrals to determine investigation necessity, scope and prioritisation
• Identifying potential evidence sources, data requirements and access constraints at the planning stage
• Establishing investigation governance, including roles, responsibilities, reporting lines and escalation protocols
• Managing investigation budgets, timelines and stakeholder expectations while maintaining investigative integrity
• Building flexibility into plans to accommodate new information or changing circumstances without compromising procedural standards

MODULE 03
Evidence Identification, Collection and Preservation
• Systematically identifying potential evidence sources across physical documents, electronic records, communications and witness testimony
• Applying appropriate collection methods that preserve evidence integrity and minimise the risk of contamination or alteration
• Establishing and maintaining chain of custody documentation that records the handling, storage and transfer of all evidence items
• Implementing secure evidence storage and access controls that protect integrity throughout the investigation lifecycle
• Documenting collection processes in sufficient detail to support subsequent review, challenge or legal scrutiny
• Managing large volumes of evidence through structured indexing, logging and retrieval systems

MODULE 04
Digital Forensics and Electronic Evidence Handling
• Understanding the principles of digital forensics that ensure electronic evidence is identified, preserved and analysed in a forensically sound manner
• Applying techniques to recover, extract and analyse data from computers, mobile devices, networks and cloud environments
• Preserving metadata, logs and audit trails that may be critical to establishing timelines, access and intent
• Addressing challenges associated with encryption, deleted data, remote storage and rapidly evolving technology platforms
• Documenting digital forensic processes and findings in a manner that demonstrates methodological rigour and supports admissibility
• Integrating digital evidence with traditional documentary and witness evidence to build a complete investigative picture

MODULE 05
Conducting Effective Interviews and Information Gathering
• Planning and preparing for interviews with subjects, witnesses and other parties in a structured and professional manner
• Applying interview techniques that elicit accurate, reliable information while minimising the risk of leading or coercive questioning
• Managing difficult interviews, including those involving reluctant, hostile or potentially deceptive individuals
• Documenting interviews through contemporaneous notes, statements or recordings in accordance with procedural requirements
• Assessing the credibility and reliability of information obtained during interviews and corroborating with other evidence
• Maintaining appropriate professional boundaries and ethical standards throughout all information-gathering activities

MODULE 06
Financial Analysis, Transaction Tracing and Quantification
• Applying forensic accounting techniques to analyse financial records, identify anomalies and trace the flow of funds or assets
• Reconstructing transactions and accounting entries to establish the nature, timing and impact of fraudulent activity
• Quantifying financial losses, misappropriations or other impacts arising from the subject matter under investigation
• Identifying patterns, relationships and irregularities that may indicate collusion, concealment or other sophisticated schemes
• Using data analytics tools to support large-scale transaction analysis while maintaining evidential standards
• Documenting analytical work in a clear, reproducible manner that supports findings and withstands challenge

MODULE 07
Maintaining Chain of Custody and Ensuring Evidence Integrity
• Establishing comprehensive chain of custody procedures that track every movement and handling of evidence items
• Implementing physical and digital security measures that protect evidence from loss, damage, alteration or unauthorised access
• Conducting regular evidence audits and reconciliations to verify that all items remain accounted for and intact
• Managing the transfer of evidence to external parties, including legal counsel, regulators or law enforcement, with appropriate documentation
• Addressing potential challenges to evidence integrity proactively through robust procedures and contemporaneous records
• Ensuring that all evidence handling complies with organisational policies and applicable legal requirements

MODULE 08
Preparing Expert Reports and Communicating Investigation Findings
• Structuring expert reports that clearly present objectives, methodology, evidence, analysis, findings and conclusions
• Writing in a clear, objective and professional style that is accessible to non-specialist readers while maintaining technical accuracy
• Supporting findings with appropriate evidence references, appendices and working papers that enable verification
• Distinguishing between facts, opinions and inferences in a manner that maintains credibility and avoids overstatement
• Tailoring report content and presentation to the needs of different audiences, including management, legal advisors and external parties
• Managing the review, revision and finalisation of reports to ensure quality and consistency before release

MODULE 09
Legal, Ethical and Professional Considerations in Forensic Work
• Understanding the legal context in which forensic investigations operate, including issues of privilege, disclosure and confidentiality
• Managing conflicts of interest, independence threats and other ethical considerations that may arise during investigations
• Ensuring that investigative activities respect individual rights, data protection requirements and procedural fairness
• Determining the appropriate point at which to involve legal counsel, regulators or law enforcement agencies
• Maintaining professional boundaries between investigative, advisory and decision-making roles
• Documenting ethical and legal considerations and decisions made throughout the investigation

MODULE 10
Testimony, Hearings and Post-Investigation Actions
• Preparing to give evidence in formal settings, including understanding the role of expert witnesses and the nature of examination
• Anticipating lines of questioning and preparing clear, consistent responses that are grounded in the evidence and methodology
• Supporting post-investigation processes, including disciplinary proceedings, recovery actions and regulatory notifications
• Contributing to organisational learning by identifying control weaknesses, systemic issues and lessons from the investigation
• Managing the secure closure and archiving of investigation files in accordance with retention and confidentiality requirements
• Reflecting on investigation outcomes to improve personal practice and contribute to the development of organisational capability
expectedOutcomes: Participants will be able to:
Conduct thorough, well-documented forensic investigations that produce reliable findings supported by properly preserved and managed evidence
Deliver clear, defensible expert reports and testimony that communicate complex findings effectively to decision-makers and external parties
Maintain the highest standards of procedural integrity, chain of custody and ethical conduct throughout all investigative activities
Support successful disciplinary, legal or regulatory outcomes through high-quality evidence gathering, analysis and reporting
Contribute to organisational learning and control improvement by identifying root causes and systemic vulnerabilities exposed during investigations
Build sustainable internal forensic capability that enables the organisation to respond effectively to future incidents with greater independence and rigour
organisationalImpact: Improved quality and defensibility of investigation outcomes that support appropriate and timely organisational responses to fraud and misconduct
Enhanced protection of the organisation’s legal position and recovery prospects through robust evidence management and expert reporting
Stronger governance and accountability arising from clear, objective findings that inform disciplinary and remedial actions
Reduced risk of compromised investigations or challenges to findings through consistent application of forensic standards
Sustainable improvement in the organisation’s ability to investigate complex matters internally with appropriate rigour and independence
Clear contribution to organisational learning, control enhancement and prevention of recurrence through high-quality post-incident analysis
personalImpact: Advanced practical expertise in forensic investigation methodology, evidence handling and expert reporting directly applicable to specialist forensic and investigation roles
Greater confidence in planning, executing and reporting on complex investigations under scrutiny from management, legal advisors or external parties
Enhanced skills in interviewing, digital forensics, financial analysis and professional communication that improve investigative effectiveness
Clearer professional pathway towards senior forensic accounting, fraud investigation and expert witness roles
Stronger ability to maintain professional standards and ethical boundaries in challenging investigative contexts
Expanded professional perspective and peer network supporting ongoing development in forensic accounting and fraud investigation practice
General Notes
Sector customisation available on request
Training material provided
Elevoris Certificate of Training issued to all participants
Optional post-programme advisory coaching available

When fraud or misconduct occurs, the quality of the subsequent investigation directly determines whether an organisation can establish facts, protect its interests and learn from the incident. By mastering structured forensic methodology, evidence integrity and clear expert communication, practitioners transform complex, contested situations into reliable findings that support sound decisions and organisational improvement.

Enrol now in the Forensic Accounting & Fraud Investigation programme to develop the investigative rigour, evidence management expertise and reporting capability required to conduct defensible, high-quality forensic work that serves justice and organisational learning.

courses.title: Government Relations & Stakeholder Engagement Masterclass
courses.overview: In an era of increasing regulatory complexity and heightened stakeholder expectations, organisations face significant challenges in navigating government relationships strategically while managing diverse interests and policy risks. This government relations training provides professionals with practical frameworks for mapping stakeholder ecosystems, developing integrated engagement strategies and building credible relationships with public sector actors. Participants develop hands-on capability to anticipate regulatory developments, influence policy outcomes ethically and align organisational objectives with government priorities. The stakeholder engagement masterclass emphasises real-world application through intensive simulations, planning exercises and scenario-based learning. This course can be facilitated in London, Dubai, Kuala Lumpur, Nairobi, and other major business centres on client-preferred dates.
whyChoose: Develop comprehensive government relations strategies that enable proactive engagement with policymakers and reduce exposure to regulatory and reputational risks
Build practical skills in stakeholder mapping, analysis and prioritisation that identify influence opportunities and guide efficient resource allocation
Strengthen capability to design and execute ethical advocacy approaches that contribute constructively to policy development while advancing organisational interests
Gain competence in managing complex, multi-stakeholder environments including regulated sectors such as energy, infrastructure and public services
Establish robust systems for monitoring policy change, managing government relations crises and protecting organisational reputation during high-pressure situations
Create measurable public affairs performance frameworks that demonstrate clear value and support continuous improvement in stakeholder engagement practice

Stakeholder Engagement Managers responsible for coordinating cross-functional stakeholder initiatives and managing priority government relationships
Public Affairs Managers tasked with aligning government engagement messaging with broader organisational communications and reputation management
Government Relations Analysts conducting political monitoring, research and preparation of briefing materials to support senior-level stakeholder interactions

Conduct systematic stakeholder mapping and political landscape analysis to identify influence pathways, risks and engagement opportunities in government and public sector contexts
Develop and execute ethical advocacy and influence approaches that contribute constructively to policy development while protecting organisational interests and reputation
Build credible, trust-based relationships with government officials and public sector stakeholders through professional communication, protocol adherence and consistent engagement
Establish robust systems for monitoring regulatory change, managing policy risk and ensuring organisational compliance and resilience in dynamic government environments
Prepare for and manage government relations crises with effective communication protocols that maintain stakeholder confidence and protect organisational reputation
Measure and demonstrate the impact of government relations and stakeholder engagement activities through clear performance frameworks and evaluation methodologies
Build sustainable organisational capability in government relations through leadership engagement, training systems and continuous improvement processes

Structured role-play and simulation exercises covering high-stakes government meetings, difficult stakeholder conversations and crisis response situations with immediate expert feedback

courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
Foundations of Government Relations and Stakeholder Strategy
• Understanding the strategic role of government relations in achieving organisational objectives within complex policy and regulatory environments
• Examining the principles of effective stakeholder engagement and the value of building long-term, trust-based relationships with public sector actors
• Identifying the key components of a successful government relations strategy including research, planning, execution and performance evaluation
• Recognising the ethical foundations, transparency requirements and governance considerations that underpin credible government relations practice
• Mapping the interface between government relations, corporate strategy, risk management and broader stakeholder communications functions
• Establishing the organisational case for investing in structured government relations capability as a strategic asset for resilience and opportunity creation

MODULE 02
Stakeholder Mapping, Analysis and Prioritisation
• Conducting comprehensive stakeholder identification and mapping exercises to identify key government actors, decision-makers, influencers and potential allies or opponents
• Applying practical analytical frameworks to assess stakeholder influence, interest, alignment and engagement potential across complex policy environments
• Developing prioritisation methodologies that guide efficient allocation of engagement resources and focus on high-impact relationships
• Utilising research methods, intelligence gathering and horizon scanning to build accurate, dynamic pictures of stakeholder landscapes
• Creating stakeholder engagement plans that adapt to changing political contexts, organisational priorities and emerging policy issues
• Establishing internal processes for maintaining stakeholder maps, tracking interactions and ensuring institutional memory in government relations functions

MODULE 03
Developing Integrated Government Engagement Strategies
• Designing multi-channel government engagement strategies that align with broader organisational goals and public policy priorities
• Integrating government relations objectives into corporate planning, risk management and communications functions for greater organisational coherence

courses.title: Hospital Operations, Administration & Management Programme
courses.overview: Hospital leaders and operations managers face mounting pressures from rising patient demand, constrained resources and heightened expectations for efficient, safe and responsive service delivery across increasingly complex organisational environments. This hospital management training equips participants with integrated frameworks for optimising patient flow, resource allocation, facilities management and administrative processes that enhance operational performance and organisational resilience. Participants develop the capability to implement data-informed decision-making, smart hospital practices and continuous improvement approaches that align operations with value-based principles and long-term strategic objectives. This course can be facilitated in London, Dubai, Riyadh, Nairobi, and other major business centres on client-preferred dates.
whyChoose: Design and implement comprehensive hospital operations frameworks that optimise patient flow, bed utilisation and capacity management while reducing delays and improving service responsiveness
Establish robust resource allocation, scheduling and workforce deployment systems that maximise efficiency, minimise waste and maintain service quality under fluctuating demand
Integrate smart hospital infrastructure, digital tools and data analytics into daily operations to enhance real-time visibility, decision support and performance monitoring
Strengthen operational risk management, resilience planning and business continuity arrangements that protect service delivery during disruptions and emergencies
Embed performance measurement, benchmarking and continuous improvement disciplines that drive measurable gains in efficiency, quality and patient experience across hospital services
Align hospital operations with value-based healthcare principles, ESG sustainability goals and governance accountability frameworks to demonstrate organisational value and regulatory compliance
audience: Hospital Chief Executive Officers and Directors of Operations accountable for overall hospital performance, service delivery and operational strategy
Heads of Hospital Operations and Service Delivery Directors responsible for planning, coordinating and optimising hospital-wide operational functions
Operations Managers and Departmental Managers tasked with managing patient flow, resource allocation and day-to-day service delivery within specific areas
Performance and Improvement Managers overseeing operational metrics, process optimisation and efficiency initiatives across hospital departments
Operations Analysts and Capacity Planning Specialists conducting data analysis, modelling and scenario planning to support operational decisions
Operations Coordinators and Administrators supporting scheduling, logistics coordination, documentation and performance reporting under senior direction
objectives: By the end of this programme, participants will be able to:

Design and implement integrated hospital operations frameworks that optimise patient flow, bed management and capacity utilisation across emergency, elective and outpatient services while maintaining safety and quality standards
Establish robust resource allocation, scheduling and logistics systems that maximise operational efficiency, minimise waste and ensure timely service delivery under variable demand conditions
Integrate smart hospital technologies, digital platforms and real-time data analytics into operational processes to enhance visibility, decision-making and performance monitoring
Develop operational risk, resilience and business continuity plans that protect critical hospital functions during disruptions, emergencies and surge events
Create comprehensive performance measurement systems with relevant KPIs, benchmarking processes and reporting mechanisms that drive accountability and continuous improvement

deliveryApproach: Structured multi-module learning journey that integrates strategic frameworks, operational case studies and organisational application across the full spectrum of hospital management disciplines
In-depth analysis of real-world hospital operations challenges through detailed case studies highlighting successful patient flow redesign, resource optimisation and smart hospital implementations
Collaborative workshops and simulation exercises requiring participants to develop capacity plans, operational dashboards and resilience strategies under realistic hospital constraints
Personal operational improvement projects applying course concepts directly to participants’ current hospital environments with implementation planning, progress review and expert facilitation

courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
Foundations of Hospital Operations and Administration
• Examining the distinctive characteristics of hospital operations management including multi-service complexity, 24/7 demands and interdependencies between clinical and support functions
• Defining core principles of effective hospital administration including process discipline, resource stewardship, patient-centred design and performance accountability
• Identifying common operational challenges in hospitals such as bottlenecks, variation in flow and misalignment between capacity and demand
• Establishing the foundational elements of robust hospital operations systems including governance structures, standard processes and data-informed decision-making
• Recognising the influence of organisational culture, leadership behaviour and external regulatory environments on operational effectiveness
• Mapping the relationship between hospital operations, strategic objectives, financial performance and stakeholder expectations in healthcare organisations

MODULE 02
Strategic Capacity Planning and Patient Flow Management
• Developing comprehensive capacity planning frameworks that align bed, theatre, outpatient and diagnostic resources with projected demand patterns
• Designing patient flow management systems that reduce delays, minimise length of stay and improve throughput across the hospital journey
• Establishing processes for demand forecasting, surge planning and dynamic resource reallocation in response to changing conditions
• Managing the interface between emergency, elective and outpatient pathways to optimise overall hospital capacity utilisation
• Integrating capacity planning with performance metrics, financial implications and quality outcomes
• Building organisational capability to maintain efficient patient flow while preserving safety, dignity and care quality

MODULE 03
Resource Allocation, Scheduling and Operational Efficiency
• Designing resource allocation frameworks that optimise staffing, equipment and support services across hospital departments and shifts
• Establishing scheduling systems and rostering practices that balance operational needs, staff wellbeing and service continuity
• Applying lean and process improvement principles to identify and eliminate waste, duplication and inefficiency in hospital operations
• Managing the trade-offs between cost efficiency, service quality and staff workload in resource-constrained environments
• Integrating resource management with performance monitoring and continuous improvement cycles
• Building organisational capability to achieve sustainable operational efficiency without compromising patient care or staff experience

MODULE 04
Facilities, Infrastructure and Smart Hospital Operations
• Examining the role of facilities management and physical infrastructure in supporting efficient, safe and patient-centred hospital operations
• Designing approaches to integrate smart hospital technologies, automation and digital infrastructure into operational workflows
• Establishing processes for maintenance planning, space utilisation optimisation and infrastructure resilience
• Managing the implications of digital transformation and smart systems on operational processes, staff capability and patient experience
• Integrating facilities and infrastructure considerations into broader operational planning, risk management and sustainability strategies
• Building organisational capability to leverage smart hospital capabilities for enhanced operational performance and future readiness

MODULE 05
Support Services, Logistics and Ancillary Operations
• Developing frameworks for managing support services including logistics, supply chain interfaces, catering, cleaning and other ancillary functions that enable clinical delivery
• Establishing operational standards, performance metrics and coordination mechanisms for support services aligned with hospital priorities
• Designing logistics and inventory management systems that ensure timely availability of resources while minimising waste and cost
• Managing the interface between support services and clinical operations to optimise overall hospital efficiency and patient experience
• Integrating support services management with quality, safety and regulatory compliance requirements
• Building organisational capability to deliver reliable, efficient and responsive support operations that underpin hospital performance

MODULE 06
Performance Measurement, KPIs and Operational Intelligence
• Developing comprehensive performance measurement frameworks with relevant operational KPIs that reflect efficiency, quality, safety and patient experience dimensions
• Establishing data collection, analysis and reporting processes that provide timely, accurate and actionable intelligence for operational decision-makers
• Designing operational dashboards, benchmarking processes and exception reporting mechanisms that highlight areas requiring attention or improvement
• Managing the use of operational data to identify trends, diagnose issues and evaluate the impact of improvement initiatives
• Integrating performance measurements with governance reporting, accountability mechanisms and strategic planning cycles
• Building organisational capability to become more data-driven and evidence-based in hospital operations management

MODULE 07
Operational Risk, Resilience and Business Continuity
• Identifying and assessing key operational risks in hospital environments including supply disruptions, infrastructure failures, surge events and process vulnerabilities
• Developing risk mitigation strategies, contingency plans and business continuity arrangements that protect critical hospital functions
• Establishing escalation protocols, crisis management structures and recovery processes for operational disruptions
• Managing the implications of operational risk events on patient safety, service continuity and organisational reputation
• Integrating operational risk management with broader organisational risk, governance and compliance frameworks
• Building organisational capability to maintain resilience and rapid recovery in the face of operational challenges and emergencies

MODULE 08
Digital Enablement and Data-Driven Hospital Operations
• Exploring opportunities to leverage digital tools, automation and data analytics to enhance hospital operational efficiency and decision support
• Designing approaches for integrating operational systems, electronic platforms and real-time data into daily management and coordination processes
• Establishing data governance, quality and security requirements that support credible operational intelligence and digital transformation
• Managing the organisational, cultural and capability implications of digital adoption in hospital operations environments
• Integrating digital enablement with performance improvement, patient flow and resource management strategies
• Building organisational capability to harness digital technologies for smarter, more responsive and efficient hospital operations

MODULE 09
Change Leadership and Continuous Improvement in Operations
• Leading change initiatives that embed operational excellence, process discipline and continuous improvement into hospital culture and practice
• Designing improvement programmes that engage staff at all levels in identifying opportunities and implementing sustainable changes
• Establishing governance, project management and benefit realisation approaches for operational transformation initiatives
• Managing resistance, cultural barriers and behavioural change requirements associated with operational improvements
• Integrating continuous improvement with performance management, recognition systems and leadership development
• Building organisational capability to sustain operational excellence and adapt processes in response to changing demands and evidence

MODULE 10
Governance, Accountability and Strategic Alignment of Hospital Operations
• Designing governance structures, committees and reporting lines that provide effective oversight of hospital operations and performance
• Establishing accountability frameworks that clarify roles, responsibilities and escalation pathways for operational issues and risks
• Aligning hospital operations with organisational strategy, value-based healthcare principles and ESG sustainability goals
• Managing the interface between operational governance, clinical governance, financial management and external regulatory requirements
• Integrating operational performance into board and executive decision-making with clear metrics and narrative reporting
• Building organisational capability to treat hospital operations as a strategic function that delivers measurable value and supports long-term organisational success

This programme provides participants with the frameworks, practical tools and leadership capability to transform hospital operations into a source of competitive advantage, regulatory confidence and lasting value for patients, staff and communities.

Enrol now in the Hospital Operations, Administration & Management Programme to develop the operational expertise, strategic insight and execution discipline required to lead high-performing hospitals that deliver measurable improvements in efficiency, resilience and patient-centred outcomes.

MODULE 01
Foundations of Hospital Operations and Administration
• Examining the distinctive characteristics of hospital operations management including multi-service complexity, 24/7 demands and interdependencies between clinical and support functions
• Defining core principles of effective hospital administration including process discipline, resource stewardship, patient-centred design and performance accountability
• Identifying common operational challenges in hospitals such as bottlenecks, variation in flow and misalignment between capacity and demand
• Establishing the foundational elements of robust hospital operations systems including governance structures, standard processes and data-informed decision-making
• Recognising the influence of organisational culture, leadership behaviour and external regulatory environments on operational effectiveness
• Mapping the relationship between hospital operations, strategic objectives, financial performance and stakeholder expectations in healthcare organisations

MODULE 02
Strategic Capacity Planning and Patient Flow Management
• Developing comprehensive capacity planning frameworks that align bed, theatre, outpatient and diagnostic resources with projected demand patterns
• Designing patient flow management systems that reduce delays, minimise length of stay and improve throughput across the hospital journey
• Establishing processes for demand forecasting, surge planning and dynamic resource reallocation in response to changing conditions
• Managing the interface between emergency, elective and outpatient pathways to optimise overall hospital capacity utilisation
• Integrating capacity planning with performance metrics, financial implications and quality outcomes
• Building organisational capability to maintain efficient patient flow while preserving safety, dignity and care quality

MODULE 03
Resource Allocation, Scheduling and Operational Efficiency
• Designing resource allocation frameworks that optimise staffing, equipment and support services across hospital departments and shifts
• Establishing scheduling systems and rostering practices that balance operational needs, staff wellbeing and service continuity
• Applying lean and process improvement principles to identify and eliminate waste, duplication and inefficiency in hospital operations
• Managing the trade-offs between cost efficiency, service quality and staff workload in resource-constrained environments
• Integrating resource management with performance monitoring and continuous improvement cycles
• Building organisational capability to achieve sustainable operational efficiency without compromising patient care or staff experience

MODULE 04
Facilities, Infrastructure and Smart Hospital Operations
• Examining the role of facilities management and physical infrastructure in supporting efficient, safe and patient-centred hospital operations
• Designing approaches to integrate smart hospital technologies, automation and digital infrastructure into operational workflows
• Establishing processes for maintenance planning, space utilisation optimisation and infrastructure resilience
• Managing the implications of digital transformation and smart systems on operational processes, staff capability and patient experience
• Integrating facilities and infrastructure considerations into broader operational planning, risk management and sustainability strategies
• Building organisational capability to leverage smart hospital capabilities for enhanced operational performance and future readiness

MODULE 05
Support Services, Logistics and Ancillary Operations
• Developing frameworks for managing support services including logistics, supply chain interfaces, catering, cleaning and other ancillary functions that enable clinical delivery
• Establishing operational standards, performance metrics and coordination mechanisms for support services aligned with hospital priorities
• Designing logistics and inventory management systems that ensure timely availability of resources while minimising waste and cost
• Managing the interface between support services and clinical operations to optimise overall hospital efficiency and patient experience
• Integrating support services management with quality, safety and regulatory compliance requirements
• Building organisational capability to deliver reliable, efficient and responsive support operations that underpin hospital performance

MODULE 06
Performance Measurement, KPIs and Operational Intelligence
• Developing comprehensive performance measurement frameworks with relevant operational KPIs that reflect efficiency, quality, safety and patient experience dimensions
• Establishing data collection, analysis and reporting processes that provide timely, accurate and actionable intelligence for operational decision-makers
• Designing operational dashboards, benchmarking processes and exception reporting mechanisms that highlight areas requiring attention or improvement
• Managing the use of operational data to identify trends, diagnose issues and evaluate the impact of improvement initiatives
• Integrating performance measurements with governance reporting, accountability mechanisms and strategic planning cycles
• Building organisational capability to become more data-driven and evidence-based in hospital operations management

MODULE 07
Operational Risk, Resilience and Business Continuity
• Identifying and assessing key operational risks in hospital environments including supply disruptions, infrastructure failures, surge events and process vulnerabilities
• Developing risk mitigation strategies, contingency plans and business continuity arrangements that protect critical hospital functions
• Establishing escalation protocols, crisis management structures and recovery processes for operational disruptions
• Managing the implications of operational risk events on patient safety, service continuity and organisational reputation
• Integrating operational risk management with broader organisational risk, governance and compliance frameworks
• Building organisational capability to maintain resilience and rapid recovery in the face of operational challenges and emergencies

Digital Enablement and Data-Driven Hospital Operations
• Exploring opportunities to leverage digital tools, automation and data analytics to enhance hospital operational efficiency and decision support
• Designing approaches for integrating operational systems, electronic platforms and real-time data into daily management and coordination processes
• Establishing data governance, quality and security requirements that support credible operational intelligence and digital transformation
• Managing the organisational, cultural and capability implications of digital adoption in hospital operations environments
• Integrating digital enablement with performance improvement, patient flow and resource management strategies
• Building organisational capability to harness digital technologies for smarter, more responsive and efficient hospital operations

MODULE 09
Change Leadership and Continuous Improvement in Operations
• Leading change initiatives that embed operational excellence, process discipline and continuous improvement into hospital culture and practice
• Designing improvement programmes that engage staff at all levels in identifying opportunities and implementing sustainable changes
• Establishing governance, project management and benefit realisation approaches for operational transformation initiatives
• Managing resistance, cultural barriers and behavioural change requirements associated with operational improvements
• Integrating continuous improvement with performance management, recognition systems and leadership development
• Building organisational capability to sustain operational excellence and adapt processes in response to changing demands and evidence

Governance, Accountability and Strategic Alignment of Hospital Operations
• Designing governance structures, committees and reporting lines that provide effective oversight of hospital operations and performance
• Establishing accountability frameworks that clarify roles, responsibilities and escalation pathways for operational issues and risks
• Aligning hospital operations with organisational strategy, value-based healthcare principles and ESG sustainability goals
• Managing the interface between operational governance, clinical governance, financial management and external regulatory requirements
• Integrating operational performance into board and executive decision-making with clear metrics and narrative reporting
• Building organisational capability to treat hospital operations as a strategic function that delivers measurable value and supports long-term organisational success

courses.title: Influencing, Persuasion & Negotiation Communication Masterclass
courses.overview: Professionals with strong technical expertise frequently discover that their most important recommendations are diluted, delayed or dismissed because they lack the precise influencing skills training required to move stakeholders from passive understanding to active commitment in complex organisational settings. This persuasion negotiation communication masterclass develops the strategic capability to analyse audiences, construct compelling arguments and conduct principled negotiations that secure alignment and drive decisions. Participants master ethical influence techniques, adaptive communication and relationship-preserving negotiation approaches that distinguish those who shape outcomes from those who merely inform. This course can be facilitated in London, Dubai, Kuala Lumpur, Nairobi, and other major business centres on client-preferred dates.
whyChoose: Prevent the hidden career cost of technically sound proposals that fail to gain traction because they lack the persuasive structure and stakeholder insight required to overcome resistance and inertia

Eliminate the professional risk of being perceived as lacking strategic judgement when influence attempts come across as either overly aggressive or insufficiently compelling to senior decision-makers
Reduce the organisational cost of stalled initiatives, compromised decisions and repeated negotiations that arise when communication fails to build genuine commitment rather than reluctant compliance
Avoid the cumulative damage to reputation that occurs when professionals repeatedly leave critical meetings or discussions without having shifted stakeholder positions in favour of better outcomes
Close the gap between positional authority and actual influence that often limits the impact of high-potential individuals who lack formal power yet carry significant responsibility for results
Overcome the inefficiency of investing substantial time in stakeholder engagement only to achieve partial or temporary alignment that unravels when pressure or competing priorities emerge
audience: Director of Corporate Affairs and Stakeholder Relations accountable for high stakes influence and negotiation outcomes across internal and external constituencies
Head of Business Development leading complex partnership negotiations, investment discussions and strategic alignment conversations
Communications Manager responsible for stakeholder messaging, reputation management and cross-functional influence initiatives
Senior Corporate Affairs Manager or Stakeholder Engagement Lead managing sensitive negotiations and multi-party alignment processes
Business Development Executive or Corporate Communications Manager preparing and conducting client, partner and internal influence discussions
Corporate Communications Executive or Stakeholder Relations Analyst supporting negotiation preparation and managing day-to-day stakeholder influence activities
objectives: By the end of this masterclass, participants will be able to:
Design and execute influence and persuasion strategies that secure stakeholder alignment and commitment to organisational priorities without relying on formal authority
Apply principled negotiation communication frameworks that achieve sustainable agreements while strengthening rather than damaging long-term professional relationships
Analyse stakeholder motivations, decision triggers and resistance patterns with precision to tailor influence approaches for maximum receptivity and impact
Structure persuasive arguments that combine logical rigour, emotional resonance and credible evidence to move audiences from scepticism to support
Manage high-pressure negotiation dynamics, objections and impasses with composure, strategic flexibility and ethical conduct
Adapt influence and negotiation techniques for virtual, hybrid and cross-cultural environments while maintaining presence, clarity and relationship quality
Build and sustain personal credibility and trust as the foundation for ongoing influence across diverse stakeholder groups and organisational contexts
Establish personal disciplines for continuous development of influencing capability that compound over time and support career advancement into senior leadership roles
deliveryApproach: Dynamic workshop methodology combining expert facilitation with extensive live role-play, negotiation simulations and influence practice using participants’ real workplace scenarios
Multiple rounds of skill application with immediate peer and instructor feedback, including video review for detailed self-assessment of presence, tone and strategic effectiveness
Collaborative case analysis of successful and unsuccessful influence and negotiation situations to extract precise techniques and avoid common failure patterns
Focused drills on stakeholder mapping, argument structuring, objection handling and principled negotiation with iterative refinement and coaching
Personal influence audits and action planning where participants apply new frameworks directly to current challenges with expert guidance
Provision of ready-to-use stakeholder analysis templates, persuasion frameworks, negotiation checklists and digital resources for immediate post-course application
courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
The Strategic Foundations of Professional Influence
• Examining how influence operates in modern organisations where formal authority is often limited and stakeholder alignment determines success or failure
• Identifying the hidden costs of ineffective influence including stalled decisions, compromised outcomes and damaged professional credibility
• Understanding the ethical foundations of sustainable influence that builds trust rather than expends it through manipulation or short-term tactics
• Recognising the direct link between influence capability and career progression, organisational impact and personal professional reputation
• Assessing personal current influence patterns, strengths and blind spots against the demands of complex stakeholder environments
• Establishing clear personal objectives for developing principled, effective and sustainable influencing capability

MODULE 02
Mapping Stakeholder Psychology and Decision Drivers
• Applying structured approaches to identify stakeholder interests, motivations, concerns and hidden decision criteria before any influence attempt
• Developing techniques for gathering intelligence on stakeholder priorities, relationships and potential resistance through formal and informal channels
• Understanding cognitive biases, emotional triggers and social proof mechanisms that shape stakeholder receptivity to influence
• Creating stakeholder influence maps that highlight key decision-makers, influencers, blockers and potential allies
• Tailoring influence strategies to different stakeholder profiles including technical experts, senior leaders, operational teams and external partners
• Practising rapid stakeholder analysis for time-sensitive situations where preparation windows are short

MODULE 03
The Architecture of Persuasive Arguments
• Designing clear, logical and emotionally resonant argument structures that guide stakeholders from current position to desired outcome
• Applying frameworks for opening with impact, building credible evidence, addressing counter-arguments and closing with compelling calls to action
• Balancing analytical rigour with narrative and emotional elements to create arguments that are both intellectually sound and motivationally powerful
• Managing information complexity so that key messages stand out while supporting detail remains accessible without overwhelming the audience
• Developing techniques for adapting argument structure in real time based on emerging stakeholder reactions and objections
• Creating personal persuasion templates for common influence situations including proposals, change initiatives and resource requests

MODULE 04
Building Credibility and Trust as Influence Capital
• Understanding that credibility is the essential foundation upon which all sustainable influence is built and maintained
• Developing techniques for establishing expertise, reliability and integrity in the eyes of stakeholders before and during influence attempts
• Managing consistency between words and actions that either builds or erodes the trust required for ongoing influence
• Handling situations where credibility has been damaged and developing approaches to rebuild stakeholder confidence over time
• Balancing self-advocacy with organisational interest in ways that enhance rather than diminish perceived integrity
• Creating personal habits and disciplines that accumulate influence capital through consistent professional conduct

MODULE 05
Principled Negotiation: Preparation and Strategic Framing
• Applying structured preparation frameworks that clarify objectives, alternatives, stakeholder interests and potential zones of agreement before entering negotiations
• Developing skills in framing negotiation issues in ways that expand the pie and create value rather than simply claiming existing value
• Identifying and preparing for likely objections, resistance points and alternative proposals from counterparties
• Establishing clear walk-away positions, BATNA considerations and acceptable trade-off parameters in advance
• Managing the balance between assertiveness and collaboration that characterises effective principled negotiation
• Creating personal negotiation preparation routines that significantly improve outcomes and reduce reactive stress during discussions

MODULE 06
Managing Resistance, Objections and Impasse Dynamics
• Developing real-time techniques for recognising, surfacing and addressing stakeholder resistance without becoming defensive or escalating conflict
• Applying structured approaches to handling objections that acknowledge concerns while redirecting towards constructive dialogue and mutual interest
• Managing negotiation impasses through reframing, creative option generation and strategic breaks that preserve momentum and relationships
• Building skills in maintaining composure, strategic thinking and professional tone under pressure and provocation
• Developing recovery techniques for moments when influence attempts or negotiations do not proceed as planned
• Creating personal approaches to turning resistance into opportunities for deeper understanding and stronger agreements

MODULE 07
Non-Verbal Presence and Emotional Intelligence in Influence Situations
• Understanding how non-verbal communication either reinforces or undermines verbal influence attempts in both in-person and virtual settings
• Developing skills in reading stakeholder emotional states, micro-expressions and body language to adjust approach in real time
• Applying emotional intelligence techniques to manage own reactions and respond constructively to stakeholder emotions during high-stakes discussions
• Building capability to project calm authority, genuine confidence and empathetic presence that enhances receptivity to influence
• Managing the specific challenges of conveying presence, credibility and emotional attunement through digital and hybrid channels
• Practising integrated verbal and non-verbal influence techniques through realistic simulations with feedback

MODULE 08
Virtual, Hybrid and Cross-Cultural Influence and Negotiation
• Adapting influence and negotiation approaches for virtual and hybrid environments where traditional cues are limited and attention dynamics differ
• Developing techniques for building rapport, reading reactions and maintaining momentum across digital platforms and time zones
• Understanding how cultural differences in communication style, decision-making and relationship expectations affect influence and negotiation effectiveness
• Building cultural intelligence to adapt framing, pacing, formality and relationship-building approaches appropriately across diverse stakeholder groups
• Managing the added complexity of multi-party, multi-cultural negotiations where assumptions about process and outcomes may differ significantly
• Establishing personal standards and preparation routines for consistent effectiveness in global and digitally mediated situations

MODULE 09
Ethical Influence, Long-Term Relationships and Reputation
• Understanding the long-term consequences of influence tactics on professional reputation, stakeholder trust and future opportunities
• Developing approaches to influence that achieve immediate objectives while strengthening rather than depleting relationship capital over time
• Managing situations where short-term gains conflict with long-term relationship considerations and making principled trade-off decisions
• Building capability to influence upwards, sideways and downwards with equal effectiveness and ethical consistency
• Creating personal boundaries and guidelines for influence that protect both organisational interests and personal integrity
• Positioning influence capability as a core leadership competency that supports career progression and organisational contribution

MODULE 10
From Personal Mastery to Organisational Influence Capability
• Developing approaches to modelling and coaching influencing skills within teams to raise collective capability and consistency
• Establishing organisational frameworks, guidelines and training that embed principled influence and negotiation practices
• Measuring and demonstrating the value of improved influence capability to senior stakeholders through clearer alignment and faster decision-making
• Building personal resilience and continuous development habits that sustain and deepen influencing effectiveness over a career
• Creating a long-term personal influence development plan that integrates skill refinement with expanding scope and responsibility
• Committing to positioning influence, persuasion and negotiation as strategic professional capabilities that define leadership contribution
expectedOutcomes: Participants will be able to:
Secure stakeholder alignment and commitment on strategic priorities through influence approaches that build genuine support rather than reluctant compliance
Conduct negotiations that achieve sustainable outcomes while preserving and often strengthening the relationships required for ongoing collaboration
Entering high-stakes influence situations with clear strategy, confident presence and adaptive capability that significantly improves success rates
Handle resistance, objections and difficult dynamics with composure and strategic flexibility that maintains momentum and respect
Adapt influence and negotiation approaches fluidly across in-person, virtual, hybrid and cross-cultural contexts without loss of effectiveness
Build a personal reputation as someone whose communication consistently shapes decisions, aligns stakeholders and delivers organisational results
organisationalImpact: Faster and higher-quality decision-making through influence and negotiation that secures genuine stakeholder commitment rather than superficial agreement
Reduced time and cost associated with stalled initiatives, repeated negotiations and compromised outcomes caused by ineffective influence attempts
Stronger organisational reputation when professionals at all levels represent positions with credibility, strategic clarity and relationship intelligence
Enhanced internal capability as skilled influencers coach and raise standards among colleagues and teams
Improved cross-functional and external collaboration through negotiation approaches that create value and preserve long-term partnerships
Sustainable improvement in how the organisation secures alignment, manages conflict and drives progress through principled communication
personalImpact: Transformed confidence and capability to shape outcomes in meetings, discussions and negotiations where decisions that matter are made
Greater career mobility as the ability to influence without formal authority becomes a recognised strength that opens doors to senior roles
Increased impact and visibility as your contributions consistently move stakeholders towards better decisions and stronger alignment
Reduced stress and frustration in high-stakes communication situations through reliable frameworks, presence and adaptive techniques
Clearer professional brand as someone who can be trusted to represent ideas, teams and the organisation effectively in complex stakeholder environments
A personal influence system and development roadmap that delivers compounding professional returns throughout your career

The professionals who shape organisations are rarely those with the best ideas alone. They are those who can move others to see, believe and act. This masterclass develops exactly that capability with precision, ethics and lasting impact.

Enrol now in the Influencing, Persuasion & Negotiation Communication Masterclass to develop the strategic influence and principled negotiation skills that will define your ability to lead outcomes and advance your career.

courses.title: International Relations & Foreign Policy Masterclass
courses.overview: In today's interconnected environment, organisations must navigate rapid geopolitical shifts, evolving foreign policy priorities and complex international interdependencies that directly influence strategic opportunities and risks. courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
Foundations of International Relations in Contemporary Global Contexts
• Understanding the practical value of international relations knowledge for organisational strategy, risk management and external engagement in an interconnected world
• Examining the core dynamics that shape global interactions including power balances, economic interdependencies and emerging transnational challenges
