• Mapping the interface between international developments, national policy environments and organisational decision-making processes
• Establishing the organisational case for investing in international relations capability as a strategic asset for resilience and opportunity identification

MODULE 02
Geopolitical Analysis and Foreign Policy Trend Identification
• Developing systematic approaches to monitoring and interpreting geopolitical developments, foreign policy announcements and international political signals
• Applying practical analytical frameworks to assess the implications of global events for organisational interests, operations and strategic planning
• Identifying early indicators of policy shifts, alliance changes and emerging international risks that may affect organisational objectives
• Utilising open-source intelligence, diplomatic reporting and credible analysis to build accurate, timely pictures of international environments
• Prioritising geopolitical developments based on potential impact, urgency and relevance to specific organisational contexts and sectors
• Creating regular briefing processes that translate complex international developments into clear, actionable insights for senior leadership

MODULE 03
Multilateral Engagement and Global Institutional Dynamics
• Understanding the structure, decision-making processes and influence pathways within multilateral organisations and international bodies
• Developing practical approaches for engaging constructively with multilateral institutions on policy, regulatory and strategic matters
• Identifying opportunities for organisational participation, advocacy and partnership within multilateral frameworks and global governance processes
• Managing the complexities of multi-stakeholder environments where diverse national interests and organisational objectives intersect
• Building capability to interpret multilateral outcomes, resolutions and policy developments in terms of practical implications for organisations
• Establishing internal processes for tracking multilateral agendas and preparing timely organisational responses to international institutional developments

MODULE 04
Strategic Stakeholder Engagement in International Contexts
• Designing comprehensive stakeholder maps that identify key international actors, decision-makers, influencers and potential partners or adversaries
• Developing tailored engagement strategies that align with organisational objectives while respecting the protocols and norms of international diplomacy
• Building skills in preparing for and conducting high-level international meetings, negotiations and relationship-building activities
• Managing cultural, political and protocol considerations when engaging with foreign government officials, international organisation representatives and global partners
• Establishing systems for tracking international stakeholder interactions, managing relationships and maintaining institutional memory across engagements
• Creating sustainable approaches to stakeholder engagement that build long-term credibility, trust and influence in international environments

MODULE 05
Political Risk Assessment and Scenario Planning
• Developing robust political risk assessment methodologies tailored to organisational contexts, sectors and international exposure profiles
• Conducting structured scenario planning exercises that explore plausible future international developments and their potential organisational implications
• Identifying early warning indicators and trigger points that signal emerging political, regulatory or geopolitical risks requiring organisational attention
• Integrating political risk considerations into broader enterprise risk management, strategic planning and investment decision processes
• Building organisational capability to respond rapidly and effectively to unexpected international developments and policy shocks
• Establishing regular review cycles that update risk assessments and scenarios in light of evolving global conditions and new information

MODULE 06
Managing International Crises and Diplomatic Disruptions
• Preparing organisational protocols for responding to international crises, diplomatic incidents and sudden foreign policy shifts affecting operations or reputation
• Developing crisis communication strategies that maintain credibility with international stakeholders while protecting organisational interests during high-pressure situations
• Coordinating internal response teams, external advisors and international liaison during geopolitical disruptions and diplomatic challenges
• Learning from past international crises to strengthen future preparedness, organisational resilience and institutional learning
• Balancing transparency requirements with legal, commercial and diplomatic sensitivities when managing international incidents
• Rebuilding trust and relationships with international stakeholders following crises or controversies through structured recovery approaches

MODULE 07
Soft Power Strategies and Cultural Diplomacy Applications
• Understanding the role of soft power, cultural influence and public diplomacy in shaping international perceptions and advancing organisational interests
• Developing practical approaches for leveraging cultural assets, values and narratives to build goodwill and influence in international contexts
• Identifying opportunities for cultural diplomacy initiatives, partnership programmes and public engagement that strengthen international relationships
• Managing the interface between formal diplomatic engagement, public diplomacy activities and broader stakeholder communication strategies
• Building capability to design and implement soft power initiatives that align with organisational brand, values and strategic objectives
• Integrating cultural intelligence and soft power considerations into international engagement planning to enhance effectiveness and reduce friction

MODULE 08
Translating International Relations Insight into Organisational Strategy
• Developing processes for systematically integrating international relations analysis into corporate strategy, risk management and external affairs functions
• Creating governance structures, roles and decision protocols that ensure international developments receive appropriate strategic attention at leadership level
• Building internal training, capability development and knowledge management systems that sustain high standards of international relations practice
• Establishing performance metrics and evaluation frameworks that demonstrate the value of international relations investment to organisational leadership
• Positioning international relations capability as a core strategic function that contributes to long-term organisational resilience, opportunity realisation and competitive advantage
• Creating continuous improvement cycles that incorporate emerging global trends, lessons from engagement and evolving organisational priorities

courses.title: Joint Venture Governance & Risk Management
courses.overview: Joint ventures demand rigorous joint venture governance training to maintain partner alignment, protect shared value and manage the complex risks that arise from shared ownership and control. This JV risk management masterclass provides advanced frameworks for designing effective board structures, implementing integrated risk systems and embedding compliance and ESG oversight within jointly owned entities. Participants develop capability to anticipate governance failures, mitigate operational and reputational risks and sustain constructive collaboration throughout the venture lifecycle. This course can be facilitated in London, Dubai, Kuala Lumpur, Nairobi, and other major business centres on client-preferred dates.
whyChoose: Design robust board and committee governance frameworks that balance partner representation with efficient decision-making and clear accountability in joint venture entities
Implement integrated risk management systems that identify, assess and mitigate operational, financial, regulatory and reputational risks across the joint venture lifecycle
Embed ESG and sustainability risk oversight into JV governance structures to meet partner expectations, regulatory requirements and long-term value protection objectives
Strengthen partner relationship oversight and conflict prevention mechanisms that anticipate tensions and resolve issues before they damage venture performance or relationships
Establish financial, compliance and operational risk controls that protect the JV entity and its partners while supporting transparent reporting and stakeholder confidence
Build organisational capability to manage governance and risk across the full joint venture lifecycle, including major transitions and exit events, with discipline and foresight
audience: JV Directors and Heads of Joint Ventures accountable for strategic oversight, governance effectiveness and risk stewardship of specific joint venture entities
Joint Venture Governance Managers and Risk Managers responsible for designing, implementing and monitoring JV governance frameworks and risk management systems
Compliance and Legal Managers tasked with ensuring regulatory adherence, contractual compliance and governance integrity within joint ventures
Performance and Finance Managers overseeing JV financial controls, reporting accuracy and value protection mechanisms
JV Operations Managers and Governance Leads managing day-to-day governance processes, risk monitoring and partner coordination activities
JV Governance Officers and Risk Analysts supporting board processes, risk assessments, compliance documentation and performance monitoring under senior guidance
objectives: By the end of this programme, participants will be able to:
Design joint venture board governance frameworks that balance partner representation with efficient decision-making and clear accountability mechanisms
Implement integrated risk management systems that identify, assess and mitigate operational, financial and reputational risks across the joint venture lifecycle
Embed ESG and sustainability risk oversight into JV governance structures to meet partner expectations, regulatory requirements and long-term value protection objectives
Establish partner relationship oversight and conflict prevention processes that anticipate tensions and resolve issues before they damage venture performance or relationships
Develop financial, compliance and operational risk controls that protect the JV entity and its partners while supporting transparent reporting and stakeholder confidence
Create governance and risk reporting frameworks that enable timely escalation, informed decision-making and clear accountability to all joint venture partners
Design lifecycle risk management approaches that address governance and risk implications of major transitions, capital events and exit scenarios
Build organisational capability to sustain effective JV governance and risk management through capability development, continuous improvement and cultural alignment
deliveryApproach: Interactive workshops focused on designing JV board structures, integrated risk frameworks and ESG oversight mechanisms using realistic joint venture scenarios
In-depth analysis of governance successes and failures in joint ventures with emphasis on board effectiveness, risk outcomes and partner relationship dynamics
Simulation exercises requiring participants to develop governance charters, risk registers and conflict resolution protocols under realistic partner and regulatory constraints
Collaborative group projects developing end-to-end JV governance and risk management plans including board frameworks, risk systems and reporting protocols
Masterclasses on specialised topics including ESG integration in JV governance, partner conflict prevention and lifecycle risk management
Personal JV governance projects applying programme frameworks directly to participants’ current joint ventures with expert facilitation and structured peer feedback
courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
Foundations of Joint Venture Governance and Risk Principles
• Examining the distinctive governance challenges that arise from shared ownership, control and economic interests in joint venture entities
• Defining the core principles of effective JV governance including accountability, transparency, fairness and protection of partner interests
• Identifying the principal categories of risk that joint ventures face including operational, financial, regulatory, reputational and partner-related risks
• Establishing the foundational requirements for sound JV governance including clear structures, documented processes and aligned incentives
• Recognising the impact of partner asymmetry, cultural differences and evolving strategic priorities on governance effectiveness and risk exposure
• Mapping the governance and risk management lifecycle from JV formation through operational phases to major transitions and exit events

MODULE 02
Board and Committee Governance in Joint Venture Entities
• Designing board composition, committee structures and decision-making authority that balance partner representation with operational efficiency
• Establishing clear roles, responsibilities and reporting lines for the JV board, management team and partner-nominated directors
• Developing processes for board effectiveness, meeting management, information flow and decision quality in shared ownership contexts
• Managing the implications of veto rights, reserved matters and supermajority requirements on governance dynamics and venture agility
• Integrating governance requirements into JV agreements, operational procedures and ongoing compliance frameworks
• Building organisational capability to sustain effective board governance that protects partner interests while enabling timely and informed decision-making

MODULE 03
Integrated Risk Management Frameworks for Joint Ventures
• Designing comprehensive risk management frameworks that address risks at both the JV entity and partner levels in an integrated manner
• Establishing processes for risk identification, assessment, prioritisation and mitigation across operational, financial and strategic dimensions
• Developing risk registers, heat maps and reporting mechanisms that provide clear visibility to the JV board and partner representatives
• Managing the interaction between JV-specific risks and the broader risk appetites and exposures of the respective partner organisations
• Integrating risk considerations into strategic planning, capital allocation and performance management processes within the joint venture
• Building organisational capability to maintain dynamic risk management that adapts to changing circumstances while protecting venture value

MODULE 04
Compliance, Regulatory and Legal Risk Oversight in JVs
• Interpreting the compliance and regulatory obligations that apply to joint venture entities across relevant jurisdictions and sectors
• Designing compliance monitoring, reporting and assurance processes that meet regulatory requirements and partner governance standards
• Establishing frameworks for managing legal and contractual risks arising from JV agreements, operational contracts and third-party arrangements
• Managing the implications of regulatory change, enforcement actions and compliance failures on JV operations, partner relationships and reputational standing
• Integrating compliance considerations into governance decision-making, risk oversight and operational management processes
• Building organisational capability to sustain robust compliance discipline that protects the JV entity and maintains partner confidence

MODULE 05
Operational and Performance Risk Management in Joint Ventures
• Identifying and assessing key operational risks including execution, supply chain, technology, health and safety and quality risks within JV operations
• Designing operational risk controls, monitoring mechanisms and incident response processes that protect venture performance and partner interests
• Establishing performance risk frameworks that address delivery shortfalls, cost overruns and quality issues with clear escalation and remediation protocols
• Managing the implications of operational risk events on financial performance, partner relationships and strategic objectives
• Integrating operational risk considerations into day-to-day management, project oversight and continuous improvement initiatives
• Building organisational capability to maintain operational resilience and performance discipline within joint venture structures

MODULE 06
ESG and Sustainability Risk Integration in JV Governance
• Examining the implications of ESG factors, climate transition and sustainability risks for joint venture governance, operations and long-term value
• Designing frameworks for embedding ESG oversight, reporting and performance requirements into JV board processes and risk management systems
• Establishing processes for assessing and mitigating environmental, social and governance risks that may affect the venture or its partners
• Managing the implications of partner ESG expectations, regulatory sustainability requirements and stakeholder scrutiny on JV governance and strategy
• Integrating ESG considerations into risk registers, performance metrics and governance decision-making within the joint venture entity
• Building organisational capability to sustain ESG-integrated governance that protects long-term value and meets partner and regulatory expectations

MODULE 07
Partner Relationship Risk and Conflict Prevention
• Identifying the sources of tension and conflict that commonly arise in joint ventures including strategic divergence, cultural differences and performance disputes
• Designing partner relationship oversight mechanisms that promote transparency, communication and early identification of emerging issues
• Establishing escalation protocols, mediation processes and dispute prevention mechanisms that protect the JV entity while respecting partner interests
• Managing the implications of changing partner strategies, personnel or circumstances on relationship dynamics and governance effectiveness
• Integrating partner relationship risk considerations into board reporting, risk oversight and strategic decision-making processes
• Building organisational capability to sustain constructive partner collaboration and prevent conflicts from damaging venture value or relationships

MODULE 08
Financial and Capital Risk Governance in Joint Ventures
• Designing financial oversight frameworks that ensure transparency, accuracy and timely reporting of JV financial performance to all partners
• Establishing processes for capital planning, funding decisions, distribution policies and financial risk management within the joint venture
• Managing the implications of financial performance, capital needs and funding constraints on governance decisions and partner relationships
• Integrating financial controls, audit requirements and partner reporting obligations into JV operational and governance processes
• Developing frameworks for evaluating and approving significant financial decisions including investments, borrowings and major expenditures
• Building organisational capability to maintain financial discipline, capital efficiency and transparent reporting within joint venture structures

MODULE 09
Dispute Prevention, Escalation and Resolution Mechanisms
• Examining the principles of dispute prevention that reduce the likelihood of formal conflicts arising within joint venture governance and operations
• Designing escalation frameworks, mediation processes and internal resolution mechanisms that address disagreements before they require external intervention
• Establishing clear protocols for invoking formal dispute resolution procedures when internal mechanisms are exhausted
• Managing the implications of disputes on JV operations, partner relationships, governance functioning and venture value
• Integrating dispute prevention and resolution considerations into JV agreements, governance charters and ongoing relationship management
• Building organisational capability to manage disagreements constructively and protect the JV entity during periods of tension or conflict

MODULE 10
Lifecycle Risk Management and Transition Planning
• Identifying the governance and risk implications of major lifecycle events including capital raises, ownership changes, strategic pivots and exit scenarios
• Establishing processes for assessing and preparing for transition risks that arise during changes in partner composition, venture scope or market conditions
• Designing governance and risk frameworks that support orderly decision-making and value protection during periods of significant change
• Managing the implications of lifecycle events on partner alignment, operational continuity and long-term venture viability
• Integrating lifecycle risk considerations into strategic planning, risk oversight and governance processes from the earliest stages of the joint venture
• Building organisational capability to anticipate, prepare for and manage governance and risk challenges across the full joint venture lifecycle

Comprehensive JV governance frameworks and integrated risk management systems ready for implementation with clear accountability and reporting lines
Documented board structures, risk registers and ESG oversight mechanisms that protect partner interests and support venture performance
Enhanced capability to prevent, identify and resolve governance and partner relationship issues before they damage venture value
Robust compliance, financial and operational risk controls that reduce exposure and support transparent stakeholder reporting
Clear escalation, dispute prevention and lifecycle transition frameworks that protect the JV entity during periods of change or tension
Improved board effectiveness, risk visibility and partner alignment that sustain long-term joint venture success and value creation
organisationalImpact: Stronger protection of joint venture value and partner interests through disciplined governance, integrated risk management and proactive conflict prevention
Reduced incidence and impact of governance failures, compliance breaches and partner disputes that can destroy venture value
Enhanced ability to maintain partner alignment and operational focus while adapting to changing circumstances and lifecycle events
Greater organisational confidence in managing complex shared ownership structures with clear frameworks and accountable processes
Sustainable improvement in JV governance quality and risk discipline through standardised approaches and capability development
Increased stakeholder confidence through transparent governance, robust risk oversight and demonstrable commitment to protecting shared enterprise value

Enhanced ability to influence JV board decisions, manage governance processes and drive risk-aware decision-making within shared ownership structures
Clearer professional pathway towards JV Director, Head of Joint Ventures, Governance Director and similar senior JV leadership roles

sourceRecord.courseSyllabus:
MODULE 01
Foundations of Joint Venture Governance and Risk Principles
• Examining the distinctive governance challenges that arise from shared ownership, control and economic interests in joint venture entities
• Defining the core principles of effective JV governance including accountability, transparency, fairness and protection of partner interests
• Identifying the principal categories of risk that joint ventures face including operational, financial, regulatory, reputational and partner-related risks
• Establishing the foundational requirements for sound JV governance including clear structures, documented processes and aligned incentives
• Recognising the impact of partner asymmetry, cultural differences and evolving strategic priorities on governance effectiveness and risk exposure
• Mapping the governance and risk management lifecycle from JV formation through operational phases to major transitions and exit events

MODULE 02
Board and Committee Governance in Joint Venture Entities
• Designing board composition, committee structures and decision-making authority that balance partner representation with operational efficiency
• Establishing clear roles, responsibilities and reporting lines for the JV board, management team and partner-nominated directors
• Developing processes for board effectiveness, meeting management, information flow and decision quality in shared ownership contexts
• Managing the implications of veto rights, reserved matters and supermajority requirements on governance dynamics and venture agility
• Integrating governance requirements into JV agreements, operational procedures and ongoing compliance frameworks
• Building organisational capability to sustain effective board governance that protects partner interests while enabling timely and informed decision-making

MODULE 03
Integrated Risk Management Frameworks for Joint Ventures
• Designing comprehensive risk management frameworks that address risks at both the JV entity and partner levels in an integrated manner
• Establishing processes for risk identification, assessment, prioritisation and mitigation across operational, financial and strategic dimensions
• Developing risk registers, heat maps and reporting mechanisms that provide clear visibility to the JV board and partner representatives
• Managing the interaction between JV-specific risks and the broader risk appetites and exposures of the respective partner organisations
• Integrating risk considerations into strategic planning, capital allocation and performance management processes within the joint venture
• Building organisational capability to maintain dynamic risk management that adapts to changing circumstances while protecting venture value

MODULE 04
Compliance, Regulatory and Legal Risk Oversight in JVs
• Interpreting the compliance and regulatory obligations that apply to joint venture entities across relevant jurisdictions and sectors
• Designing compliance monitoring, reporting and assurance processes that meet regulatory requirements and partner governance standards
• Establishing frameworks for managing legal and contractual risks arising from JV agreements, operational contracts and third-party arrangements
• Managing the implications of regulatory change, enforcement actions and compliance failures on JV operations, partner relationships and reputational standing
• Integrating compliance considerations into governance decision-making, risk oversight and operational management processes
• Building organisational capability to sustain robust compliance discipline that protects the JV entity and maintains partner confidence

MODULE 05
Operational and Performance Risk Management in Joint Ventures
• Identifying and assessing key operational risks including execution, supply chain, technology, health and safety and quality risks within JV operations
• Designing operational risk controls, monitoring mechanisms and incident response processes that protect venture performance and partner interests
• Establishing performance risk frameworks that address delivery shortfalls, cost overruns and quality issues with clear escalation and remediation protocols
• Managing the implications of operational risk events on financial performance, partner relationships and strategic objectives
• Integrating operational risk considerations into day-to-day management, project oversight and continuous improvement initiatives
• Building organisational capability to maintain operational resilience and performance discipline within joint venture structures

MODULE 06
ESG and Sustainability Risk Integration in JV Governance
• Examining the implications of ESG factors, climate transition and sustainability risks for joint venture governance, operations and long-term value
• Designing frameworks for embedding ESG oversight, reporting and performance requirements into JV board processes and risk management systems
• Establishing processes for assessing and mitigating environmental, social and governance risks that may affect the venture or its partners
• Managing the implications of partner ESG expectations, regulatory sustainability requirements and stakeholder scrutiny on JV governance and strategy
• Integrating ESG considerations into risk registers, performance metrics and governance decision-making within the joint venture entity
• Building organisational capability to sustain ESG-integrated governance that protects long-term value and meets partner and regulatory expectations

MODULE 07
Partner Relationship Risk and Conflict Prevention
• Identifying the sources of tension and conflict that commonly arise in joint ventures including strategic divergence, cultural differences and performance disputes
• Designing partner relationship oversight mechanisms that promote transparency, communication and early identification of emerging issues
• Establishing escalation protocols, mediation processes and dispute prevention mechanisms that protect the JV entity while respecting partner interests
• Managing the implications of changing partner strategies, personnel or circumstances on relationship dynamics and governance effectiveness
• Integrating partner relationship risk considerations into board reporting, risk oversight and strategic decision-making processes
• Building organisational capability to sustain constructive partner collaboration and prevent conflicts from damaging venture value or relationships

MODULE 08
Financial and Capital Risk Governance in Joint Ventures
• Designing financial oversight frameworks that ensure transparency, accuracy and timely reporting of JV financial performance to all partners
• Establishing processes for capital planning, funding decisions, distribution policies and financial risk management within the joint venture
• Managing the implications of financial performance, capital needs and funding constraints on governance decisions and partner relationships
• Integrating financial controls, audit requirements and partner reporting obligations into JV operational and governance processes
• Developing frameworks for evaluating and approving significant financial decisions including investments, borrowings and major expenditures
• Building organisational capability to maintain financial discipline, capital efficiency and transparent reporting within joint venture structures

MODULE 09
Dispute Prevention, Escalation and Resolution Mechanisms
• Examining the principles of dispute prevention that reduce the likelihood of formal conflicts arising within joint venture governance and operations
• Designing escalation frameworks, mediation processes and internal resolution mechanisms that address disagreements before they require external intervention
• Establishing clear protocols for invoking formal dispute resolution procedures when internal mechanisms are exhausted
• Managing the implications of disputes on JV operations, partner relationships, governance functioning and venture value
• Integrating dispute prevention and resolution considerations into JV agreements, governance charters and ongoing relationship management
• Building organisational capability to manage disagreements constructively and protect the JV entity during periods of tension or conflict

MODULE 10
Lifecycle Risk Management and Transition Planning
• Identifying the governance and risk implications of major lifecycle events including capital raises, ownership changes, strategic pivots and exit scenarios
• Establishing processes for assessing and preparing for transition risks that arise during changes in partner composition, venture scope or market conditions
• Designing governance and risk frameworks that support orderly decision-making and value protection during periods of significant change
• Managing the implications of lifecycle events on partner alignment, operational continuity and long-term venture viability
• Integrating lifecycle risk considerations into strategic planning, risk oversight and governance processes from the earliest stages of the joint venture
• Building organisational capability to anticipate, prepare for and manage governance and risk challenges across the full joint venture lifecycle

courses.title: Joint Venture Negotiation & Structuring Excellence
courses.overview: Business development and M&A leaders must master the front-end art of joint venture negotiation training to select the right partners, structure balanced equity and governance arrangements and negotiate term sheets that protect long-term value before any binding contract is signed. This JV deal structuring excellence programme provides rigorous frameworks for partner evaluation, contribution valuation, risk allocation and term sheet development that create the foundation for successful jointly owned entities. Participants develop capability to manage complex negotiations, balance competing interests and produce clear, commercially sound term sheets that enable efficient transition to legal documentation. This course can be facilitated in London, Dubai, Kuala Lumpur, Nairobi, and other major business centres on client-preferred dates.
whyChoose: Identify and evaluate potential joint venture partners using structured criteria that assess strategic fit, cultural alignment, financial strength and operational capability
Design balanced equity structures and contribution valuations that reflect the relative value of each partner’s inputs while creating sustainable economic alignment
Develop clear governance frameworks and decision rights at the term sheet stage that prevent future disputes and enable efficient management of the joint venture
Structure risk allocation, liability provisions and exit mechanisms in term sheets that protect partner interests while maintaining commercial viability of the proposed venture
Lead effective negotiation processes that manage deal dynamics, build trust and achieve term sheets that serve as a solid foundation for subsequent legal documentation
Integrate digital deal rooms and AI-assisted due diligence tools into the structuring process to improve speed, rigour and quality of partner evaluation and term sheet preparation

Deal Analysts and Business Development Analysts supporting opportunity screening, data analysis and documentation preparation under senior guidance

Conduct rigorous partner evaluation and due diligence processes that assess strategic fit, financial capacity, cultural compatibility and operational capability

Lead structured negotiation processes that manage competing interests, build trust and produce commercially balanced term sheets ready for legal drafting
Integrate digital deal rooms and AI-assisted due diligence tools into partner evaluation and structuring workflows to improve rigour and efficiency
Prepare clear transition documentation and briefing materials that enable seamless handover from structuring teams to legal and contract drafting functions

courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
Strategic Rationale and Opportunity Screening for Joint Ventures
• Examining the strategic drivers that lead organisations to pursue joint ventures rather than acquisitions, organic growth or contractual partnerships
• Defining clear criteria for screening potential joint venture opportunities against corporate strategy, risk appetite and resource availability
• Identifying the key commercial and operational questions that must be resolved at the structuring stage before significant resources are committed
• Establishing processes for early-stage opportunity assessment that filter out unsuitable ventures before detailed partner engagement begins
• Recognising the resource, management attention and opportunity cost implications of pursuing joint venture structures
• Mapping the typical timeline and key decision gates from opportunity identification through to signed term sheet

MODULE 02
Partner Selection Criteria and Strategic Fit Assessment
• Designing structured frameworks for evaluating potential joint venture partners against strategic, financial, operational and cultural dimensions
• Establishing processes for gathering and analysing information on prospective partners including capabilities, track record and reputation
• Assessing cultural compatibility, management style alignment and long-term strategic intent between potential partners
• Managing the implications of asymmetric information and partner motivations during early-stage evaluation
• Developing criteria for shortlisting and prioritising potential partners before formal engagement begins
• Building organisational capability to conduct disciplined partner evaluation that reduces the risk of selecting unsuitable counterparts

MODULE 03
Due Diligence and Partner Evaluation Processes
• Designing comprehensive due diligence frameworks tailored to the joint venture context that address financial, operational, legal and reputational dimensions
• Establishing processes for planning, coordinating and interpreting due diligence findings to inform structuring and negotiation decisions
• Managing the interaction between internal analysis, external advisers and partner-provided information during the evaluation phase
• Integrating digital deal rooms and AI-assisted due diligence tools to improve the speed and depth of partner assessment
• Identifying red flags and material issues that should influence partner selection or term sheet positions
• Building organisational capability to conduct rigorous, efficient due diligence that supports confident structuring decisions

MODULE 04
Equity Structuring and Contribution Valuation
• Applying joint venture valuation methodology to assess the fair value of each partner’s proposed contributions to the venture
• Designing equity split structures that reflect relative contributions while creating appropriate incentives for ongoing performance
• Establishing processes for documenting and agreeing valuation assumptions and methodologies with all prospective partners
• Managing the implications of different contribution types including cash, assets, intellectual property and ongoing services
• Developing frameworks for addressing valuation disputes and reaching commercially acceptable equity arrangements
• Building organisational capability to produce defensible and mutually acceptable equity structures at the term sheet stage

MODULE 05
Governance and Decision Rights Design at Term Sheet Stage
• Designing high-level governance frameworks that define board composition, voting rights and key decision-making authorities
• Establishing the scope of reserved matters and veto rights that protect fundamental partner interests without paralysing operations
• Developing principles for balancing partner representation with the need for efficient day-to-day management of the joint venture
• Managing the implications of different governance models on control, information flow and dispute prevention
• Documenting governance principles in term sheets in sufficient detail to guide subsequent legal drafting
• Building organisational capability to design governance arrangements that support both partner protection and operational effectiveness

MODULE 06
Economic Terms and Value Sharing Mechanisms
• Designing economic terms that govern profit distribution, loss allocation and capital return mechanisms within the joint venture
• Establishing frameworks for addressing future capital requirements and the implications for ownership and control
• Developing principles for performance-based incentives, promoting structures and other mechanisms that align partner interests with venture success
• Managing the implications of different economic arrangements on partner behaviour, risk appetite and long-term alignment
• Documenting key economic principles in term sheets that provide clear direction for legal and financial documentation
• Building organisational capability to negotiate economic terms that create sustainable value for all partners

MODULE 07
Risk Allocation and Liability Structuring in Term Sheets
• Identifying the principal risks that should be addressed at the term sheet stage including construction, operational, market and partner-related risks
• Designing high-level risk allocation principles that assign responsibility and liability in a commercially balanced manner
• Establishing frameworks for addressing contingent liabilities, indemnities and insurance requirements at the structuring stage
• Managing the implications of different risk allocation approaches on partner willingness to proceed and on subsequent legal documentation
• Documenting agreed risk allocation principles in term sheets to reduce later negotiation friction
• Building organisational capability to structure risk allocation that protects partner interests while enabling the venture to proceed

MODULE 08
Term Sheet Development and Key Commercial Terms
• Designing comprehensive term sheet structures that capture all material commercial, governance and risk allocation agreements in clear, concise language
• Establishing processes for drafting, reviewing and iterating term sheets with internal stakeholders and prospective partners
• Managing version control, issue tracking and negotiation of outstanding points during the term sheet phase
• Integrating legal, financial and commercial perspectives into cohesive term sheet documents that serve as effective instructions for legal drafting
• Developing protocols for obtaining internal approvals and partner sign-off on term sheets before proceeding to contract phase
• Building organisational capability to produce high-quality term sheets that minimise downstream legal and commercial disputes

MODULE 09
Negotiation Strategy and Deal Dynamics Management
• Developing structured approaches to JV negotiation that balance assertive pursuit of commercial interests with relationship-building requirements
• Establishing processes for preparing negotiation positions, identifying trade-offs and managing concessions during term sheet discussions
• Managing multi-party dynamics, cultural differences and power imbalances that commonly arise in joint venture negotiations
• Developing techniques for breaking deadlocks, reframing issues and maintaining momentum towards agreed term sheets
• Integrating internal stakeholder management with external negotiation processes to maintain alignment and decision-making speed
• Building organisational capability to lead complex, multi-party negotiations that produce commercially sound and relationship-preserving outcomes

MODULE 10
Transition to Legal Documentation and Post-Term Sheet Process
• Establishing clear processes for transitioning from agreed term sheets to legal documentation phases
• Developing comprehensive briefing materials and instructions that enable legal teams to draft agreements efficiently and accurately
• Managing the interaction between structuring teams and legal counsel during the contract drafting phase to maintain commercial intent
• Identifying common areas where term sheet ambiguity creates downstream issues and developing practices to minimise such gaps
• Establishing protocols for managing changes requested during legal drafting that protect the commercial deal agreed at term sheet stage
• Building organisational capability to manage the critical handover from deal structuring to legal execution with discipline and clarity
expectedOutcomes: Participants will be able to:
High-quality term sheets for new joint ventures that clearly document equity, governance, economic and risk allocation terms ready for legal drafting
Documented partner evaluation reports and due diligence findings that support confident partner selection and structuring decisions
Structured negotiation strategies and supporting materials that enable effective management of complex multi-party JV discussions
Clear transition documentation that enables legal teams to produce accurate shareholders and joint venture agreements aligned with commercial intent
Enhanced capability to integrate digital tools and AI-assisted analysis into JV structuring processes while maintaining commercial rigour
Improved internal alignment and approval processes that accelerate term sheet development and reduce downstream friction
organisationalImpact: Higher quality joint venture opportunities reaching term sheet stage through more disciplined partner evaluation and structuring processes
Reduced time and cost in legal documentation phases through clearer, more complete term sheets that minimise ambiguity
Stronger protection of commercial interests through robust risk allocation and governance design at the earliest stage of JV formation
Improved ability to manage complex, multi-party negotiations while preserving relationships and deal momentum
Sustainable improvement in JV origination and structuring capability that increases the probability of successful, value-creating joint ventures
Enhanced organisational reputation with potential partners through professional, well-prepared structuring processes
personalImpact: Advanced practical expertise in joint venture partner evaluation, equity structuring and term sheet negotiation at a strategic level
Enhanced ability to lead complex multi-party negotiations and manage competing interests to achieve commercially balanced outcomes
Clearer professional pathway towards Head of Corporate Development, M&A Director, Deal Structuring Director and similar senior business development leadership roles
Immediately applicable skills in due diligence design, contribution valuation and term sheet development that strengthen current deal execution capability
Expanded perspective on JV structuring dynamics, negotiation strategy and transition to legal processes that support long-term career relevance
Greater personal confidence and credibility when leading JV structuring discussions, advising internal stakeholders and representing the organisation in partner negotiations

The quality of partner selection, equity design, governance principles and term sheet clarity directly determines whether a joint venture creates lasting value or becomes a source of friction and underperformance. This programme provides participants with the frameworks, negotiation discipline and structuring rigour required to originate and shape joint ventures that stand the test of time.

Enrol now in the Joint Venture Negotiation & Structuring Excellence programme to develop the partner evaluation expertise, term sheet mastery and deal leadership capability required to structure high-quality joint ventures from the very beginning.

• Integrating digital deal rooms and AI-assisted due diligence tools to improve the speed and depth of partner assessment
• Identifying red flags and material issues that should influence partner selection or term sheet positions
• Building organisational capability to conduct rigorous, efficient due diligence that supports confident structuring decisions

MODULE 04
Equity Structuring and Contribution Valuation
• Applying joint venture valuation methodology to assess the fair value of each partner’s proposed contributions to the venture
• Designing equity split structures that reflect relative contributions while creating appropriate incentives for ongoing performance
• Establishing processes for documenting and agreeing valuation assumptions and methodologies with all prospective partners
• Managing the implications of different contribution types including cash, assets, intellectual property and ongoing services
• Developing frameworks for addressing valuation disputes and reaching commercially acceptable equity arrangements
• Building organisational capability to produce defensible and mutually acceptable equity structures at the term sheet stage

MODULE 05
Governance and Decision Rights Design at Term Sheet Stage
• Designing high-level governance frameworks that define board composition, voting rights and key decision-making authorities
• Establishing the scope of reserved matters and veto rights that protect fundamental partner interests without paralysing operations
• Developing principles for balancing partner representation with the need for efficient day-to-day management of the joint venture
• Managing the implications of different governance models on control, information flow and dispute prevention
• Documenting governance principles in term sheets in sufficient detail to guide subsequent legal drafting
• Building organisational capability to design governance arrangements that support both partner protection and operational effectiveness

MODULE 06
Economic Terms and Value Sharing Mechanisms
• Designing economic terms that govern profit distribution, loss allocation and capital return mechanisms within the joint venture
• Establishing frameworks for addressing future capital requirements and the implications for ownership and control
• Developing principles for performance-based incentives, promoting structures and other mechanisms that align partner interests with venture success
• Managing the implications of different economic arrangements on partner behaviour, risk appetite and long-term alignment
• Documenting key economic principles in term sheets that provide clear direction for legal and financial documentation
• Building organisational capability to negotiate economic terms that create sustainable value for all partners

MODULE 07
Risk Allocation and Liability Structuring in Term Sheets
• Identifying the principal risks that should be addressed at the term sheet stage including construction, operational, market and partner-related risks
• Designing high-level risk allocation principles that assign responsibility and liability in a commercially balanced manner
• Establishing frameworks for addressing contingent liabilities, indemnities and insurance requirements at the structuring stage
• Managing the implications of different risk allocation approaches on partner willingness to proceed and on subsequent legal documentation
• Documenting agreed risk allocation principles in term sheets to reduce later negotiation friction
• Building organisational capability to structure risk allocation that protects partner interests while enabling the venture to proceed

MODULE 08
Term Sheet Development and Key Commercial Terms
• Designing comprehensive term sheet structures that capture all material commercial, governance and risk allocation agreements in clear, concise language
• Establishing processes for drafting, reviewing and iterating term sheets with internal stakeholders and prospective partners
• Managing version control, issue tracking and negotiation of outstanding points during the term sheet phase
• Integrating legal, financial and commercial perspectives into cohesive term sheet documents that serve as effective instructions for legal drafting
• Developing protocols for obtaining internal approvals and partner sign-off on term sheets before proceeding to contract phase
• Building organisational capability to produce high-quality term sheets that minimise downstream legal and commercial disputes

MODULE 09
Negotiation Strategy and Deal Dynamics Management
• Developing structured approaches to JV negotiation that balance assertive pursuit of commercial interests with relationship-building requirements
• Establishing processes for preparing negotiation positions, identifying trade-offs and managing concessions during term sheet discussions
• Managing multi-party dynamics, cultural differences and power imbalances that commonly arise in joint venture negotiations
• Developing techniques for breaking deadlocks, reframing issues and maintaining momentum towards agreed term sheets
• Integrating internal stakeholder management with external negotiation processes to maintain alignment and decision-making speed
• Building organisational capability to lead complex, multi-party negotiations that produce commercially sound and relationship-preserving outcomes

MODULE 10
Transition to Legal Documentation and Post-Term Sheet Process
• Establishing clear processes for transitioning from agreed term sheets to legal documentation phases
• Developing comprehensive briefing materials and instructions that enable legal teams to draft agreements efficiently and accurately
• Managing the interaction between structuring teams and legal counsel during the contract drafting phase to maintain commercial intent
• Identifying common areas where term sheet ambiguity creates downstream issues and developing practices to minimise such gaps
• Establishing protocols for managing changes requested during legal drafting that protect the commercial deal agreed at term sheet stage
• Building organisational capability to manage the critical handover from deal structuring to legal execution with discipline and clarity

courses.title: Joint Venture Performance & Exit Mastery
courses.overview: Joint venture leaders often face performance drift and exit complexities that erode value and damage partner relationships without disciplined foresight. This joint venture exit strategy training equips participants with rigorous frameworks for performance measurement, intervention planning and exit execution, including trigger protocols, valuation methodologies and dispute resolution mechanisms. This JV performance masterclass integrates continuous performance governance with proactive exit strategies to maximise value realisation across the joint venture lifecycle. This course can be facilitated in London, Dubai, Kuala Lumpur, Nairobi, and other major business centres on client-preferred dates.
whyChoose: Establish robust joint venture performance measurement frameworks and early warning systems that enable timely intervention before issues escalate into material value erosion
Develop structured exit planning processes, trigger event protocols and valuation methodologies that protect partner economic interests during transition and exit scenarios
Strengthening governance mechanisms for performance oversight, strategic review and exit decision-making that provide clarity, accountability and partner alignment
Embed proactive performance improvement methodologies and intervention strategies that address root causes, restore alignment and protect the commercial and strategic objectives of the joint venture
Design dispute resolution and exit mechanism frameworks that minimise conflict, reduce transaction costs and preserve relationships during challenging transition periods
Build organisational capability to manage the full performance-to-exit continuum with foresight, discipline and value-protecting execution across the joint venture lifecycle
audience: JV Directors and Heads of Joint Ventures accountable for strategic performance oversight, governance decisions and exit strategy approval in shared ownership entities
JV Performance Managers and Governance Managers responsible for designing, implementing and maintaining performance management systems and monitoring protocols
Commercial Managers and Partnership Managers tasked with operational performance delivery, issue resolution and preparation for lifecycle transition events
Senior JV Analysts and Valuation Specialists conducting performance reviews, financial modelling and exit economics assessment
JV Officers and Performance Coordinators supporting data management, reporting accuracy and compliance with performance and exit governance requirements
JV Performance Analysts and Exit Preparation Officers facilitating documentation, stakeholder engagement and execution of transition plans under senior direction
objectives: By the end of this programme, participants will be able to:

Design and implement comprehensive joint venture performance measurement frameworks and early warning systems that enable proactive intervention and sustained value creation across multi-party JV structures
Establish robust monitoring, reporting and governance processes that provide transparency to all partners and support timely, evidence-based decision-making throughout the venture lifecycle
Develop and apply performance improvement and intervention strategies that address root causes, restore alignment and protect the commercial and strategic objectives of the joint venture
Identify, define and operationalise trigger events and decision gates that prompt strategic reviews and proactive responses to emerging performance or partnership issues

Create exit strategy frameworks, including trigger protocols and planning roadmaps, that align partner interests and prepare the venture for orderly transition when performance or strategic conditions require
Apply exit valuation methodologies and economic settlement frameworks that accurately reflect contributions, protect partner value and minimise erosion during exit or restructuring events

Lead transition execution, post-exit integration and organisational learning processes that capture insights, protect residual value and enhance future joint venture capability
deliveryApproach: Interactive workshops exploring real-world JV performance challenges and exit case studies with emphasis on practical framework application and decision-making under pressure
Detailed analysis of performance crises, successful interventions and executed exits highlighting critical success factors, governance lessons and value outcomes
Simulation exercises requiring participants to design performance dashboards, define trigger events, model exit scenarios and negotiate transition terms under realistic partner and time constraints
Collaborative group projects developing integrated performance management systems and exit strategy plans for complex joint venture situations with structured peer review and expert facilitation

courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
Foundations of Joint Venture Performance Management
• Examining the distinctive performance dynamics that arise in jointly owned entities due to shared control, economic participation and partner interdependencies
• Defining the core principles of effective JV performance management including alignment of interests, transparency of information and proactive issue resolution
• Identifying the key performance tensions, governance gaps and behavioural challenges that commonly emerge across different JV structures and partner profiles
• Establishing the foundational requirements for sound performance practice including clear metrics, disciplined review processes and defined escalation protocols
• Recognising the influence of partner strategic priorities, organisational cultures and external market conditions on JV performance expectations and management behaviours
• Mapping the performance lifecycle of a joint venture from initial operational stabilisation through growth, maturity and eventual transition or exit

MODULE 02
Designing Performance Measurement Frameworks and Key Indicators
• Developing comprehensive performance measurement frameworks that capture financial, operational, strategic and relational dimensions relevant to all joint venture partners
• Selecting and defining key performance indicators that reflect both individual partner objectives and collective venture success criteria in balanced and measurable terms
• Establishing balanced approaches that integrate quantitative metrics with qualitative assessments of partnership health, collaboration quality and strategic progress
• Designing data collection, validation, aggregation and reporting processes that ensure accuracy, consistency, timeliness and accessibility for all stakeholders
• Integrating performance measurement with existing governance structures, board reporting cycles and strategic decision-making processes within the joint venture
• Building organisational capability to maintain, review and evolve performance frameworks as the joint venture matures and external conditions evolve

MODULE 03
Monitoring Systems, Reporting and Early Warning Mechanisms
• Establishing robust monitoring systems that track performance against agreed metrics, milestones and strategic objectives on a consistent and timely basis
• Designing reporting frameworks that provide partners with clear, relevant and actionable information without creating undue administrative burden
• Developing early warning mechanisms and threshold-based alerts that signal emerging issues before they escalate into material performance or relationship problems
• Implementing exception reporting, variance analysis and trend identification processes that focus attention on areas requiring governance intervention
• Integrating monitoring and reporting with operational management, risk oversight and strategic planning activities within the joint venture entity
• Building organisational capability to sustain disciplined, transparent monitoring that supports proactive management and partner confidence

MODULE 04
Performance Review, Analysis and Continuous Improvement
• Conducting structured performance reviews that examine results, underlying drivers and partner perspectives in a constructive and forward-looking manner
• Applying analytical techniques to identify root causes of performance shortfalls, emerging risks and opportunities for value enhancement
• Establishing continuous improvement processes that translate review findings into actionable initiatives with clear ownership, timelines and success measures
• Managing the implications of performance reviews on partner relationships, governance dynamics and strategic direction of the joint venture
• Integrating performance analysis and improvement planning into regular governance cycles and strategic planning activities
• Building organisational capability to embed a culture of performance discipline, learning and adaptive improvement across the joint venture

MODULE 05
Managing Performance Issues, Interventions and Partner Alignment
• Identifying and diagnosing performance issues at early stages through systematic analysis of metrics, behaviours and external factors
• Designing intervention strategies that address root causes while preserving partner relationships and the strategic rationale of the joint venture
• Establishing escalation protocols and governance processes for approving, implementing and monitoring performance interventions
• Managing the implications of performance challenges on partner trust, economic interests and long-term collaboration commitments
• Developing approaches for restoring alignment between partners when performance issues create divergence in priorities or expectations
• Building organisational capability to respond to performance issues with speed, professionalism and value-protecting outcomes

MODULE 06
Trigger Events, Decision Points and Strategic Lifecycle Reviews
• Defining trigger events and decision gates that prompt formal strategic reviews of joint venture performance, direction and partner alignment
• Establishing criteria and thresholds for activating strategic reviews based on performance metrics, market changes or partnership developments
• Designing governance processes for conducting lifecycle reviews that evaluate continued strategic fit, value creation potential and exit readiness
• Managing the implications of trigger events on partner behaviour, governance dynamics and decision-making timelines
• Integrating trigger-based reviews into ongoing performance management and strategic planning frameworks
• Building organisational capability to use trigger events and decision points as structured opportunities for proactive governance and value protection

MODULE 07
Exit Strategy Planning and Governance Frameworks
• Developing comprehensive exit strategy frameworks that anticipate potential transition scenarios and prepare the joint venture for orderly change
• Establishing governance structures and decision-making processes for exit planning that involve all partners in a transparent and aligned manner
• Designing exit planning roadmaps that identify key workstreams, dependencies, timelines and responsibilities for different exit scenarios
• Managing the implications of exit planning on ongoing performance, partner relationships and operational continuity of the joint venture
• Integrating exit strategy considerations into performance management, risk oversight and strategic decision-making from an early stage
• Building organisational capability to plan for exit as a disciplined, value-protecting process rather than a reactive crisis response

MODULE 08
Exit Valuation, Economic Modelling and Settlement Design
• Applying joint venture valuation methodology to assess the fair economic value of partner interests in the context of exit or restructuring scenarios
• Developing economic models that capture the full range of contributions, accumulated value, future prospects and settlement considerations
• Designing settlement frameworks that address distribution of assets, liabilities, intellectual property and ongoing obligations in a fair and enforceable manner
• Managing the implications of valuation disputes, differing partner expectations and external market conditions on exit economics and timelines
• Establishing processes for independent valuation review, negotiation of settlement terms and documentation of economic agreements
• Building organisational capability to conduct exit valuations and design settlements that protect partner value and minimise erosion during transition

MODULE 09
Dispute Resolution Mechanisms and Exit Implementation
• Designing dispute resolution and exit mechanism protocols that provide structured pathways for managing conflict during performance challenges or exit processes
• Establishing escalation procedures, mediation approaches and arbitration frameworks that resolve disputes efficiently while preserving commercial relationships where possible
• Developing implementation plans for exit mechanisms that coordinate legal, financial, operational and governance workstreams under clear leadership
• Managing the implications of disputes and exit implementation on partner trust, venture reputation and residual value
• Integrating dispute resolution and exit mechanisms into broader governance frameworks and performance management processes
• Building organisational capability to execute exit strategies professionally, minimise value destruction and protect long-term interests of all parties

MODULE 10
Transition Management, Post-Exit Review and Capability Building
• Leading transition execution processes that manage the operational, financial, legal and human dimensions of exit or restructuring with discipline and care
• Establishing post-exit review processes that capture lessons learned, assess value outcomes and identify improvements for future joint venture activity
• Developing knowledge transfer, documentation and organisational learning mechanisms that retain institutional memory from joint venture experience
• Managing the implications of transition on ongoing partner relationships, reputation and future collaboration opportunities
• Integrating transition management and post-exit review into the joint venture's governance and performance management culture
• Building organisational capability to treat exit as a strategic lifecycle event that generates lasting value and enhances future joint venture performance
expectedOutcomes: Participants will be able to:
Comprehensive joint venture performance dashboards, early warning systems and trigger protocols ready for immediate implementation with clear governance ownership
Documented exit strategy frameworks, valuation models and economic settlement approaches that protect partner value and support orderly transition execution
Enhanced capability to diagnose performance issues, design interventions and manage partner alignment through structured, evidence-based processes
Robust dispute resolution and exit mechanism protocols that reduce conflict costs, preserve relationships and minimise value erosion during challenging periods
Clear strategic narrative and communication framework for engaging partners, boards and stakeholders on performance status, trigger decisions and exit planning
Practical preparation for lifecycle events including performance reviews, trigger activations and exit scenarios that protect shared enterprise value and organisational reputation
organisationalImpact: Improved joint venture value protection through disciplined performance management, early intervention and proactive exit planning that prevents value erosion
Stronger partner confidence and relationship stability arising from transparent performance governance, fair processes and professional exit execution
Reduced financial, operational and reputational costs associated with unmanaged performance decline or poorly executed exits and transitions
Enhanced organisational capability to manage the full JV lifecycle with foresight, reducing the probability of value-destroying outcomes
Sustainable improvement in JV performance oversight and exit readiness that increases the overall success rate of shared ownership initiatives
Increased stakeholder and partner trust through demonstrable commitment to performance excellence, fair treatment and value protection across the venture lifecycle
personalImpact: Advanced practical expertise in joint venture performance management, trigger design, exit valuation and transition leadership at a strategic level
Enhanced ability to influence JV board decisions, manage performance interventions and lead exit processes that protect partner interests and organisational value
Clearer professional pathway towards JV Director, Head of Joint Ventures, Performance Governance Director and similar senior JV leadership roles
Immediately applicable skills in designing performance frameworks, implementing early warning systems and preparing exit strategies that strengthen current JV responsibilities
Expanded perspective on dispute-exit mechanisms, post-transition learning and lifecycle value protection that supports long-term career relevance in complex partnership environments
Greater personal confidence and credibility when advising on JV performance challenges, recommending trigger actions and leading exit negotiations with partners and stakeholders
General Notes
Sector customisation available on request
Training material provided
Elevoris Certificate of Training issued to all participants
Optional post-programme advisory coaching available

Effective performance management and well-structured exits determine whether joint ventures deliver sustained value or become prolonged sources of friction, conflict and value destruction. Mastering both dimensions requires integrated frameworks, disciplined governance and the foresight to treat exit as a strategic lifecycle event rather than a reactive crisis. This programme provides participants with the methodologies, practical tools and leadership capability to optimise joint venture performance and execute exits that protect partner capital and strategic interests with professionalism and confidence.

Enrol now in the Joint Venture Performance & Exit Mastery programme to develop the performance oversight expertise, exit strategy capability and transition leadership skills required to maximise value and minimise risk across the complete joint venture lifecycle.

courses.title: Lean Supply Chain & Process Improvement
courses.overview: Supply chains frequently suffer from excessive waste, fragmented processes, long lead times and hidden inefficiencies that inflate costs, erode service levels and heighten vulnerability to disruption. This lean supply chain training programme equips practitioners with systematic frameworks and practical tools to identify, eliminate and prevent non-value-adding activities while building sustainable cultures of continuous improvement. Participants develop applied skills in value stream analysis, structured problem-solving and process optimisation that deliver measurable gains in flow, quality and responsiveness across procurement, operations and logistics. The supply chain process improvement emphasis enables organisations to create more agile, resilient and cost-effective end-to-end processes. This course can be facilitated in London, Dubai, Kuala Lumpur, Nairobi, and other major business centres on client-preferred dates.
whyChoose: Master lean principles and waste-elimination methodologies specifically adapted to complex, multi-tier supply chain environments to drive systematic efficiency and value creation
Develop advanced capabilities in value stream mapping, process analysis and structured continuous improvement that deliver quantifiable reductions in lead time, inventory, cost and defects
Learn to apply lean tools and thinking across procurement, inventory, warehousing, logistics and supplier interfaces for integrated end-to-end optimisation
Strengthening the integration of lean practices with risk management, quality systems, sustainability and resilience building to protect performance under uncertainty
Acquiring proven change leadership and cultural transformation approaches that embed continuous improvement behaviours and sustain gains across organisational boundaries
Position your organisation to achieve higher operational excellence, lower total cost of ownership and enhanced competitive advantage through disciplined, data-informed lean supply chain practices
audience: Supply Chain Directors and Heads of Operations responsible for end-to-end process performance and efficiency
Lean Practitioners, Continuous Improvement Managers and Process Excellence Leads driving operational transformation
Procurement and Sourcing Managers seeking to embed lean principles into upstream supply chain activities
Logistics, Warehouse and Distribution Managers optimising flow, inventory and fulfilment processes
Operations Directors and Manufacturing Leads accountable for production-to-delivery performance and waste reduction
Quality, Risk and Compliance Managers integrating lean methodologies with governance, safety and resilience frameworks
objectives: By the end of this programme, participants will be able to:
Apply lean principles and value stream mapping techniques to diagnose waste, bottlenecks and non-value-adding activities across complex, multi-tier supply chain processes
Design and implement structured process improvement initiatives using root cause analysis, standardisation and visual management approaches that deliver measurable efficiency and quality gains
Integrate lean methodologies into procurement, supplier management and sourcing processes to reduce lead times, total costs and supply risks while enhancing value creation and collaboration
Optimise inventory, warehousing and logistics operations through lean flow principles, pull systems and demand-driven planning that minimise waste and improve service reliability

Strategic Context and Value of Lean Thinking in Supply Chains

• Developing targeted countermeasures and improvement actions for each waste type using lean problem-solving methodologies

• Embedding waste elimination thinking into daily operations, performance reviews and supplier collaboration processes

MODULE 03

• Identifying value-adding versus non-value-adding activities and quantifying lead time, process time and value-added ratios
• Developing future-state value stream maps that eliminate waste, improve flow and align processes with customer demand and strategic goals
• Applying root cause analysis and structured problem-solving techniques to address bottlenecks, delays and quality issues revealed by mapping
• Engaging cross-functional and supplier teams in collaborative mapping and improvement workshops to build shared understanding and ownership
• Using value stream insights to prioritise improvement projects, resource allocation and performance monitoring activities

MODULE 04
