• Designing and facilitating kaizen events and rapid improvement workshops that deliver focused, time-bound process enhancements
• Establishing standardised work processes, procedures and visual controls that reduce variation and enable consistent high performance
• Using structured problem-solving cycles to address recurring issues, defects and inefficiencies with data-driven rigour
• Integrating lean tools with existing quality management and continuous improvement systems for synergistic effect
• Building internal capability to select, adapt and sustain appropriate lean tools across different supply chain functions and contexts

MODULE 05
Applying Lean Principles in Procurement, Sourcing and Supplier Management
• Mapping procurement and sourcing processes to identify waste in specification development, tendering, negotiation, ordering and supplier interaction
• Applying lean thinking to reduce lead times, transaction costs and administrative burden while improving supplier collaboration and value creation
• Developing pull-based replenishment and supplier integration approaches that minimise inventory waste and improve responsiveness
• Establishing performance frameworks and continuous improvement mechanisms with key suppliers that align incentives and drive mutual gains
• Integrating lean criteria into supplier selection, evaluation and development processes to build more efficient and resilient supply bases
• Managing the interface between internal lean initiatives and supplier operations to prevent sub-optimisation and maximise end-to-end value

MODULE 06
Lean in Inventory, Warehousing and Logistics Operations
• Applying lean flow principles, pull systems and demand-driven planning to optimise inventory levels and reduce carrying costs and obsolescence
• Designing warehouse layouts, picking processes and material handling systems that minimise motion, waiting and transport waste
• Implementing visual management, standardised work and continuous improvement practices in warehousing and distribution operations
• Optimising logistics and distribution networks for flow efficiency, load consolidation and reduced empty running or backhauls
• Integrating lean inventory and logistics practices with production scheduling, customer fulfilment and returns processes
• Establishing performance metrics and review mechanisms that drive ongoing waste reduction and service improvement in physical operations

MODULE 07
Integrating Lean with Quality, Risk Management and Supply Chain Resilience
• Embedding lean practices within broader quality management systems to reduce defects, rework and variability across the supply chain
• Identifying and mitigating operational and supply risks through lean-informed process design, standardisation and visual control mechanisms
• Building resilience by creating flow, reducing inventory buffers strategically and developing flexible response capabilities to disruption
• Applying lean problem-solving and root cause analysis to quality failures, delivery issues and risk events for sustainable prevention
• Aligning lean initiatives with sustainability objectives to reduce waste, resource consumption and environmental impact simultaneously
• Developing integrated governance and assurance approaches that maintain lean discipline while managing emerging risks and uncertainties

MODULE 08
Data-Driven Decision Making and Digital Enablers for Lean Supply Chains
• Establishing data requirements, collection processes and performance dashboards that support lean visibility and decision-making
• Applying analytics to identify waste patterns, predict process deviations and prioritise high-impact improvement opportunities
• Evaluating and integrating digital tools and platforms that enhance real-time monitoring, visual management and collaborative improvement
• Using data to validate improvement hypotheses, measure benefits and sustain gains through evidence-based management
• Addressing data quality, integration and governance challenges that can limit the effectiveness of lean digital initiatives
• Building organisational capability to interpret lean-relevant data and translate insights into targeted process interventions

MODULE 09
Leading Lean Transformation, Change and Cultural Embedding
• Diagnosing organisational readiness and cultural barriers to lean adoption across supply chain functions and partner organisations
• Designing and executing comprehensive change management and communication strategies that build understanding, ownership and commitment
• Developing targeted capability-building programmes, coaching and on-the-job support to close lean skills gaps at all levels
• Identifying and empowering lean champions and improvement facilitators within teams and across the extended supply chain
• Measuring adoption, behavioural change and cultural shifts to inform ongoing reinforcement and adjustment of transformation efforts
• Embedding lean thinking into standard operating procedures, performance expectations, recognition systems and leadership behaviours for sustainability

MODULE 10
Performance Measurement, Benefits Realisation and Sustaining Lean Excellence
• Designing integrated performance frameworks that connect lean process metrics to strategic objectives, cost outcomes and customer value
• Selecting and implementing meaningful KPIs for waste reduction, flow improvement, quality, cost and service across the supply chain
• Establishing review cadences, audit processes and continuous improvement governance that maintains momentum and prevent regression
• Conducting structured benefits tracking and realisation reviews to demonstrate financial and operational returns from lean initiatives
• Capturing lessons learned, codifying successful practices and scaling proven improvements across the organisation and supply network
• Developing long-term roadmaps for advancing lean maturity, building internal expertise and sustaining competitive advantage through continuous improvement

courses.title: LNG Business & Commercial Strategy Masterclass
courses.overview: In a rapidly expanding global LNG market shaped by shifting supply dynamics, evolving buyer requirements and intensifying competition, many energy professionals and commercial leaders lack the integrated strategic and commercial capability required to capture value, manage complex contractual arrangements and position organisations effectively across the full LNG value chain. This LNG training masterclass delivers a rigorous, practitioner-intensive development experience focused on advanced commercial strategy, contract structuring, pricing and risk management, and partnership leadership specific to LNG. Participants master frameworks to optimise offtake arrangements, navigate price volatility and build sustainable competitive positions in both traditional and emerging LNG markets. The LNG business commercial strategy masterclass combines deep commercial insight with extensive live application, ensuring leaders return with immediately usable tools and a transformed approach to LNG business leadership. This course can be facilitated in London, Dubai, Kuala Lumpur, Nairobi, and other major business centres on client-preferred dates.
whyChoose: Avoid the substantial hidden value leakage that occurs when LNG offtake agreements, shipping arrangements and pricing mechanisms are structured without full understanding of long-term market, volume and flexibility implications

Prevent the strategic disadvantage created when organisations fail to anticipate shifts in global LNG trade flows, buyer preferences and competitive positioning, resulting in lost market share or suboptimal portfolio outcomes

Reduce the commercial and financial exposure arising from poorly negotiated contracts, inadequate risk allocation and weak management provisions that only surface during periods of price volatility or operational disruption

Eliminate the organisational cost of fragmented commercial approaches across liquefaction, shipping and regasification that prevent capture of integration synergies and portfolio optimisation opportunities

Close the critical capability gap that leaves even technically strong LNG teams unable to translate operational excellence into sustainable commercial advantage and strategic influence with buyers, partners and host governments

Overcome the personal and career limitation of remaining a functional LNG specialist without developing the integrated commercial strategy, negotiation mastery and stakeholder leadership skills required for senior LNG business roles
audience: Vice President LNG Commercial and Director of Gas & LNG Strategy accountable for enterprise LNG portfolio strategy, major offtake agreements and market positioning
General Manager – LNG Business Development and Head of LNG Trading responsible for growth strategy, contract origination and trading optimisation across LNG assets
LNG Commercial Manager and Gas Contracts Lead managing day-to-day commercial operations, contract performance and renegotiation of high-value LNG arrangements
Business Development Manager – LNG and LNG Trading Manager leading opportunity origination, deal structuring and portfolio risk management
Senior LNG Analyst and Commercial Coordinator – Gas & LNG providing analytical support, contract administration and commercial intelligence for LNG business units
LNG Business Analyst and Gas Marketing Executive developing foundational commercial strategy and contract management capability for progression into LNG leadership roles
objectives: By the end of this masterclass, participants will be able to:

Design and execute integrated LNG commercial strategies that maximise value across liquefaction, shipping, regasification and trading segments while aligning with corporate portfolio objectives and energy transition pathways

Structure, negotiate and administer complex LNG offtake agreements, master sale and purchase agreements and shipping contracts that protect flexibility, manage volume risk and optimise long-term commercial outcomes
Develop robust LNG pricing, hedging and risk management frameworks that navigate international crude oil benchmark pricing dynamics, spot market exposure and basis risk across global LNG portfolios
Lead LNG project development, investment appraisal and capital allocation decisions that balance technical, commercial, regulatory and ESG considerations to deliver superior risk-adjusted returns
Establish and manage high-value joint ventures, strategic partnerships and stakeholder relationships that secure access, align interests and sustain collaborative advantage in competitive LNG markets
Apply advanced negotiation, dispute prevention and commercial conflict resolution techniques that protect organisational interests while preserving critical buyer and partner relationships
Integrate ESG, carbon management and sustainability requirements into LNG commercial strategy, contract design and stakeholder engagement to maintain social licence and access to capital
Demonstrate LNG business and commercial strategy excellence through live case applications and apply learning to strengthen both current LNG operations and future strategic positioning
deliveryApproach: Intensive masterclass format combining expert facilitation with extensive hands-on workshops, commercial case study analysis and live negotiation simulations using authentic LNG market and contractual scenarios
Collaborative development of LNG commercial strategies, offtake structures and risk management frameworks with immediate structured feedback from facilitators and peer commercial leaders
High-fidelity negotiation role-plays and contract review exercises where participants practise structuring, pricing and dispute resolution in realistic LNG buyer and partner contexts
Personal LNG portfolio audits and strategic planning sessions where delegates apply new frameworks directly to live commercial challenges from their own organisations
Facilitated exploration of global LNG trade dynamics, pricing mechanisms and energy transition impacts through group scenario planning and strategic dialogue
Comprehensive participant materials, commercial templates, pricing models, governance checklists and post-masterclass application resources provided for immediate workplace use
courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
The Global LNG Market Landscape and Strategic Commercial Context
• Analysing current and emerging global LNG supply, demand, trade flow and competitive dynamics that shape strategic and commercial decision-making
• Identifying the implications of shifting buyer preferences, portfolio diversification strategies and new market entrants for existing and future LNG positions
• Understanding the commercial impact of energy transition policies, decarbonisation requirements and evolving end-use demand on LNG market positioning
• Assessing the strategic roles of traditional LNG exporters, emerging suppliers and major importing markets in a changing global gas trade environment
• Recognising the management-level opportunities and risks created by spot market growth, portfolio trading and flexible contract structures
• Establishing clear personal and organisational objectives for the masterclass aligned with current LNG commercial challenges and strategic priorities

MODULE 02
LNG Value Chain Integration and Business Model Optimisation
• Mapping the full LNG value chain from upstream supply through liquefaction, shipping and regasification to identify integration opportunities and value leakage points
• Developing approaches to optimise commercial interfaces and capture synergies across liquefaction, shipping and regasification assets within a single portfolio
• Building capability to design and evaluate integrated LNG business models that balance long-term contracted volumes with flexible and spot market exposure
• Managing supply chain resilience, shipping optimisation and regasification capacity strategies at a commercial portfolio level
• Establishing performance metrics and governance mechanisms that align value chain activities with overall LNG business objectives
• Creating practical frameworks for identifying and executing value-creating integration and optimisation opportunities in existing LNG portfolios

MODULE 03
Structuring LNG Offtake Agreements and Master Commercial Contracts
• Applying structured approaches to designing, negotiating and documenting LNG offtake agreements, master sale and purchase agreements and related commercial contracts
• Developing skills in allocating volume, price, destination and flexibility risks through clear contractual mechanisms that protect long-term value
• Building capability to manage contract lifecycle processes including nominations, scheduling, quality specifications and payment mechanisms
• Establishing robust change management, amendment and dispute resolution provisions that minimise future commercial friction
• Managing the interface between long-term contracted positions and shorter-term or spot market opportunities within a coherent portfolio strategy
• Creating practical standards for contract drafting, review and administration that reduce ambiguity and protect organisational commercial interests

MODULE 04
LNG Pricing Mechanisms, Hedging and Price Risk Management
• Understanding the structure and dynamics of LNG pricing mechanisms including oil-linked, gas-linked, hybrid and spot-based formulations across global markets
• Developing advanced techniques for identifying, measuring and managing price, volume and basis risk exposures across LNG portfolios
• Building capability to design and implement hedging and risk mitigation strategies that protect margins while preserving commercial upside
• Managing the interface between physical LNG operations, trading activities and financial risk management functions
• Establishing governance frameworks, trading controls and compliance processes appropriate for LNG price risk participation
• Creating practical approaches to scenario planning and stress testing that prepare organisations for sustained price volatility and structural market shifts

MODULE 05
LNG Project Development, Investment Appraisal and Capital Decisions
• Applying structured investment appraisal frameworks to LNG liquefaction, shipping, regasification and infrastructure projects that incorporate commercial, regulatory and ESG factors
• Developing capability to evaluate and prioritise capital investments, capacity expansions and new market entries at portfolio and enterprise level
• Building skills in managing stage-gate processes, risk allocation and commercial structuring for greenfield and brownfield LNG developments
• Balancing the competing demands of long-term contracted cash flows, spot market exposure and energy transition investment requirements
• Establishing governance and approval processes that improve the quality and consistency of LNG investment decisions
• Creating approaches to maintain capital discipline while preserving strategic flexibility in competitive and capital-intensive LNG environments

MODULE 06
Joint Ventures, Partnerships and Stakeholder Management in LNG
• Applying structured approaches to LNG joint venture formation, governance design and partner selection that protect organisational interests while enabling effective collaboration
• Developing skills in managing joint venture operations, decision-making processes and commercial alignment in complex multi-party LNG projects
• Building capability to align partner objectives, manage cultural and strategic differences and maintain productive relationships over the life of LNG ventures
• Leading stakeholder engagement with host governments, regulators, buyers and communities that secures and sustains social licence for LNG operations
• Managing the commercial and strategic implications of farm-ins, farm-outs, capacity trades and partnership restructurings within LNG portfolios
• Creating practical frameworks for building and sustaining high-value commercial relationships that support long-term LNG business objectives

MODULE 07
LNG Trading, Portfolio Optimisation and Commercial Agility
• Developing structured approaches to LNG portfolio optimisation that balance long-term contracted positions with flexible and spot market opportunities
• Building capability to identify, evaluate and execute trading, arbitrage and optimisation strategies across global LNG markets
• Managing the interface between physical operations, commercial trading and logistics to maximise portfolio value while maintaining operational reliability
• Establishing governance frameworks, risk limits and compliance processes appropriate for active LNG trading and optimisation activities
• Creating practical approaches to real-time commercial decision-making and portfolio rebalancing in response to changing market conditions
• Building organisational capability to capture value from short-term market movements while protecting long-term strategic positioning

MODULE 08
Regulatory, ESG and Sustainability Integration in LNG Commercial Strategy
• Establishing robust approaches to regulatory compliance, permitting and stakeholder expectations that support reliable LNG operations and market access
• Developing capability to integrate ESG considerations, carbon management and sustainability requirements into LNG commercial strategy, contract design and investment decisions
• Building skills in managing reputational risk, social licence and stakeholder scrutiny in increasingly transparent and regulated LNG environments
• Managing the commercial implications of emissions reduction targets, methane management and decarbonisation pathways for existing and new LNG assets
• Establishing governance and reporting mechanisms that provide clear visibility of regulatory and ESG performance to senior leadership and external stakeholders
• Creating practical frameworks for turning sustainability requirements into sources of competitive advantage and access to premium markets and capital

This AI leadership training equips executives with integrated frameworks to harness AI capabilities strategically while preserving human judgement, ethical standards and organisational coherence. Participants develop practical capabilities in applying AI-enhanced insight to foresight and decision-making, leading responsible transformation and building teams that collaborate effectively with intelligent systems. The leading in the age of AI course emphasis enables leaders to navigate the human-machine interface with strategic clarity, governance discipline and adaptive confidence. This course can be facilitated in London, Dubai, Kuala Lumpur, Nairobi, and other major business centres on client-preferred dates.

courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
Strategic Context and Imperatives for AI in Executive Leadership
• Examining how artificial intelligence is reshaping competitive dynamics, decision-making horizons and organisational operating models across sectors
• Identifying strategic opportunities and risks arising from AI adoption including efficiency gains, insight enhancement and potential disruption to existing advantages
• Recognising the leader’s evolving role in setting direction, governance and cultural tone for responsible AI integration
• Mapping the interplay between AI capabilities, human judgement and organisational strategy in complex environments
• Establishing clear strategic objectives and success criteria for AI initiatives aligned with broader organisational purpose and risk appetite
• Conducting organisational assessments to diagnose current AI maturity, capability gaps and readiness for strategic adoption

MODULE 02
AI-Enhanced Decision-Making, Foresight and Strategic Analysis
• Applying AI-driven analytics and modelling techniques to improve the quality, speed and breadth of strategic analysis and scenario planning
• Integrating machine learning outputs with human judgement to strengthen foresight and early identification of emerging opportunities and threats
• Establishing decision frameworks that combine data-driven insight with ethical considerations, stakeholder impact and long-term consequences
• Managing cognitive biases and over-reliance on algorithmic recommendations in high-stakes leadership decisions
• Building organisational capacity for distributed, evidence-based decision-making supported by AI tools while maintaining accountability
• Embedding continuous learning from AI outcomes into strategic review and adaptation processes

MODULE 03
Human-AI Collaboration, Team Dynamics and Augmented Leadership
• Designing team structures, roles and workflows that optimise collaboration between humans and AI systems while preserving human oversight and creativity
• Developing leadership practices that foster psychological safety, trust and constructive challenge in environments where AI augments decision-making
• Managing the impact of AI on team dynamics, skill requirements and role evolution to maintain engagement and performance
• Establishing protocols for human review, intervention and accountability when AI systems generate recommendations or automate processes
• Building team capability to interpret, challenge and effectively utilise AI outputs in operational and strategic contexts
• Measuring and improving the effectiveness of human-AI collaboration on team outcomes, innovation and decision quality

MODULE 04
Ethical Governance, Risk Management and Responsible AI Leadership
• Identifying the full spectrum of ethical, reputational, regulatory and operational risks associated with AI adoption and deployment
• Establishing governance frameworks, oversight mechanisms and decision rights that ensure responsible, transparent and accountable AI use
• Developing policies and controls for data privacy, algorithmic bias, explainability and fairness in AI applications
• Managing the interface between AI-driven automation and human ethical judgement in sensitive or high-impact decisions
• Integrating AI risk considerations into broader enterprise risk management, compliance and stakeholder reporting processes
• Building organisational culture and leadership behaviours that prioritise ethical responsibility alongside innovation and performance

MODULE 05
Leading AI-Driven Organisational Transformation
• Diagnosing organisational readiness for AI-enabled transformation and identifying cultural, structural and capability barriers
• Designing change leadership approaches that combine strategic direction with iterative learning, stakeholder engagement and sustainable adoption
• Communicating AI transformation in ways that build understanding, address concerns and mobilise commitment across the organisation
• Managing the human dimensions of AI adoption including workforce transition, skill development and role redesign
• Establishing governance, measurement and reinforcement mechanisms that sustain transformation momentum and prevent regression
• Evaluating the organisational impact of AI initiatives on performance, culture and strategic positioning

MODULE 06
Building AI-Capable Talent, Skills and Organisational Capability
• Identifying current and future skill requirements for effective human-AI collaboration and AI-enabled leadership across functions
• Developing talent strategies, learning programmes and development pathways that build AI literacy and capability at multiple organisational levels
• Establishing coaching, mentoring and knowledge-sharing practices that accelerate organisational learning about AI applications and implications
• Aligning recruitment, performance management and reward systems with the evolving demands of AI-augmented work
• Building internal centres of expertise, communities of practice and external partnerships to sustain AI capability development
• Measuring the impact of capability-building initiatives on AI adoption success and organisational performance

MODULE 07
Data Strategy, Analytics and Insight Leadership in AI Environments
• Establishing robust data governance, quality and accessibility frameworks that enable effective and responsible AI applications
• Developing data strategies that align information assets with strategic priorities and AI use cases across the organisation
• Leveraging advanced analytics and AI-generated insight to enhance strategic planning, operational decision-making and performance monitoring
• Managing the ethical, privacy and security implications of large-scale data use in AI systems
• Building organisational capability to interpret, challenge and act on AI-derived insights while maintaining human accountability
• Integrating data and analytics leadership into broader strategic governance and performance management processes

MODULE 08
Change Leadership, Culture and Behavioural Adaptation for AI Adoption
• Diagnosing cultural and behavioural factors that enable or constrain successful AI integration and organisational adaptation
• Designing leadership interventions that address resistance, build trust and foster a culture of responsible experimentation and learning
• Communicating AI-related changes in ways that create meaning, reduce anxiety and sustain engagement across diverse stakeholder groups
• Managing the emotional and practical transitions required as roles, processes and decision-making evolve with AI capabilities
• Embedding new behaviours, norms and practices into organisational routines, performance systems and leadership modelling
• Sustaining cultural and behavioural change through governance, recognition and continuous reinforcement mechanisms

MODULE 09
Personal Leadership Agility, Mindset and Reflective Practice in the AI Era
• Developing personal disciplines for continuous learning, critical evaluation of AI outputs and adaptation to technological change
• Building emotional regulation, presence and influence skills that support effective leadership when AI augments or challenges human decision-making
• Managing personal energy, priorities and boundaries to sustain effectiveness amid rapid technological and organisational change
• Cultivating reflective practice habits that enable recognition of personal biases, assumptions and impact in AI-influenced contexts
• Developing authentic leadership approaches that model transparency, ethical responsibility and learning orientation expected of others
• Creating personal development plans that integrate ongoing feedback, deliberate practice and capability growth in AI-era leadership

MODULE 10
Future-Proofing Leadership and Sustaining Strategic Advantage in AI Environments
• Anticipating emerging AI developments, capabilities and implications that will shape future organisational and leadership requirements
• Developing strategies to evaluate, pilot and scale new AI applications in alignment with strategic priorities, risk appetite and organisational values
• Positioning AI leadership as a core organisational capability that supports sustained competitiveness, resilience and value creation
• Integrating AI considerations into long-term strategy, talent planning, governance and cultural development
• Building organisational agility to adapt AI strategies and practices in response to technological, regulatory and market evolution
• Creating actionable roadmaps for sustaining and extending AI leadership advantage aligned with organisational purpose and long-term success

courses.title: Meeting Management, Minute-Taking & Event Coordination Masterclass
courses.overview: Organisations across sectors lose substantial productive time through unstructured meetings, incomplete documentation and poorly coordinated events, leading to unclear decisions, weak accountability and missed opportunities. This meeting management training delivers practical, practitioner-focused methodologies to transform how meetings are planned, facilitated and documented. Participants develop advanced minute-taking capabilities and event coordination skills that support better governance and stakeholder outcomes. The minute-taking event coordination masterclass provides extensive hands-on practice with realistic scenarios and ready-to-use templates. This course can be facilitated in London, Dubai, Kuala Lumpur, Nairobi, and other major business centres on client-preferred dates.
whyChoose: Design and run focused, outcome-driven meetings that reduce wasted time and produce clearer decisions with stronger accountability
Master professional minute-taking techniques that create accurate, concise and actionable records supporting governance and compliance
Build robust event coordination capabilities that deliver seamless logistics, stakeholder engagement and successful outcomes
Strengthen follow-up systems that ensure actions are tracked, completed and reported, closing the loop on every commitment
Adapt meeting and event practices confidently for virtual, hybrid and in-person environments while maintaining quality and inclusivity
Establish organisational standards and continuous improvement approaches that raise the overall effectiveness of meetings and events
audience: Head of Administration responsible for strategic oversight of organisational meeting and event governance
Office Manager accountable for operational meeting standards, coordination and administrative efficiency
Senior Secretary and Senior Administrator managing high-level meeting documentation and executive support
Administrative Team Leader or Office Coordinator overseeing meeting logistics, scheduling and team coordination
Personal Assistant to Senior Management handling complex diary management, meeting preparation and stakeholder liaison
Secretary or Administrative Assistant producing meeting documentation and supporting day-to-day coordination activities
objectives: By the end of this masterclass, participants will be able to:
Design and implement meeting management frameworks and minute-taking standards that improve organisational decision-making efficiency, accountability and governance
Establish robust event coordination and follow-up systems that enhance stakeholder engagement and ensure timely delivery of agreed actions
Apply structured planning and facilitation techniques that keep meetings focused, inclusive and productive across different formats
Produce clear, accurate and professionally formatted minutes that capture decisions, actions and context effectively
Manage virtual, hybrid and in-person meetings with equal confidence, ensuring participation, technical coordination and documentation quality
Develop practical event planning, logistics and risk management approaches that deliver successful outcomes within constraints
Implement systematic action tracking and reporting processes that drive accountability and demonstrate the value of well-managed meetings
Build team and organisational capability in meeting excellence through standards, coaching and continuous improvement practices
deliveryApproach: Interactive workshop methodology combining expert input with extensive practical exercises in meeting planning, facilitation and minute-taking
Hands-on development of agendas, minutes, action trackers, event plans and coordination checklists using participants’ real workplace examples
Collaborative group activities to design, critique and refine meeting frameworks and event coordination approaches for different contexts
Detailed review of effective and ineffective meeting practices to extract transferable techniques and common pitfalls to avoid
Personal meeting audit and improvement planning exercises focused on immediate workplace application and measurable results
Provision of ready-to-use templates, style guides, checklists and digital resources for post-course implementation and sustained improvement
courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
Foundations of Effective Meeting Management
• Examining the strategic role of well-managed meetings in supporting organisational decision-making, accountability and productivity
• Identifying common challenges including unclear purpose, poor preparation, weak facilitation and inadequate follow-up
• Understanding core principles of purpose-driven meetings: clarity, focus, participation, documentation and action
• Recognising the direct impact of meeting quality on organisational time, resources and outcomes
• Assessing current meeting practices within participants’ organisations to establish baseline performance and priorities
• Setting clear personal and team objectives for improvement aligned with organisational needs

MODULE 02
Planning and Preparing for Successful Meetings
• Defining clear objectives, desired outcomes and required participants for every meeting type
• Developing structured, focused agendas that guide discussion and drive decision-making
• Preparing briefing materials, papers and supporting information to enable informed participation
• Managing logistics, timing, venue or virtual setup and resource requirements effectively
• Anticipating potential challenges and building contingency into meeting plans
• Creating personal and team planning checklists that support consistent, high-quality preparation

MODULE 03
Facilitation Skills and Chairing Techniques
• Applying facilitation techniques that encourage constructive participation while managing group dynamics
• Keeping meetings focused, on time and productive while allowing sufficient discussion of key issues
• Handling difficult participants, off-topic contributions and conflicts with professionalism and diplomacy
• Building consensus, clarifying decisions and summarising outcomes clearly during meetings
• Adapting facilitation approach for different meeting formats, sizes and purposes
• Developing personal facilitation confidence, presence and impact in meetings

MODULE 04
Professional Minute-Taking and Documentation
• Understanding the organisational and governance significance of accurate, reliable minutes
• Applying structured approaches to capturing discussions, decisions and actions in real time
• Distinguishing clearly between discussion points, formal decisions, action items and matters for information
• Producing concise, objective, professionally formatted minutes suitable for different audiences and purposes
• Managing minute-taking for formal, informal, action-focused and confidential meetings
• Establishing quality standards, review processes and templates for consistent meeting documentation

MODULE 05
Managing Virtual, Hybrid and In-Person Meetings
• Adapting meeting management and facilitation practices for virtual, hybrid and physical environments
• Establishing protocols for engagement, participation and technical management in digital settings
• Managing time zones, connectivity challenges and digital fatigue while maintaining meeting effectiveness
• Ensuring inclusivity, equal voice and accessibility regardless of attendance mode
• Handling recording, documentation and follow-up in hybrid contexts with consistency
• Developing good practice guidelines for modern, flexible meeting environments

MODULE 06
Event Coordination and Logistics Management
• Planning and coordinating internal and external events from initial concept through to successful delivery
• Managing detailed logistics including scheduling, resources, venues and stakeholder requirements
• Developing comprehensive event timelines, checklists, risk assessments and contingency plans
• Coordinating participants, speakers, vendors and support teams with clarity and professionalism
• Ensuring compliance, safety, accessibility and professional standards throughout event delivery
• Evaluating event outcomes and capturing lessons to improve future coordination and planning

MODULE 07
Stakeholder Communication and Engagement in Meetings
• Identifying stakeholder needs, expectations and communication requirements for different meeting types
• Preparing clear pre-meeting communications that set expectations and enable preparation
• Managing communication during meetings, participation and information flow effectively
• Handling sensitive discussions, confidential matters and diverse stakeholder perspectives with diplomacy
• Producing timely, clear post-meeting communications that reinforce decisions and actions
• Establishing feedback mechanisms that capture stakeholder experience and drive improvement

MODULE 08
Follow-up, Action Tracking and Accountability
• Establishing robust systems for capturing, assigning and tracking action items from every meeting
• Developing clear, specific action point formats that specify responsibility, deadlines and required outcomes
• Monitoring progress, following up constructively on commitments and addressing delays
• Reporting on action completion and outcomes to maintain momentum and demonstrate value
• Integrating meeting outcomes into broader organisational planning, reporting and performance processes
• Creating sustainable personal and team habits that close the loop on decisions and commitments

MODULE 09
Technology and Tools for Modern Meeting and Event Coordination
• Identifying appropriate digital tools that enhance meeting efficiency, documentation and action tracking
• Applying technology to support agenda distribution, minute capture, collaborative working and event management
• Managing data security, confidentiality and appropriate use when working with digital meeting platforms
• Balancing technological support with essential human facilitation and relationship-building elements
• Evaluating new tools and approaches to improve meeting and event processes sustainably
• Establishing team standards, training and good practice for effective technology use in coordination roles

MODULE 10
Building a Culture of Effective Meetings and Continuous Improvement
• Developing organisational standards, templates and guidelines that support consistent meeting excellence
• Coaching and supporting colleagues to improve meeting preparation, participation and documentation skills
• Measuring meeting and event effectiveness through relevant indicators, feedback and outcome tracking
• Implementing continuous improvement cycles that raise quality, reduce waste and increase impact over time
• Advocating on cultural change that values preparation, focus, accountability and respect for participants’ time
• Positioning meeting management and event coordination as strategic administrative capabilities that drive organisational performance
expectedOutcomes: Participants will be able to:
Plan, facilitate and document meetings that produce clearer decisions, stronger accountability and measurable outcomes
Produce accurate, professional minutes and records that support governance, compliance and effective follow-up
Coordinate events and meetings across virtual, hybrid and in-person formats with confidence and consistency
Implement robust action tracking systems that ensure commitments are delivered and progress is visible
Reduce time wasted in unproductive meetings while improving stakeholder engagement and satisfaction
Establish personal and team standards that raise the overall quality and impact of meetings and events
organisationalImpact: Significant reduction in time and cost lost to unproductive or poorly documented meetings
Improved decision quality, accountability and speed of execution across teams and functions
Stronger governance through accurate, reliable meeting records and clear action tracking
Enhanced stakeholder confidence through professional, well-coordinated meetings and events
Greater organisational agility and responsiveness through effective hybrid and virtual meeting practices
Sustainable improvement in administrative efficiency and the strategic contribution of meeting and event functions
personalImpact: Advanced practical skills in meeting design, facilitation, minute-taking and event coordination
Greater confidence and professional credibility when managing meetings at all levels
Improved ability to support senior leaders and stakeholders through high-quality documentation and follow-up
Clearer techniques for managing time, priorities and workload in meeting-intensive roles
Stronger foundation for career progression through demonstrated expertise in governance and coordination
Ready-to-use templates, frameworks and personal systems that deliver immediate and lasting improvements

This office management certificate delivers a rigorous, practice-oriented programme that unites the essential disciplines of modern administration into a single, coherent learning experience. Participants develop advanced capabilities in operational leadership, digital transformation, governance, communication and resource management while preparing for a formal assessment of their competence. The administration certificate course is designed to confirm readiness to contribute at a higher level and accelerate career progression. This course can be facilitated in London, Dubai, Kuala Lumpur, Nairobi, and other major business centres on client-preferred dates.

courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
Foundations of Modern Office Management and Administration
• Examining the evolving role of office management and administration as a strategic organisational function in contemporary workplaces
• Identifying the core principles of effective administration including efficiency, accuracy, accountability, adaptability and stakeholder focus
• Understanding the scope of responsibilities across operational, governance, communication and resource management dimensions
• Recognising the impact of strong office management on organisational performance, culture and external reputation
• Assessing personal and organisational current practices against contemporary standards and future requirements
• Establishing clear personal learning objectives aligned with the certificate assessment and professional development goals

MODULE 02
Strategic Alignment and Operational Planning
• Connecting administrative operations directly to organisational strategy, objectives and performance expectations
• Developing structured approaches to operational planning, priority setting and resource allocation
• Creating administrative strategies that support broader business goals while maintaining service excellence
• Building capability to translate strategic direction into practical administrative action plans and performance measures
• Managing the balance between operational delivery and longer-term improvement initiatives
• Producing clear planning documentation and progress reports that demonstrate administrative contribution to strategic outcomes

MODULE 03
Digital Transformation and Technology-Enabled Administration
• Understanding the opportunities and challenges presented by digital transformation in office and administrative environments
• Identifying high-impact opportunities to introduce automation, digital workflows and technology solutions
• Managing people, process and governance dimensions of technology adoption within administrative teams
• Ensuring data security, accessibility and appropriate use when implementing digital tools and systems
• Developing change management approaches that support sustainable adoption and minimise disruption
• Creating a personal and team roadmap for ongoing digital capability development and technology integration

MODULE 04
Records Management, Document Control and Information Governance
• Establishing comprehensive records classification, retention and disposal frameworks aligned with organisational and regulatory requirements
• Implementing robust document control procedures that ensure version integrity, accessibility and audit readiness
• Applying metadata standards, filing conventions and search optimisation techniques to improve information usability
• Managing the transition towards sustainable, paperless administrative practices while maintaining authenticity and compliance
• Aligning records and information practices with data protection regulations and broader governance obligations
• Developing monitoring, audit and continuous improvement processes for records and document management systems

MODULE 05
Communication Excellence and Stakeholder Relationship Management
• Developing advanced skills in adapting communication style, tone and channel for diverse internal and external stakeholders
• Building trust, credibility and rapport through consistent, professional and ethical communication practices
• Managing difficult conversations, conflicting expectations and sensitive matters with diplomacy and constructive outcomes
• Strengthening professional presence and the ability to influence positively without formal authority
• Leveraging written, verbal and digital channels effectively to maintain engagement and clarity in hybrid environments
• Establishing personal and team standards that raise the overall quality and impact of stakeholder communication

MODULE 06
Workflow Optimisation, Coordination and Resource Management
• Applying structured techniques to map, analyse and optimise administrative workflows and processes
• Developing coordination mechanisms that reduce friction, duplication and delays across teams and functions
• Managing competing priorities, resource allocation and scheduling to maximise productivity and service quality
• Building resilience into administrative operations to handle changing demands and unexpected challenges
• Implementing performance monitoring and simple indicators to track efficiency and identify improvement opportunities
• Creating sustainable systems and habits that support ongoing operational excellence and continuous improvement

MODULE 07
Meeting, Event and Governance Support Excellence
• Designing and facilitating focused, outcome-driven meetings that produce clear decisions and strong accountability
• Producing accurate, professional minutes and records that support governance, compliance and effective follow-up
• Coordinating internal and external events with robust planning, logistics management and stakeholder engagement
• Establishing systematic tracking and reporting processes that close the loop on commitments
• Adapting meeting and event practices confidently for virtual, hybrid and in-person formats
• Building organisational capability and standards that raise the overall quality and impact of meetings and events

MODULE 08
Financial Administration, Budgeting and Value-for-Money Practices
• Understanding core financial concepts, budget structures and reporting requirements relevant to administrative roles
• Applying practical techniques for budget planning, monitoring, variance analysis and corrective action
• Managing financial documentation, procurement support and expense processes with accuracy and compliance
• Identifying opportunities for cost awareness, resource optimisation and improved value for money
• Preparing clear financial summaries and briefings that support informed decision-making by non-finance stakeholders
• Strengthening personal and team financial administration practices that reduce risk and enhance accountability

MODULE 09
Leadership, Professional Presence and Career Development in Administration
• Developing leadership capabilities to influence, motivate and support colleagues within administrative functions
• Strengthening executive presence, confidence and professional credibility in interactions at all organisational levels
• Building skills in coaching, mentoring and developing others to raise team and departmental capability
• Creating a clear personal vision and development roadmap for long-term career progression in office management
• Managing personal resilience, workload and professional boundaries to sustain high performance
• Positioning administrative professionals as strategic contributors and preparing for advancement into more senior roles

MODULE 10
Integration, Assessment Preparation and Sustainable Professional Practice
• Consolidating learning across all modules into an integrated understanding of effective office management and administration
• Reviewing key concepts, frameworks and techniques in preparation for the formal written assessment
• Reflecting on personal strengths, development areas and immediate opportunities to apply learning in the workplace
• Developing a sustainable personal action plan that embeds new practices and supports continuous professional growth
• Understanding the value of the certificate credential and how to leverage it for career and organisational impact
• Committing to ongoing professional development and contribution to raising standards in office management and administration
• Assessment & Evaluation
• Upon successful completion of this programme, an Elevoris Certificate of Completion will be awarded to delegates who meet the passing requirements.

courses.title: Oil & Gas Business Management Certificate
courses.overview: In the oil and gas sector, where volatile commodity markets, accelerating energy transition pressures and complex commercial arrangements across the full value chain create both significant opportunities and material risks, many professionals with strong operational backgrounds lack the integrated business management capability required to lead strategically. This oil gas business management certificate delivers a rigorous, assessment-based programme that develops advanced competence in strategic planning, petroleum economics, commercial leadership, operational governance and investment decision-making. Participants master frameworks to align upstream, midstream and downstream activities with corporate objectives while navigating regulatory, ESG and market volatility challenges. The O&G business management training culminates in a formal credential that validates the ability to drive sustainable value and organisational resilience in a transforming energy landscape. This course can be facilitated in London, Dubai, Kuala Lumpur, Nairobi, and other major business centres on client-preferred dates.
whyChoose: Avoid the strategic missteps and value erosion that occur when leaders make decisions in isolation across the energy value chain without understanding the commercial, financial and operational interdependencies

Preventing the career limitations that arise when technically strong professionals are not equipped with the business acumen, strategic thinking and governance skills increasingly required for senior and executive roles in IOCs, NOCs and energy companies

Reduce the financial and reputational exposure created by suboptimal investment decisions, poorly structured commercial arrangements, unmanaged price and contractual risk, and weak governance in high-stakes energy environments
Eliminate the organisational inefficiency of siloed functions that fail to capture synergies between exploration and production, transportation and processing, and marketing and trading activities

Close the critical capability gap that leaves organisations vulnerable to energy transition disruption because leaders cannot develop coherent strategies balancing current hydrocarbon optimisation with new energy business models
Overcome the personal and organisational cost of reactive, short-term management in volatile markets by building proactive, integrated and value-creating business leadership practices
audience: Vice President of Strategy and Business Development and General Manager – E&P Assets accountable for portfolio strategy, capital allocation and asset performance
Director of Commercial Operations and Head of LNG Business responsible for market development, contract structuring and revenue optimisation across gas value chains
Operations Manager – Upstream and Midstream and Commercial Manager – Downstream leading integrated value chain delivery, performance improvement and supply chain resilience
Finance Manager – Energy Investments and Planning Manager – Oil & Gas managing capital allocation, petroleum economics analysis and strategic planning processes
Business Development Manager – Gas and New Energies and Contracts Manager responsible for deal origination, partnership development and contractual governance
Business Analyst – Petroleum Economics and Strategic Planning Coordinator supporting investment appraisal, performance reporting and organisational decision-making in energy companies
objectives: By the end of this certification programme, participants will be able to:

Design and execute integrated oil and gas business strategies that align upstream, midstream and downstream activities with corporate objectives, market opportunities and energy transition requirements
Develop petroleum economics evaluation frameworks that enable robust investment appraisal and capital allocation decisions across E&P and broader energy portfolios
Lead commercial negotiations, contract structuring and partnership management processes that protect value, allocate risk appropriately and build sustainable commercial relationships
Establish operational governance, performance management and supply chain frameworks that optimise asset utilisation, cost efficiency and delivery reliability across the energy value chain
Integrate ESG considerations, carbon management and energy transition pathways into core business planning, investment decisions and organisational strategy
Apply structured risk management, trading and hedging approaches to navigate oil and gas price volatility and protect organisational margins and cash flows
Build high-performing teams, governance structures and organisational capabilities that support strategic transformation and effective decision-making in dynamic energy environments
Demonstrate integrated oil and gas business management excellence through successful completion of the formal assessment and apply learning to drive measurable improvement in current and future roles
deliveryApproach: Structured certification programme combining expert facilitation with in-depth case study analysis, strategic simulations and practical workshops using authentic oil and gas business scenarios from across the value chain
Collaborative development of business strategies, investment cases, commercial frameworks and governance models with immediate structured feedback from facilitators and peers
Facilitated exploration of value chain dynamics, energy transition challenges and commercial complexities through group exercises and scenario planning
Personal strategic audits and capability assessments where participants apply new frameworks directly to their own organisational contexts and live business challenges
Progressive skill-building exercises, case-based discussions and mock assessments throughout the programme to prepare participants thoroughly for the end-of-course formal written assessment
Comprehensive participant materials, strategic frameworks, economic modelling templates, governance checklists and post-programme reference resources provided for immediate workplace application
courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
The Global Oil & Gas Business Environment and Strategic Context
• Analysing the interplay of geopolitical, regulatory, technological and market forces that shape strategic decision-making across the energy sector
• Identifying the implications of energy transition, decarbonisation policies and evolving demand patterns for traditional hydrocarbon and new energy business models
• Understanding the distinct and evolving roles of national oil companies, international oil companies and independent players in a transforming industry
• Assessing competitive dynamics, market entry barriers, growth opportunities and strategic risks in upstream, midstream and downstream segments
• Recognising the management-level impact of digitalisation, data analytics and advanced technologies on operational decision-making and business model innovation
• Establishing clear personal and organisational learning objectives aligned with current strategic priorities and the certification assessment

MODULE 02
Value Chain Integration and Business Model Optimisation
• Mapping the full energy value chain from exploration through production, transportation, processing and marketing to identify integration opportunities and value leakage points
• Developing approaches to optimise commercial and operational interfaces between upstream, midstream and downstream activities for enhanced overall performance
• Building capability to design and evaluate integrated business models that capture synergies while managing complexity and risk across segments
• Managing supply chain resilience, local content requirements and logistics strategies at a portfolio level to support reliable and cost-effective operations
• Establishing performance metrics and governance mechanisms that align activities across the value chain with corporate strategic objectives
• Creating practical frameworks for identifying and executing value-creating integration opportunities in existing asset portfolios

MODULE 03
Petroleum Economics, Investment Analysis and Capital Discipline
• Applying structured petroleum economics principles to evaluate investment opportunities, including cash flow modelling, risk-adjusted returns and portfolio optimisation
• Developing robust investment appraisal processes that incorporate uncertainty, scenario analysis and strategic fit alongside financial metrics
• Building capability to allocate capital efficiently across exploration, development, production and new energy opportunities while maintaining financial discipline
• Managing the interface between technical, commercial and financial considerations in investment decision-making at asset and portfolio level
• Establishing governance frameworks for investment proposals, stage-gate reviews and post-investment evaluation that improve decision quality over time
• Creating approaches to balance short-term cash generation with long-term value creation in capital-intensive energy environments

MODULE 04
Commercial Strategy, Contracting and Negotiation Excellence
• Designing commercial strategies that maximise value from existing assets and new opportunities through effective market positioning and deal structuring
• Developing advanced skills in structuring, negotiating and administering complex energy contracts, including production sharing agreements, joint venture agreements and offtake arrangements
• Building capability to identify, allocate and manage commercial risks through contractual mechanisms while maintaining operational flexibility
• Managing the full commercial lifecycle from opportunity identification through negotiation, execution and ongoing contract performance assurance
• Establishing internal governance and approval processes that ensure commercial decisions are aligned with organisational risk appetite and strategic priorities
• Creating practical frameworks for building and maintaining constructive commercial relationships that support long-term value creation

MODULE 05
Joint Venture, Partnership and Alliance Management
• Applying structured approaches to joint venture formation, governance design and partner selection that protect organisational interests while enabling effective collaboration
• Developing skills in managing joint venture operations, decision-making processes and dispute resolution mechanisms in complex multi-party environments
• Building capability to align partner objectives, manage cultural and strategic differences and maintain productive working relationships over the life of the venture
• Establishing governance frameworks, reporting structures and performance management systems that support effective joint venture oversight
• Managing the commercial, operational and strategic implications of farm-ins, farm-outs, acquisitions and divestments within partnership contexts
• Creating approaches to build internal capability for effective participation in joint ventures and strategic alliances across the energy sector

MODULE 06
Operational Excellence, Asset Management and Supply Chain Leadership
• Developing operational strategies that maximise production efficiency, uptime and cost performance while maintaining safety and environmental standards
• Building capability to implement asset integrity, maintenance and reliability strategies at a management level that protect long-term value
• Managing supply chain strategy, contractor performance and procurement governance to deliver operational excellence and cost optimisation
• Establishing performance management systems, benchmarking processes and continuous improvement cultures across operational assets
• Integrating digital tools and data-driven decision-making into operational leadership without compromising safety or governance standards
• Creating frameworks for balancing operational performance with capital discipline, energy transition requirements and stakeholder expectations

MODULE 07
Energy Trading, Risk Management and Price Risk Strategies
• Understanding the fundamentals of energy trading, market structures and price formation mechanisms across crude oil, natural gas and refined products
• Developing structured approaches to identify, measure and manage price, volume and basis risk exposures across the portfolio
• Building capability to design and implement hedging strategies that protect margins and cash flows while preserving upside potential
• Managing the interface between physical operations, commercial trading and financial risk management functions
• Establishing governance frameworks, trading controls and compliance processes appropriate for energy market participation
• Creating practical approaches to scenario planning and stress testing that prepare organisations for sustained price volatility and structural market shifts

MODULE 08
Corporate Governance, Compliance, Ethics and ESG Integration
• Establishing robust corporate governance frameworks that ensure accountability, transparency and effective oversight in energy organisations
• Developing approaches to embed regulatory compliance, ethical standards and anti-corruption requirements into routine business operations and decision-making
• Building capability to integrate ESG considerations, carbon management and sustainability reporting into core strategy, investment decisions and performance management
• Managing stakeholder expectations, reputational risk and social licence to operate in increasingly scrutinised energy environments
• Establishing board and executive reporting mechanisms that provide clear visibility of governance, compliance and ESG performance
• Creating continuous improvement processes that strengthen organisational resilience and stakeholder trust over time

MODULE 09
Energy Transition Strategy and Sustainable Business Transformation
• Analysing the strategic implications of energy transition, net zero commitments and evolving policy landscapes for existing and future business portfolios
• Developing coherent strategies that optimise current hydrocarbon operations while building credible positions in lower-carbon and new energy opportunities
• Building capability to evaluate and execute investments in carbon management, renewables integration and adjacent energy businesses
• Managing the organisational, cultural and capability changes required to deliver credible and value-accretive energy transition strategies
• Establishing governance and performance frameworks that track progress on transition objectives alongside traditional financial and operational metrics
• Creating practical approaches to communicate transition strategy credibly to investors, regulators, partners and other stakeholders

MODULE 10
Strategic Leadership, Organisational Capability and Executive Decision-Making
• Consolidating learning across the programme into an integrated personal leadership approach for oil and gas business management
• Developing skills in leading cross-functional teams, driving strategic alignment and building organisational capability for sustained high performance
• Building capability to make high-quality decisions under uncertainty, balancing analytical rigour with commercial judgement and stakeholder considerations
• Establishing mechanisms for measuring, communicating and improving the business impact of strategic and operational decisions
• Creating personal and team action plans for immediate application and long-term continuous development in energy business leadership
• Committing to ongoing mastery and active contribution to building organisational capability in integrated oil and gas business management
• Assessment & Evaluation
• Upon successful completion of this programme, an Elevoris Certificate of Training will be awarded to delegates who meet the passing requirements.

In an industry defined by capital intensity, long investment cycles, geopolitical complexity and profound structural transformation, excellence in oil and gas business management is no longer optional. This certificate provides the depth, practical frameworks and formal credential required to lead with confidence at the highest levels of the energy sector.

Enrol now in the Oil & Gas Business Management Certificate to develop the integrated business leadership capability that will position you and your organisation for enduring success in the evolving global energy landscape.
