courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
The Strategic Role of Contracts in Oil & Gas Value Creation
• Examining how contracts function as primary instruments of commercial strategy, risk allocation and value protection across the energy value chain
• Identifying the hidden costs of treating contract negotiation as a purely legal or transactional process rather than a core commercial leadership discipline
• Understanding the interplay between contract architecture, operational reality and long-term organisational performance in capital-intensive energy projects
• Recognising how shifts in energy transition policy, stakeholder expectations and market dynamics are reshaping the commercial terms that define successful contracts
• Assessing the specific negotiation and governance capabilities that distinguish organisations which consistently create value through contracts from those that merely avoid major failures
• Establishing clear personal and organisational objectives for the masterclass aligned with current commercial challenges and strategic priorities

MODULE 02
Contract Lifecycle Governance and Strategic Alignment
• Applying systematic approaches to contract initiation, formation, execution, monitoring and close-out that maintain strategic alignment and commercial control at every stage
• Developing governance frameworks that define roles, approval gates, escalation paths and performance accountability across complex, multi-year agreements
• Building techniques for maintaining version control, obligation tracking and milestone visibility that prevent oversights in long-duration energy contracts
• Managing the transition between contract phases, including mobilisation, steady-state operations, extensions, amendments and demobilisation with minimal value leakage
• Establishing contract portfolio reporting and review rhythms that keep senior stakeholders informed and enable timely strategic adjustments
• Creating practical standards for lifecycle discipline that can be applied consistently across diverse upstream, midstream and downstream agreements

MODULE 03
Advanced Contract Drafting, Interpretation and Risk Allocation
• Developing advanced skills in drafting, reviewing and interpreting contractual language to identify ambiguities, unintended obligations and opportunities for value enhancement
• Applying structured techniques for allocating commercial, operational, political and force majeure risks through precise and enforceable provisions
• Building capability to translate negotiated commercial intent into clear, administrable contractual terms that minimise future interpretation disputes
• Managing the balance between legal precision, operational practicality and commercial flexibility in different contract types and risk contexts
• Establishing consistent interpretation guidelines and internal precedents that support uniform application across teams and over the life of agreements
• Creating robust review protocols that combine commercial, operational, legal and risk perspectives before contracts are finalised

MODULE 04
Production Sharing Agreements, Joint Ventures and Partnership Contracts
• Applying structured approaches to negotiating and structuring production sharing agreements and joint venture contracts that balance host government requirements with investor interests
• Developing skills in designing governance, decision-making and dispute resolution mechanisms that support effective joint venture operations over extended periods
• Building capability to manage partner alignment, cultural differences and changing strategic priorities within multi-party energy ventures
• Managing the commercial and strategic implications of farm-ins, farm-outs, carried interests and partnership restructurings
• Establishing robust provisions for cost recovery, profit sharing, lifting entitlements and transfer of rights that protect long-term value
• Creating practical frameworks for ongoing joint venture contract administration and performance management that sustain collaborative advantage

MODULE 05
Negotiation Strategy, Planning and Tactical Excellence
• Applying comprehensive negotiation planning frameworks that integrate commercial objectives, stakeholder mapping, BATNA analysis and scenario development
• Developing advanced negotiation tactics, communication techniques and psychological insights tailored to oil and gas commercial contexts
• Building capability to manage multi-party, multi-issue negotiations involving governments, national oil companies, international partners and service providers
• Managing the critical balance between value creation, relationship preservation and firm defence of core interests during high-stakes discussions
• Establishing internal negotiation governance, team roles, mandate processes and real-time decision protocols that improve outcomes
• Creating practical approaches to post-negotiation debriefing, organisational learning and continuous improvement of negotiation capability

MODULE 06
Claims Management, Variations and Dispute Prevention
• Developing systematic approaches to identify, document and evaluate potential claims early through performance trends, correspondence analysis and obligation tracking
• Building skills in preparing, presenting and negotiating claims with robust evidence, clear causation narratives and commercial awareness
• Applying structured techniques for managing variations, change orders and contract amendments that protect positions while maintaining project momentum
• Establishing proactive dispute prevention cultures, early-warning systems and escalation protocols that address issues before they mature into formal disputes
• Managing the interface between contractual dispute resolution mechanisms, negotiation and alternative dispute resolution pathways
• Creating practical frameworks for rebuilding commercial relationships and momentum following periods of conflict or claims activity

MODULE 07
Price, Volume and Market Risk in Commercial Contracts
• Understanding the structure and implications of different pricing mechanisms, indexation formulas and adjustment provisions across crude oil, natural gas, LNG and refined product contracts
• Developing advanced techniques for identifying, allocating and managing price, volume, currency and basis risk through contractual and commercial mechanisms
• Building capability to negotiate flexible pricing, take-or-pay, destination and volume flexibility provisions that balance risk and opportunity
• Managing the interface between physical contract terms, trading activities and financial hedging strategies
• Establishing governance frameworks for price review clauses, hardship provisions and renegotiation triggers that protect long-term value
• Creating practical approaches to scenario planning and stress testing of contract economics under different market and regulatory conditions

MODULE 08
ESG, Sustainability and Regulatory Integration in Contract Design
• Integrating environmental, social and governance requirements, carbon management obligations and sustainability commitments into contract structures and negotiation positions
• Developing approaches to managing regulatory compliance, local content, modern slavery and anti-bribery provisions within commercial agreements
• Building capability to negotiate and administer contracts that support social licence, reputational protection and access to capital in increasingly scrutinised environments
• Managing the commercial implications of emissions reduction targets, methane management and decarbonisation pathways within existing and new contractual arrangements
• Establishing governance and reporting mechanisms that ensure ongoing compliance and performance visibility across the contract portfolio
• Creating practical frameworks for turning ESG requirements into sources of competitive advantage and differentiation in contract negotiations

MODULE 09
Digital Enablement and Contract Lifecycle Management
• Identifying appropriate opportunities to leverage contract lifecycle management platforms, automation tools and analytics to improve accuracy, visibility and efficiency
• Developing practical approaches to data capture, obligation extraction, performance monitoring and risk flagging that transform contract repositories into active management assets
• Building skills in responsible use of digital tools for version control, workflow automation, e-signature and real-time reporting while maintaining human oversight and auditability
• Managing the challenges of system integration, data quality and organisational change when introducing or upgrading digital contract capabilities
• Establishing metrics and dashboards that provide leadership with actionable insight into contract portfolio health, obligation status and commercial performance
• Creating sustainable digital contract administration disciplines that combine technological efficiency with professional judgement and organisational governance requirements

MODULE 10
Strategic Leadership in Commercial Negotiations and Organisational Capability
• Consolidating learning across the masterclass into a coherent personal and organisational approach to contracts and commercial negotiations
• Developing skills in leading cross-functional negotiation teams, building internal capability and embedding commercial discipline across the organisation
• Building capability to influence senior and executive level on contract strategy, major negotiations and commercial risk appetite
• Establishing mechanisms for measuring, communicating and improving the business impact of contract and negotiation performance
• Creating personal and team action plans for immediate application and long-term development in commercial leadership
• Committing to ongoing mastery and active contribution to building organisational capability in strategic contract leadership and value-creating negotiation
expectedOutcomes: Participants will be able to:
Lead complex oil and gas contract negotiations and commercial discussions with demonstrably greater strategic clarity, commercial discipline and value creation
Structure and administer production sharing agreements, joint ventures and offtake contracts that deliver superior risk-adjusted outcomes and long-term flexibility
Prevent and resolve commercial disputes more effectively through proactive identification, robust preparation and skilled negotiation
Integrate ESG, regulatory and sustainability requirements into contract design and administration in ways that enhance competitive positioning and stakeholder confidence
Drive measurable improvement in contract portfolio performance, obligation compliance and commercial relationship quality
Accelerate progression into senior commercial, business development and contracts leadership roles through demonstrated mastery of oil and gas contracts and negotiation
organisationalImpact: Improved quality and consistency of contract outcomes, risk allocation and commercial terms across the portfolio
Significant reduction in value leakage, claims costs and dispute frequency through more rigorous and proactive contract leadership
Stronger competitive positioning through more effective negotiation of major agreements and partnership structures
Enhanced organisational resilience to market volatility, regulatory change and counterparty behaviour through better-structured and governed contracts
Greater internal capability to originate, negotiate and manage complex commercial arrangements without excessive reliance on external advisers
Sustainable improvement in commercial performance, stakeholder relationships and long-term value creation from contractual arrangements
personalImpact: Clear acceleration in career trajectory as contracts and commercial negotiation capability becomes a recognised personal strength and differentiator for senior commercial roles
Greater professional confidence and influence when leading high-stakes negotiations and engaging senior stakeholders on complex commercial matters
A distinctive professional brand as a commercially astute leader capable of structuring and negotiating agreements that protect and enhance organisational value
A practical toolkit of negotiation frameworks, contract templates, governance tools and dispute management approaches that deliver immediate and lasting improvements
Enhanced ability to contribute strategically to organisational commercial success rather than remaining focused on narrow transactional responsibilities
Clear personal development roadmap and professional brand as a trusted leader in oil and gas contracts and commercial negotiations
General Notes
Sector customisation available on request
Training material provided
Elevoris Certificate of Training issued to all participants
Optional post-programme advisory coaching available

In an industry where contracts are the primary mechanism through which value is created, protected and sometimes destroyed, excellence in commercial negotiation and contract leadership is no longer a support function. It is a core strategic capability that determines whether organisations capture or concede value in every major agreement. This masterclass provides the depth, live practice and transformation required to lead at that level.

Enrol now in the Oil & Gas Contracts & Commercial Negotiations Masterclass to develop the commercial mastery that will distinguish you as an outstanding contracts and negotiation leader in the energy sector.

courses.title: Operations Excellence & Process Improvement in Healthcare Masterclass
courses.overview: Healthcare organisations continue to face persistent operational inefficiencies, delays, resource waste and process variation that compromise service quality, increase costs and undermine staff and patient experience. This healthcare operations training delivers an intensive, practitioner-focused masterclass equipping managers with advanced lean, process improvement and operational excellence methodologies tailored specifically to complex healthcare environments. Participants develop hands-on skills in value stream mapping, data-driven problem solving, flow optimisation and sustainable change implementation that deliver measurable efficiency gains and service improvements. This course can be facilitated in London, Dubai, Riyadh, Nairobi, and other major business centres on client-preferred dates.
whyChoose: Apply structured lean and process improvement methodologies to identify, analyse and eliminate waste, variation and bottlenecks across hospital and healthcare operational pathways
Design and implement value stream mapping, flow optimisation and capacity management solutions that reduce delays, improve throughput and enhance service responsiveness
Integrate data analytics, performance measurement and root cause analysis techniques to diagnose operational issues and prioritise high-impact improvement initiatives
Lead practical changes and implementation programmes that engage staff, overcome resistance and embed sustainable process improvements into daily operations
Develop operational excellence frameworks that align process improvement with value-based healthcare principles, cost efficiency and quality outcomes
Build organisational capability to create a culture of continuous improvement, standardisation and visual management that sustains performance gains over time
audience: Directors of Operations and Heads of Process Excellence accountable for organisation-wide operational performance, efficiency strategy and improvement governance
Operations Managers and Service Improvement Managers responsible for leading process redesign, patient flow optimisation and efficiency initiatives within clinical and support services
Performance Improvement Managers and Lean Practitioners tasked with applying structured methodologies, facilitating workshops and delivering measurable operational gains
Quality and Compliance Managers integrating process improvement with regulatory requirements, risk mitigation and quality management systems
Operations Analysts and Improvement Specialists conducting process mapping, data analysis, root cause investigation and improvement project support
Process Improvement Officers and Coordinators facilitating workshops, documentation, implementation tracking and stakeholder engagement under senior direction
objectives: By the end of this masterclass, participants will be able to:
Apply lean thinking, value stream mapping and waste elimination techniques to diagnose and optimise complex healthcare operational processes, patient pathways and support service workflows
Design and implement flow optimisation, capacity management and scheduling solutions that reduce delays, improve throughput and enhance operational responsiveness across hospital services
Utilise data analytics, statistical process control and root cause analysis methods to identify performance gaps, prioritise improvement opportunities and measure intervention impact
Lead structured change and implementation programmes that engage multidisciplinary teams, manage resistance and embed sustainable process improvements into operational practice
Develop operational excellence frameworks, standard work practices and visual management systems that sustain efficiency gains and support continuous improvement cultures
Integrate process improvement initiatives with value-based healthcare principles, cost control objectives and quality outcomes to demonstrate measurable organisational value
Build organisational capability to scale improvement methodologies, develop internal expertise and create self-sustaining operational excellence across departments and services
Communication improvement results effectively through data storytelling, performance reporting and stakeholder engagement that secures ongoing leadership support and resource commitment

Detailed case study analysis of successful healthcare operations excellence programmes highlighting methodology application, implementation challenges and measurable outcomes
Practical simulation exercises requiring participants to map processes, identify waste, redesign workflows and develop implementation plans with real-time expert coaching
Collaborative improvement projects developing end-to-end process improvement solutions for common healthcare challenges such as patient flow, resource utilisation and support service efficiency
Masterclasses on specialised topics including data-driven improvement, change leadership, digital process enablement and sustaining operational excellence cultures
Personal operational improvement projects applying masterclass techniques to participants’ current organisational challenges with implementation planning, progress review and expert feedback
courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
Foundations of Operations Excellence in Healthcare Management
• Examining the distinctive operational challenges facing healthcare organisations including complexity, interdependencies and the imperative for efficiency alongside quality and safety
• Defining core principles of operations excellence including customer focus, process discipline, waste elimination and continuous improvement thinking
• Identifying common sources of operational waste, variation and inefficiency in hospital and healthcare service delivery pathways
• Establishing the foundational elements of effective process improvement practice including leadership commitment, staff engagement and data-informed decision-making
• Recognising the relationship between operational excellence, financial performance, patient experience and strategic organisational objectives
• Mapping the operational excellence journey from current state assessment through improvement implementation to sustainable performance gains

MODULE 02
Lean Thinking and Waste Elimination Methodologies
• Applying lean thinking principles to identify and categorise waste across healthcare operational, administrative and support processes

Patient Flow Optimisation and Capacity Management

• Integrating flow optimisation with performance metrics, quality outcomes and patient experience considerations

MODULE 05
Data Analytics and Performance Measurement for Improvement
• Utilising healthcare operational data to establish performance baselines, identify improvement opportunities and track intervention impact

courses.title: Presentation Skills & Public Speaking Masterclass
courses.overview: Even accomplished professionals frequently watch their expertise lose impact the moment they stand to speak, their carefully prepared content undermined by delivery that fails to command attention, build credibility or move audiences to action. This presentation skills training transforms how individuals prepare, structure and deliver messages that resonate deeply and drive decisive outcomes in high-stakes environments. Participants develop commanding presence, persuasive structure and adaptive performance capabilities that distinguish exceptional communicators from the competent. The public speaking masterclass course combines rigorous practice with targeted feedback to build lasting confidence and professional influence. This course can be facilitated in London, Dubai, Kuala Lumpur, Nairobi, and other major business centres on client-preferred dates.
whyChoose: Avoid the hidden career cost of brilliant ideas that never gain traction because delivery fails to inspire confidence or urgency in decision-makers
Eliminate the professional risk of diminished credibility when senior audiences perceive hesitation, disorganisation or lack of authority during critical presentations
Prevent the organisational cost of misaligned decisions caused by presentations that inform without persuading or engage without committing stakeholders to action
Overcome the personal frustration of knowing your content is strong yet watching it land weakly due to nerves, poor structure or ineffective delivery habits
Reduce the cumulative damage to reputation that occurs when professionals repeatedly underperform in visible, high-stakes communication moments that shape how others perceive their capability
Close the gap between technical expertise and leadership presence that often stalls career progression for otherwise high-performing individuals
audience: Director of Strategy and Corporate Development who regularly presents board papers, investment cases and strategic recommendations
Head of Business Development leading high-value client pitches, partnership negotiations and internal growth proposals
Communications Manager responsible for team briefings, stakeholder updates and organisational messaging delivery
Senior Project Manager delivering progress reports, risk assessments and recommendations to executive and cross-functional audiences
Business Development Executive preparing and presenting client proposals, tender responses and performance reviews
Communications Officer or Analyst supporting presentation development and occasionally delivering findings to management and project teams
objectives: By the end of this masterclass, participants will be able to:
Design and deliver high-impact presentations that command attention from the opening moment, sustain engagement and drive audiences to clear, decisive action in high-stakes business settings
Structure complex information into compelling, memorable narratives that align audience understanding with desired organisational outcomes
Project authentic executive presence through voice, body language and composure that establishes immediate credibility and authority, even under pressure
Adapt delivery techniques with precision for in-person, virtual and hybrid environments while maintaining connection, clarity and persuasive power
Manage audience dynamics, questions and objections strategically to maintain control, build rapport and advance intended messages
Apply targeted techniques to manage performance anxiety and convert nervous energy into focused, confident delivery
Integrate visual, data and supporting materials that enhance rather than dilute the core message and strengthen audience retention
Establish a personal practice and feedback system that enables continuous improvement and sustains excellence in presentation performance
deliveryApproach: Dynamic workshop methodology combining expert input with extensive live presentation practice, peer observation and immediate structured feedback
Multiple opportunities for participants to deliver prepared and impromptu presentations with video recording for detailed self-assessment and targeted coaching
Collaborative exercises in audience analysis, message structuring and narrative development using real workplace scenarios and current challenges
Focused skill drills on voice, body language, pacing and audience engagement with real-time adjustment and peer coaching
Facilitated review of effective and ineffective presentation examples to extract precise techniques and common failure patterns
Personal action planning with specific, measurable commitments for continued practice and development beyond the programme
courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
The Inner Game of Presence: Building Unshakeable Confidence from Within
• Examining the psychological foundations of speaker confidence and the common mental patterns that undermine even experienced professionals
• Developing practical mindset techniques to reframe anxiety as focused energy and maintain composure under scrutiny
• Establishing personal rituals and preparation routines that create consistent readiness and reduce last-minute panic
• Understanding the relationship between self-perception and audience perception and how to align the two authentically
• Building resilience to setbacks, difficult questions and unexpected disruptions during live delivery
• Creating a personal confidence framework that can be activated before any high-stakes presentation

MODULE 02
Audience Intelligence: Mapping Needs, Motivations and Decision Triggers
• Applying structured approaches to analyse audience composition, knowledge levels, priorities and hidden agendas before designing content
• Identifying the specific outcomes different stakeholder groups seek and tailoring messages to address both rational and emotional drivers
• Mapping formal and informal power dynamics within audiences to anticipate support, resistance and key influencers
• Developing techniques to read live audience reactions and adjust tone, pace and emphasis in real time
• Establishing methods for gathering pre-presentation intelligence through formal and informal channels
• Creating audience profiles and engagement strategies that increase relevance and receptivity

MODULE 03
The Architecture of Persuasion: Structuring Arguments That Move Audiences
• Designing clear, logical narrative structures that guide audiences from current understanding to desired action without confusion or overload
• Applying proven frameworks for opening with impact, building tension, delivering key messages and closing with commitment
• Balancing logical argument with emotional resonance to create presentations that are both credible and compelling
• Managing information hierarchy so that critical points stand out while supporting detail remains accessible but secondary
• Developing techniques for handling complex or technical content without losing audience attention or diluting persuasive force
• Creating flexible structures that allow adaptation during delivery while preserving overall coherence and impact

MODULE 04
Voice, Body and Non-Verbal Command: Projecting Authority Without Words
• Developing vocal techniques including strategic pacing, emphasis, volume control and tonal variety that increase clarity and engagement
• Mastering body language fundamentals including posture, gesture, movement and eye contact that reinforce rather than contradict spoken messages
• Understanding how non-verbal signals influence audience perception of confidence, trustworthiness and expertise
• Practising techniques for managing nervous habits and converting physical tension into purposeful, controlled presence
• Adapting non-verbal communication for different room sizes, audience distances and cultural contexts
• Building awareness of personal non-verbal patterns through video feedback and deliberate adjustment

MODULE 05
Visual Storytelling and Supporting Materials: Enhancing Without Overwhelming
• Designing visual aids that support and amplify the core narrative rather than compete with or distract from the speaker
• Applying principles of visual clarity, simplicity and relevance when creating slides, charts and supporting documents
• Managing the timing and integration of visual materials so they enhance rather than interrupt audience connection
• Developing techniques for using data and evidence persuasively without overwhelming audiences with complexity
• Creating handout and leave-behind materials that extend impact beyond the live presentation
• Establishing personal standards for visual quality and message consistency across all presentation materials

MODULE 06
Managing Nerves and High-Pressure Delivery: Composure Under Scrutiny
• Understanding the physiological and cognitive effects of performance anxiety and evidence-based techniques to regulate them
• Developing pre-presentation routines that reduce cortisol response and create focused, calm readiness
• Applying in-the-moment strategies including breathing, grounding and cognitive reframing when anxiety spikes during delivery
• Building confidence through progressive exposure and deliberate practice in increasingly challenging scenarios
• Managing the specific pressures of board-level, client-facing and public presentations where stakes are highest
• Creating personal recovery techniques for moments when delivery does not go to plan

MODULE 07
Reading and Engaging the Room: Interactive Techniques for Dynamic Connection
• Developing real-time audience reading skills to detect engagement levels, confusion, resistance and emerging questions
• Applying interactive techniques including strategic questioning, polling and discussion prompts that maintain energy and involvement
• Managing dominant voices, disengaged participants and side conversations without damaging rapport or losing control
• Building skills in storytelling, analogy and live examples that make abstract or complex content concrete and memorable
• Developing techniques for handling unexpected audience reactions, interruptions and challenging moments with professionalism
• Creating inclusive engagement approaches that work across diverse audience demographics and communication preferences

MODULE 08
Virtual and Hybrid Presentation Excellence: Projecting Presence Across Digital Platforms
• Adapting presence, energy and connection techniques for camera-based delivery where traditional non-verbal cues are limited
• Managing technical setup, lighting, framing, sound and background to project professionalism and minimise distractions
• Developing specific engagement techniques for virtual audiences including chat management, polls and breakout structures
• Maintaining audience connection and energy across longer virtual sessions where attention fatigue is a significant risk
• Handling the unique challenges of hybrid presentations where some participants are present and others remote
• Establishing personal standards and checklists for consistent virtual and hybrid delivery quality

MODULE 09
Persuasion in Practice: Moving Audiences from Understanding to Commitment
• Applying advanced persuasion principles including framing, social proof, scarcity and authority in ethical, professional contexts
• Developing skills in handling objections, scepticism and competing viewpoints without becoming defensive or losing momentum
• Building capability to tailor persuasive approaches to different decision-making styles and organisational cultures
• Practising the art of the ask: structuring clear, compelling calls to action that audiences can and will act upon
• Managing the balance between logical rigour and emotional appeal in high-stakes business environments
• Creating personal persuasion frameworks that can be adapted rapidly for different audiences and objectives

MODULE 10
The Path to Lasting Mastery: Feedback, Refinement and Continuous Excellence
• Establishing systematic approaches to self-assessment and peer feedback that accelerate skill development after the programme
• Developing a personal practice regimen that maintains and extends presentation capabilities over time
• Building capability to coach and support colleagues in improving their own presentation performance
• Creating mechanisms for capturing lessons from every significant presentation and applying them to future work
• Understanding how presentation mastery contributes to broader leadership presence and career advancement
• Committing to a long-term development plan that positions presentation excellence as a core professional capability
expectedOutcomes: Participants will be able to:
Command immediate attention and sustain engagement throughout presentations, regardless of audience size, seniority or format
Deliver messages that are remembered, believed and acted upon because they combine clarity, persuasion and authentic presence
Walk into any room or virtual setting with the quiet confidence that comes from knowing exactly how to prepare and perform
Adapt delivery fluidly between in-person, virtual and hybrid environments without loss of impact or connection
Handle questions, objections and difficult moments with poise, strategic thinking and maintained audience respect
Continuously refine performance through deliberate practice, feedback and self-assessment, becoming measurably stronger with every presentation
organisationalImpact: Improved quality of decision-making through presentations that present information clearly, build genuine understanding and drive commitment
Reduced time wasted in meetings and briefings caused by unclear, unfocused or unpersuasive communication
Stronger organisational reputation when professionals at all levels represent the organisation with confidence and credibility
Faster alignment and execution when strategic messages are delivered in ways that inspire action rather than mere compliance
Enhanced internal capability as skilled presenters coach and raise standards among colleagues and teams
Sustainable improvement in how the organisation communicates its vision, performance and proposals to all stakeholders
personalImpact: Transformed professional presence that immediately signals capability, authority and credibility in every presentation setting
Greater career mobility as the ability to present with impact becomes a recognised strength rather than a limiting factor
Increased influence in meetings, negotiations and leadership discussions where ideas must compete for attention and support
Reduced anxiety and increased enjoyment in situations that previously triggered stress and underperformance
Clearer personal brand as someone who can be trusted to represent ideas, teams and the organisation effectively
Practical frameworks, techniques and a personal practice system that deliver compounding returns throughout a professional career

Training material provided

Enrol now in the Presentation Skills & Public Speaking Masterclass to develop the presence, structure and persuasive power that will define how decision-makers experience you and your ideas.

sourceRecord.courseSyllabus:
MODULE 01
The Inner Game of Presence: Building Unshakeable Confidence from Within
• Examining the psychological foundations of speaker confidence and the common mental patterns that undermine even experienced professionals
• Developing practical mindset techniques to reframe anxiety as focused energy and maintain composure under scrutiny
• Establishing personal rituals and preparation routines that create consistent readiness and reduce last-minute panic
• Understanding the relationship between self-perception and audience perception and how to align the two authentically
• Building resilience to setbacks, difficult questions and unexpected disruptions during live delivery
• Creating a personal confidence framework that can be activated before any high-stakes presentation

MODULE 02
Audience Intelligence: Mapping Needs, Motivations and Decision Triggers
• Applying structured approaches to analyse audience composition, knowledge levels, priorities and hidden agendas before designing content
• Identifying the specific outcomes different stakeholder groups seek and tailoring messages to address both rational and emotional drivers
• Mapping formal and informal power dynamics within audiences to anticipate support, resistance and key influencers
• Developing techniques to read live audience reactions and adjust tone, pace and emphasis in real time
• Establishing methods for gathering pre-presentation intelligence through formal and informal channels
• Creating audience profiles and engagement strategies that increase relevance and receptivity

MODULE 03
The Architecture of Persuasion: Structuring Arguments That Move Audiences
• Designing clear, logical narrative structures that guide audiences from current understanding to desired action without confusion or overload
• Applying proven frameworks for opening with impact, building tension, delivering key messages and closing with commitment
• Balancing logical argument with emotional resonance to create presentations that are both credible and compelling
• Managing information hierarchy so that critical points stand out while supporting detail remains accessible but secondary
• Developing techniques for handling complex or technical content without losing audience attention or diluting persuasive force
• Creating flexible structures that allow adaptation during delivery while preserving overall coherence and impact

MODULE 04
Voice, Body and Non-Verbal Command: Projecting Authority Without Words
• Developing vocal techniques including strategic pacing, emphasis, volume control and tonal variety that increase clarity and engagement
• Mastering body language fundamentals including posture, gesture, movement and eye contact that reinforce rather than contradict spoken messages
• Understanding how non-verbal signals influence audience perception of confidence, trustworthiness and expertise
• Practising techniques for managing nervous habits and converting physical tension into purposeful, controlled presence
• Adapting non-verbal communication for different room sizes, audience distances and cultural contexts
• Building awareness of personal non-verbal patterns through video feedback and deliberate adjustment

MODULE 05
Visual Storytelling and Supporting Materials: Enhancing Without Overwhelming
• Designing visual aids that support and amplify the core narrative rather than compete with or distract from the speaker
• Applying principles of visual clarity, simplicity and relevance when creating slides, charts and supporting documents
• Managing the timing and integration of visual materials so they enhance rather than interrupt audience connection
• Developing techniques for using data and evidence persuasively without overwhelming audiences with complexity
• Creating handout and leave-behind materials that extend impact beyond the live presentation
• Establishing personal standards for visual quality and message consistency across all presentation materials

MODULE 06
Managing Nerves and High-Pressure Delivery: Composure Under Scrutiny
• Understanding the physiological and cognitive effects of performance anxiety and evidence-based techniques to regulate them
• Developing pre-presentation routines that reduce cortisol response and create focused, calm readiness
• Applying in-the-moment strategies including breathing, grounding and cognitive reframing when anxiety spikes during delivery
• Building confidence through progressive exposure and deliberate practice in increasingly challenging scenarios
• Managing the specific pressures of board-level, client-facing and public presentations where stakes are highest
• Creating personal recovery techniques for moments when delivery does not go to plan

MODULE 07
Reading and Engaging the Room: Interactive Techniques for Dynamic Connection
• Developing real-time audience reading skills to detect engagement levels, confusion, resistance and emerging questions
• Applying interactive techniques including strategic questioning, polling and discussion prompts that maintain energy and involvement
• Managing dominant voices, disengaged participants and side conversations without damaging rapport or losing control
• Building skills in storytelling, analogy and live examples that make abstract or complex content concrete and memorable
• Developing techniques for handling unexpected audience reactions, interruptions and challenging moments with professionalism
• Creating inclusive engagement approaches that work across diverse audience demographics and communication preferences

MODULE 08
Virtual and Hybrid Presentation Excellence: Projecting Presence Across Digital Platforms
• Adapting presence, energy and connection techniques for camera-based delivery where traditional non-verbal cues are limited
• Managing technical setup, lighting, framing, sound and background to project professionalism and minimise distractions
• Developing specific engagement techniques for virtual audiences including chat management, polls and breakout structures
• Maintaining audience connection and energy across longer virtual sessions where attention fatigue is a significant risk
• Handling the unique challenges of hybrid presentations where some participants are present and others remote
• Establishing personal standards and checklists for consistent virtual and hybrid delivery quality

MODULE 09
Persuasion in Practice: Moving Audiences from Understanding to Commitment
• Applying advanced persuasion principles including framing, social proof, scarcity and authority in ethical, professional contexts
• Developing skills in handling objections, scepticism and competing viewpoints without becoming defensive or losing momentum
• Building capability to tailor persuasive approaches to different decision-making styles and organisational cultures
• Practising the art of the ask: structuring clear, compelling calls to action that audiences can and will act upon
• Managing the balance between logical rigour and emotional appeal in high-stakes business environments
• Creating personal persuasion frameworks that can be adapted rapidly for different audiences and objectives

MODULE 10
The Path to Lasting Mastery: Feedback, Refinement and Continuous Excellence
• Establishing systematic approaches to self-assessment and peer feedback that accelerate skill development after the programme
• Developing a personal practice regimen that maintains and extends presentation capabilities over time
• Building capability to coach and support colleagues in improving their own presentation performance
• Creating mechanisms for capturing lessons from every significant presentation and applying them to future work
• Understanding how presentation mastery contributes to broader leadership presence and career advancement
• Committing to a long-term development plan that positions presentation excellence as a core professional capability

Public Affairs Strategy & Government Engagement Programme
courses.overview: Public affairs professionals face mounting pressure to deliver strategic influence amid complex regulatory environments, shifting political priorities and heightened stakeholder expectations. This public affairs strategy training provides leaders with structured frameworks for analysing political landscapes, mapping stakeholder ecosystems and developing integrated government engagement strategies that align organisational objectives with public policy priorities. Participants gain practical capability to build credible relationships with government stakeholders, anticipate regulatory developments and manage policy risk proactively. The government engagement programme ensures participants can translate strategic insight into actionable plans that protect reputation and create sustainable competitive advantage. This course can be facilitated in London, Dubai, Kuala Lumpur, Nairobi, and other major business centres on client-preferred dates.
whyChoose: Develop strategic public affairs frameworks that enable proactive rather than reactive engagement with government and regulatory stakeholders
Build credible, influential relationships with policymakers that enhance organisational reputation and create opportunities for constructive policy dialogue
Anticipate and manage regulatory and policy risks more effectively through systematic horizon scanning and strategic stakeholder engagement
Strengthen organisational capability to influence public policy outcomes in ways that support business objectives and societal value creation
Integrate public affairs considerations into corporate strategy, risk management and communications functions for greater organisational coherence
Establish measurable public affairs performance systems that demonstrate clear return on investment and inform continuous improvement
audience: Directors of Government Affairs accountable for strategic government engagement, policy influence and organisational positioning in complex regulatory environments
Heads of Public Policy responsible for leading engagement teams, shaping advocacy strategies and advising senior leadership on government relations
Government Relations Managers tasked with developing and executing stakeholder engagement plans and maintaining day-to-day government interactions
Public Affairs Managers responsible for aligning public affairs messaging with broader organisational communications and reputation management
Policy Advisers supporting policy analysis, advocacy planning and cross-functional coordination on government affairs initiatives
Government Relations Analysts conducting political monitoring, research and preparation of briefing materials for senior-level stakeholder engagement
objectives: By the end of this programme, participants will be able to:
Design integrated public affairs strategies that align organisational objectives with government policy priorities and stakeholder expectations across complex regulatory environments
Conduct comprehensive political landscape analysis and stakeholder mapping to identify influence opportunities, risks and engagement pathways
Develop and execute government engagement plans that build credible, trust-based relationships with policymakers and public sector stakeholders
Apply strategic advocacy and communication techniques to influence policy outcomes while maintaining ethical standards and transparency
Establish robust systems for monitoring regulatory change, managing policy risk and ensuring organisational compliance and resilience
Prepare for and manage government relations crises with effective communication protocols that protect reputation and maintain stakeholder confidence
Measure and demonstrate the impact of public affairs activities through clear performance frameworks and evaluation methodologies
Build sustainable organisational public affairs capability through leadership engagement, training systems and continuous improvement processes
deliveryApproach: Structured multi-strand learning journey that integrates political analysis, stakeholder strategy development, relationship-building skills and performance measurement across interconnected modules
Facilitated workshops applying strategic frameworks to realistic organisational scenarios with expert guidance and peer collaboration
Case study analysis of public affairs successes and challenges drawn from diverse government and corporate contexts to extract transferable lessons
Hands-on stakeholder mapping and strategy development exercises enabling participants to create complete government engagement plans for their own organisational contexts
Simulation activities and role-play focused on high-stakes government interactions, difficult conversations and crisis response situations
Personal application projects with structured coaching that support immediate translation of course concepts into current professional responsibilities and upcoming challenges
courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
Foundations of Public Affairs Strategy and Government Relations
• Understanding the strategic role of public affairs in achieving organisational objectives within complex policy and regulatory environments
• Examining the principles of effective government engagement and the value of building long-term, trust-based relationships with public sector stakeholders
• Identifying the key components of a successful public affairs strategy including research, planning, execution and evaluation
• Recognising the ethical foundations and transparency requirements that underpin credible public affairs practice
• Mapping the interface between public affairs, corporate strategy, risk management and stakeholder communications
• Establishing the organisational case for investing in structured public affairs capability and professional development

MODULE 02
Political Landscape Analysis and Stakeholder Mapping
• Conducting systematic analysis of political, regulatory and policy environments to identify opportunities, risks and influence pathways
• Developing comprehensive stakeholder maps that identify key government actors, decision-makers, influencers and potential allies or opponents
• Applying open government principles and transparency frameworks to enhance credibility and reduce perception of undue influence
• Utilising research methods, intelligence gathering and horizon scanning to anticipate policy developments and legislative changes
• Prioritising stakeholders based on influence, interest and alignment with organisational objectives
• Creating dynamic stakeholder engagement plans that adapt to changing political contexts and organisational priorities

MODULE 03
Developing Integrated Government Engagement Strategies
• Designing multi-channel government engagement strategies that align with broader organisational goals and public policy priorities
• Integrating public affairs objectives into corporate planning, risk management and communications functions
• Developing clear messaging frameworks, policy positions and advocacy narratives that resonate with government audiences
• Establishing governance structures, roles and approval processes for government engagement activities
• Balancing proactive relationship-building with reactive issue management and crisis response capabilities
• Creating implementation road maps with clear milestones, responsibilities and resource requirements

MODULE 04
Building and Maintaining Credible Government Relationships
• Practising techniques for initiating, nurturing and sustaining productive relationships with government officials and policymakers at various levels
• Understanding the protocols, etiquette and professional norms that govern effective interactions with public sector stakeholders
• Developing skills in briefing, presenting and communicating complex issues to busy government audiences with clarity and impact
• Managing expectations, building trust and demonstrating organisational value through consistent, transparent engagement
• Handling difficult conversations, disagreements and conflicting priorities with diplomacy and professionalism
• Establishing internal systems for tracking interactions, managing contacts and ensuring institutional memory in government relations

MODULE 05
Policy Advocacy, Influence and Strategic Communication
• Developing evidence-based policy advocacy approaches that contribute constructively to public policy development
• Crafting compelling submissions, position papers and presentations that influence legislative and regulatory outcomes
• Utilising coalition-building, partnership strategies and third-party advocacy to amplify organisational voice
• Managing media and public communications in support of government engagement objectives while maintaining appropriate boundaries
• Navigating the ethical considerations and disclosure requirements associated with advocacy and lobbying activities
• Measuring and communicating the impact of advocacy efforts on policy development and organisational interests

MODULE 06
Managing Regulatory Change, Compliance and Policy Risk
• Establishing robust systems for monitoring, interpreting and responding to regulatory developments and policy shifts
• Integrating public affairs insights into organisational risk management, compliance and strategic planning processes
• Developing contingency plans and scenario-based strategies for managing policy uncertainty and regulatory change
• Engaging constructively with regulators and policymakers during consultation processes and implementation phases
• Building organisational resilience through proactive relationship management and early engagement in emerging policy issues
• Ensuring alignment between public affairs activities, legal compliance and corporate governance standards

MODULE 07
Crisis Communication and Reputation Protection in Government Relations
• Preparing for and managing government relations crises including regulatory investigations, policy controversies and reputational challenges
• Developing crisis communication protocols that maintain credibility with government stakeholders while protecting organisational interests
• Coordinating internal response teams, external advisors and government liaison during high-pressure situations
• Learning from past crises and near-misses to strengthen future preparedness and organisational learning
• Balancing transparency requirements with legal and commercial sensitivities in crisis situations
• Rebuilding trust and relationships with government stakeholders following incidents or controversies

MODULE 08
Measuring Impact, Evaluation and Building Sustainable Public Affairs Capability
• Designing performance metrics, KPIs and evaluation frameworks for public affairs and government engagement activities
• Conducting regular reviews and impact assessments to demonstrate value and inform strategic adjustments
• Developing internal training, capability building and knowledge management systems that sustain high standards of public affairs practice
• Integrating public affairs considerations into leadership development, succession planning and organisational culture
• Positioning public affairs as a strategic function that contributes to long-term organisational success and societal value
• Creating continuous improvement cycles that incorporate feedback, emerging best practices and evolving stakeholder expectations
expectedOutcomes: Participants will be able to:
Comprehensive public affairs strategy documents and government engagement plans ready for immediate organisational implementation
Detailed stakeholder maps, political analysis reports and influence pathway documents tailored to participants' organisational contexts
Documented crisis preparedness protocols and communication frameworks for government relations scenarios
Clear performance measurement frameworks and evaluation tools to track public affairs impact and demonstrate value to leadership
Practical advocacy toolkits including position papers, submission templates and messaging frameworks
Sustainable capability building plans including training curricula and knowledge management systems for ongoing public affairs excellence
organisationalImpact: Enhanced strategic alignment between organisational objectives and government policy environments through more effective public affairs practice
Reduced regulatory and reputational risk through proactive stakeholder engagement and early identification of policy developments
Improved ability to influence policy outcomes in support of organisational interests and broader public value
Stronger internal integration of public affairs with strategy, risk, compliance and communications functions
Greater organisational resilience and adaptability in navigating complex, changing regulatory and political landscapes
Sustainable improvement in government relations capability that protects and enhances organisational reputation over time
personalImpact: Advanced strategic expertise in public affairs strategy development, government engagement and policy influence at organisational level
Enhanced capability to lead government relations functions, advise senior leaders and represent the organisation in high-level stakeholder interactions
Clearer professional pathway towards senior roles in government affairs, public policy, external relations and corporate affairs leadership
Immediately applicable skills in stakeholder mapping, strategy development, advocacy and crisis management that strengthen current responsibilities
Expanded perspective on the strategic value of transparent, ethical public affairs practices in building long-term organisational success
Greater personal confidence and credibility when engaging with government stakeholders, presenting policy positions and managing complex stakeholder dynamics
General Notes
Sector customisation available on request
Training material provided
Elevoris Certificate of Training issued to all participants
Optional post-programme advisory coaching available

Effective public affairs strategy and skilled government engagement are essential for organisations seeking to navigate regulatory complexity, influence policy outcomes and build enduring stakeholder trust. By mastering these capabilities, professionals position their organisations to anticipate change, manage risk and contribute constructively to the policy environments in which they operate.

Enrol now in the Public Affairs Strategy & Government Engagement Programme to develop the strategic frameworks, relationship-building expertise and policy influence skills required to lead with confidence in complex government and stakeholder environments.

Participants develop practical capability to align quality strategies with internationally recognised healthcare quality standards while embedding evidence-based approaches across their organisations. This course can be facilitated in London, Dubai, Riyadh, Nairobi, and other major business centres on client-preferred dates.
whyChoose: Design and implement comprehensive quality management systems that integrate internationally recognised healthcare quality standards with organisational strategy, governance and operational processes
Establish robust performance measurement frameworks, key quality indicators and reporting systems that provide actionable intelligence for leadership and regulatory accountability
Apply structured process improvement methodologies to identify, analyse and eliminate sources of waste, variation and inefficiency across healthcare operations and service pathways
Integrate value-based healthcare principles and outcomes-driven approaches into quality strategies to enhance patient-centred care while optimising resource utilisation and demonstrating value
Develop governance, compliance and accountability mechanisms that strengthen regulatory readiness, risk mitigation and organisational learning cultures
Build sustainable quality improvement capability that engages staff at all levels, embeds continuous improvement into daily operations and delivers lasting organisational impact

Operations Managers and Service Delivery Leads tasked with embedding quality standards, reducing variation and optimising processes within their areas of responsibility
Clinical Governance Coordinators and Quality Specialists supporting the development, audit and continuous refinement of quality frameworks and reporting
Quality and Performance Analysts conducting data analysis, indicator development, benchmarking and evidence-based improvement project support
Quality Improvement Officers and Administrators facilitating documentation, training logistics, compliance tracking and project coordination under senior direction

MODULE 01
Foundations of Quality Management in Healthcare Organisations
• Examining the evolution and core principles of quality management as applied to healthcare organisational contexts and service delivery systems
• Defining the distinctive requirements of quality management in healthcare including stakeholder expectations, regulatory environments and outcome accountability
• Identifying common sources of variation, waste and quality gaps in healthcare operations and their impact on organisational performance and stakeholder trust
• Establishing the foundational elements of effective quality management systems including leadership commitment, process focus and data-driven decision-making
• Recognising the role of organisational culture, staff engagement and governance structures in sustaining quality improvement over time
• Mapping the relationship between quality management, patient safety, operational efficiency and strategic organisational objectives in healthcare settings

MODULE 02
Quality Frameworks and Internationally Recognised Standards
• Exploring the structure and application of internationally recognised healthcare quality standards and accreditation frameworks in organisational settings
• Designing quality management system architectures that integrate standard requirements with local operational realities and strategic priorities
• Establishing processes for gap analysis, compliance mapping and system documentation aligned with quality framework expectations
• Managing the implications of standards implementation on resource allocation, process redesign and staff competency development
• Integrating quality framework requirements into existing governance, risk and performance management systems
• Building organisational capability to achieve and maintain alignment with internationally recognised healthcare quality standards through disciplined implementation

MODULE 03
Performance Measurement and Quality Indicator Development
• Developing comprehensive performance measurement frameworks that capture quality dimensions relevant to patients, regulators, payers and internal stakeholders
• Selecting, defining and operationalising key quality indicators that provide meaningful insights into safety, effectiveness, timeliness and patient-centredness
• Establishing data collection, validation, aggregation and reporting processes that ensure indicator reliability and usefulness for decision-making
• Designing dashboards, scorecards and reporting mechanisms that communicate quality performance clearly to governance bodies and operational leaders
• Integrating performance measurement with strategic planning, resource allocation and accountability mechanisms
• Building organisational capability to use quality indicators proactively for monitoring, benchmarking and driving targeted improvement

MODULE 04
Process Improvement Methodologies for Healthcare Operations
• Applying structured process improvement methodologies to map, analyse and optimise healthcare operational processes and service pathways
• Identifying and eliminating sources of waste, delay, error and variation that compromise quality and efficiency in healthcare delivery
• Establishing rapid improvement cycles, standard work practices and visual management techniques adapted to healthcare operational environments
• Managing change and staff engagement requirements associated with process redesign and new standard operating procedures
• Integrating process improvement with quality management systems, risk mitigation and performance measurement frameworks
• Building organisational capability to sustain process improvements and embed continuous improvement thinking into daily operations

MODULE 05
Data Analytics and Evidence-Based Quality Improvement
• Utilising healthcare data analytics techniques to identify patterns, trends and improvement opportunities within quality and performance datasets
• Applying statistical process control, root cause analysis and other analytical tools to diagnose quality issues and evaluate intervention effectiveness
• Establishing processes for transforming raw operational and clinical data into actionable quality intelligence for managers and leaders
• Managing data quality, integrity and governance requirements to support credible quality reporting and decision-making
• Integrating analytics capabilities with existing quality management and governance structures
• Building organisational capability to become more data-driven in quality monitoring, improvement prioritisation and outcome evaluation

MODULE 06
Patient Safety Integration and Risk-Based Quality Approaches
• Examining the interface between quality management and patient safety systems from an organisational governance and leadership perspective
• Designing integrated approaches that link quality improvement initiatives with proactive risk identification, assessment and mitigation processes
• Establishing mechanisms for learning from incidents, near misses and complaints to drive systemic quality enhancements
• Managing the cultural and behavioural dimensions of safety and quality improvement across multidisciplinary teams and departments
• Integrating safety and quality considerations into operational planning, resource decisions and performance oversight
• Building organisational capability to maintain high reliability principles and resilient systems that prevent harm and promote continuous learning

MODULE 07
Leadership, Culture and Engagement for Quality Excellence
• Exploring the critical role of leadership at all levels in creating and sustaining cultures of quality and continuous improvement
• Developing strategies for engaging clinical and non-clinical staff in quality initiatives and building ownership for improvement outcomes
• Establishing communication, recognition and capability-building approaches that embed quality values into organisational behaviour and decision-making
• Managing resistance to change and fostering psychological safety that encourages reporting, innovation and collaborative problem-solving
• Integrating quality leadership development with broader talent management and succession planning processes
• Building organisational capability to develop quality champions and distributed leadership that sustains improvement momentum

MODULE 08
Governance, Compliance and Accountability in Quality Systems
• Designing governance structures, committees and reporting lines that provide effective oversight of quality performance and improvement progress
• Establishing accountability frameworks that clarify roles, responsibilities and escalation pathways for quality-related issues and risks
• Developing compliance monitoring, audit and assurance processes that support regulatory readiness and internal control effectiveness
• Managing the interface between quality governance, corporate governance, risk management and external regulatory requirements
• Integrating quality governance into board and executive decision-making processes with clear metrics and narrative reporting
• Building organisational capability to maintain robust, transparent quality governance that protects patients, staff and organisational reputation

MODULE 09
Value-Based Healthcare and Outcomes-Driven Quality Improvement
• Examining the principles of value-based healthcare and their implications for quality management and performance improvement strategies
• Designing approaches that link quality improvement efforts to measurable outcomes, cost-effectiveness and patient-reported experience and outcome measures
• Establishing processes for identifying high-value interventions, reducing low-value activities and optimising resource utilisation through quality lenses
• Managing the shift from volume-based to value-based performance metrics and the associated cultural and system changes required
• Integrating value-based considerations into quality strategy, commissioning decisions and provider performance management
• Building organisational capability to deliver and demonstrate value through quality improvement in evolving healthcare funding and accountability environments

MODULE 10
Sustaining Quality Improvement and Building Organisational Learning
• Developing sustainability frameworks that embed quality improvement into organisational strategy, operations and culture for long-term impact
• Establishing knowledge management, lesson capture and best practice sharing mechanisms that accelerate organisational learning from quality initiatives
• Designing recognition, reward and capability development systems that maintain staff engagement and build internal quality improvement expertise
• Managing the evolution of quality management systems in response to changing regulatory, technological and strategic contexts
• Integrating quality sustainability into performance management, leadership accountability and strategic planning cycles
• Building organisational capability to treat quality improvement as a core strategic competency rather than a series of isolated projects
• Assessment & Evaluation
• Upon successful completion of this programme, an Elevoris Certificate of Training will be awarded to delegates who meet the passing requirements.

Enrol now in the Quality Management & Performance Improvement in Healthcare Certificate to develop the expertise, methodologies and strategic insight required to lead quality transformation and deliver lasting improvements in safety, outcomes and operational excellence.
