Supply Chain Directors and Logistics Managers overseeing end-to-end fulfilment and distribution networks
Inventory and Stock Control Managers seeking to optimise storage, accuracy and replenishment processes
Health, Safety and Environment Managers operating in warehouse and logistics facilities
Procurement and 3PL Contract Managers accountable for warehouse services, outsourcing and performance agreements
Operations Excellence, Lean and Continuous Improvement Leads driving warehouse transformation initiatives
objectives: By the end of this programme, participants will be able to:

Design comprehensive warehouse strategies and operational frameworks that align facility capabilities, processes and performance targets with organisational service, cost and sustainability objectives
Apply warehouse layout optimisation and storage system selection techniques to maximise space utilisation, improve picking efficiency and reduce operational costs
Implement robust inventory handling, order fulfilment and despatch processes that enhance accuracy, speed and reliability while minimising errors and damage
Integrate appropriate warehouse technology, data analytics and automation solutions to provide real-time visibility, improve decision quality and support continuous improvement
Establish and enforce rigorous safety, compliance, risk and security management systems that protect personnel, assets and operational integrity in warehouse environments
Develop workforce planning, training and performance management approaches that build capable, motivated and high-performing warehouse teams
Apply lean principles, waste elimination and structured problem-solving methodologies to drive continuous improvement and operational excellence across warehouse operations
Design integrated performance measurement frameworks, dashboards and governance mechanisms that demonstrate clear warehouse contribution to supply chain and organisational outcomes
deliveryApproach: In-depth analysis of real-world warehouse case studies illustrating design successes, operational challenges and lessons in efficiency, safety and performance improvement
Interactive workshops focused on warehouse layout design, storage optimisation, process mapping, technology selection and performance dashboard development
Simulations exploring layout decisions, picking strategies, safety scenarios and workforce scheduling under realistic operational constraints
Structured group exercises developing warehouse improvement plans, standard operating procedures, risk assessments and KPI frameworks using authentic organisational data
Facilitated peer learning sessions for sharing implementation experiences, cultural challenges and proven approaches to sustaining warehouse excellence
Personal and organisational action planning with expert feedback to support immediate application and measurable performance gains in ongoing warehouse operations
courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
Strategic Role and Governance of Warehouse Operations
• Examining the contribution of warehouse operations to overall supply chain strategy, customer service, cost efficiency and competitive advantage
• Identifying key external drivers including e-commerce growth, sustainability expectations, labour availability and technological change affecting warehouse decisions
• Mapping the full warehouse lifecycle from strategic planning and design through operations, maintenance and continuous improvement or reconfiguration
• Establishing clear strategic objectives, service level agreements and value propositions for warehouse functions that secure cross-functional alignment and investment
• Recognising the interplay between warehouse operations, inventory management, procurement, transport and broader organisational performance frameworks
• Conducting organisational assessments to diagnose current warehouse maturity, capability gaps and opportunities for strategic and operational improvement

MODULE 02
Warehouse Design, Layout Optimisation and Capacity Planning
• Applying structured frameworks to determine warehouse size, configuration and location requirements aligned with demand patterns and supply chain strategy
• Designing optimal internal layouts including receiving, storage, picking, packing, despatch and returns zones to maximise flow and minimise travel time
• Selecting appropriate storage systems, racking configurations and material handling equipment based on product characteristics, volume and handling requirements
• Conducting capacity planning, space utilisation analysis and future-proofing assessments to accommodate growth and changing product profiles
• Integrating sustainability considerations including energy efficiency, carbon reduction and responsible material use into warehouse design decisions
• Establishing governance processes for layout approval, change control and periodic review to maintain optimal configuration over time

MODULE 03
Inventory Storage, Handling and Order Fulfilment Excellence
• Developing receiving, put-away, storage and replenishment processes that maintain inventory accuracy and protect product integrity
• Designing picking, packing and despatch workflows that optimise speed, accuracy and ergonomics while meeting service commitments
• Implementing slotting strategies, product placement logic and dynamic allocation approaches that reduce travel time and improve fulfilment efficiency
• Managing returns, reverse logistics, quarantine and damaged goods processes to minimise value loss and operational disruption
• Establishing quality control checkpoints, inspection protocols and error-proofing measures throughout storage and fulfilment operations
• Integrating warehouse handling processes with broader inventory management, demand planning and customer fulfilment systems for seamless execution

MODULE 04
Warehouse Technology, Systems Integration and Digital Enablement
• Assessing current technology maturity and identifying opportunities for warehouse management systems, automation and digital tools to enhance performance
• Evaluating and selecting appropriate technology solutions for inventory tracking, order management, labour management and real-time visibility
• Planning and managing the integration of warehouse systems with enterprise resource planning platforms, transport systems and supplier interfaces
• Applying data analytics to identify performance trends, predict operational issues and support evidence-based decision-making in warehouse operations
• Managing the human and organisational aspects of technology adoption including training, change management and data governance in warehouse environments
• Developing roadmaps for ongoing technology evolution that maintain alignment with organisational digital strategy and emerging capabilities in warehouse management

MODULE 05
Safety, Compliance, Risk and Security Management in Warehouses
• Identifying and assessing the full spectrum of risks in warehouse operations including safety, operational, security, regulatory and environmental risks
• Developing and implementing robust safety management systems, risk assessments and control measures that protect personnel and assets
• Establishing compliance frameworks for health and safety regulations, fire safety, hazardous materials handling and environmental requirements
• Designing and managing physical security, access control and loss prevention measures to protect inventory and facilities from theft and damage
• Integrating warehouse risk and safety considerations into broader organisational risk, insurance and business continuity frameworks
• Building safety-aware cultures and behaviours that encourage proactive hazard identification, incident reporting and continuous improvement in warehouse teams

MODULE 06
Workforce Planning, Productivity and Performance Leadership
• Developing workforce strategies that address labour planning, skills requirements, shift patterns and succession needs in warehouse operations
• Designing and implementing training, competency development and performance management systems that build capable and engaged warehouse teams
• Applying productivity measurement, incentive schemes and continuous improvement approaches to optimise labour utilisation and output quality
• Managing change, communication and employee engagement initiatives that support operational transformation and sustain high performance
• Establishing clear roles, responsibilities and accountability structures for warehouse leadership and team supervision
• Building leadership capability at all levels to drive safety, quality, efficiency and continuous improvement behaviours across warehouse operations

MODULE 07
Lean Principles, Waste Reduction and Continuous Improvement in Warehousing
• Applying lean thinking and waste elimination methodologies to identify and remove non-value-adding activities in warehouse processes
• Implementing 5S workplace organisation, visual management and standard work practices that stabilise and improve daily operations
• Designing and facilitating kaizen events and rapid improvement workshops focused on specific warehouse processes and performance gaps
• Using structured problem-solving and root cause analysis techniques to address recurring issues in accuracy, productivity and safety
• Integrating lean practices with existing quality, safety and performance management systems for synergistic effect
• Embedding continuous improvement cultures and behaviours that sustain gains and drive ongoing optimisation across warehouse functions

MODULE 08
Supplier, 3PL and Inbound/Outbound Interface Management
• Managing the interface between warehouse operations and suppliers, carriers and 3PL providers to ensure seamless inbound and outbound flows
• Establishing performance frameworks, service level agreements and continuous improvement mechanisms with warehouse service providers and partners
• Designing and optimising receiving, put-away and despatch processes that integrate effectively with transport schedules and supplier capabilities
• Developing collaborative approaches with key suppliers and logistics partners that improve visibility, reduce lead times and enhance reliability
• Managing contract administration, performance monitoring and issue resolution processes for outsourced warehouse and logistics services
• Building resilience through diversified supplier and carrier relationships and contingency planning for inbound and outbound disruptions

MODULE 09
Performance Measurement, Cost Control and Benefits Realisation
• Designing integrated performance frameworks that connect warehouse metrics to service levels, cost, safety and broader organisational objectives
• Selecting and implementing meaningful KPIs for productivity, accuracy, safety, utilisation, cost per unit and customer service in warehouse operations
• Establishing dashboards, reporting systems and review processes that provide timely visibility and support proactive management intervention
• Conducting structured cost analysis, benchmarking and improvement planning to identify and capture efficiency opportunities
• Tracking and demonstrating the financial and operational benefits of warehouse improvement initiatives through robust measurement and reporting
• Embedding accountability, recognition and continuous improvement governance that sustain performance gains and drive ongoing excellence

MODULE 10
Strategic Leadership, Change and Future-Proofing Warehouse Excellence
• Developing the leadership capabilities required to guide warehouse teams through complexity, change and sustained performance pressure
• Building organisational capability, skills and cultures that embed operational excellence, safety and continuous improvement in warehouse environments
• Anticipating emerging trends in technology, automation, sustainability, labour markets and customer expectations to evolve warehouse strategies proactively
• Establishing knowledge management, lessons learned and capability development processes that protect and enhance warehouse expertise
• Positioning the warehouse functions as a strategic contributor to organisational competitiveness, resilience and responsible performance
• Creating actionable roadmaps for advancing warehouse management maturity aligned with organisational capacity, digital evolution and strategic priorities
• Assessment & Evaluation
• Upon successful completion of this programme, an Elevoris Certificate of Training will be awarded to delegates who meet the passing requirements.

courses.syllabus:
MODULE 01
Strategic Foundations of Supplier Relationship Management
• Examining the evolution of supplier relationships from transactional purchasing to strategic partnership models that deliver competitive advantage
• Identifying the strategic drivers for supplier relationship management including cost pressures, risk exposure, innovation needs and sustainability expectations
• Mapping the full supplier relationship lifecycle from initial selection and onboarding through performance management, development and strategic evolution or exit
• Establishing clear strategic objectives, value propositions and success metrics for supplier relationship management that secure executive alignment and cross-functional support
• Recognising the interplay between supplier relationship management, category strategy, contract management and broader supply chain performance frameworks
• Conducting organisational assessments to diagnose current supplier relationship maturity, capability gaps and opportunities for strategic improvement

MODULE 02
Supplier Segmentation, Categorisation and Strategic Alignment
• Applying structured segmentation frameworks that consider spend, risk, strategic importance, performance potential and relationship complexity
• Developing differentiated relationship strategies, governance intensity and resource allocation for strategic, tactical and transactional supplier categories
• Aligning supplier segmentation with category management, sourcing strategy and organisational priorities to ensure coherent portfolio management
• Establishing clear criteria and decision frameworks for supplier tiering, key supplier identification and strategic partnership designation
• Building governance mechanisms for segmentation review, supplier movement between categories and portfolio rebalancing over time
• Communicating segmentation logic and relationship expectations to internal stakeholders and suppliers to ensure consistent application and understanding

MODULE 03
Supplier Selection, Onboarding and Relationship Initiation
• Designing robust supplier selection processes that evaluate capability, cultural fit, risk profile and strategic alignment alongside commercial and technical criteria
• Developing structured onboarding programmes that accelerate supplier integration, establish clear expectations and build foundational relationship strength
• Establishing governance arrangements, roles, responsibilities and communication protocols at the start of supplier relationships
• Managing the transition from sourcing to ongoing relationship management, including knowledge transfer and performance baseline setting
• Building early warning systems and relationship health indicators that enable proactive management from the outset
• Creating supplier portals, information-sharing protocols and collaborative platforms that support effective relationship initiation and ongoing interaction

MODULE 04
Performance Measurement, KPIs and Balanced Scorecard Development
• Designing comprehensive performance measurement frameworks that connect supplier performance to organisational cost, quality, delivery, innovation and sustainability outcomes
• Selecting and implementing meaningful KPIs across financial, operational, quality, risk, compliance and relationship dimensions
• Developing balanced scorecards that provide clear, actionable visibility into supplier performance while avoiding metric overload or gaming behaviours
• Establishing performance review cadences, data collection processes and dashboard systems that support timely decision-making and intervention
• Integrating supplier performance data with internal systems and broader supply chain performance reporting for enterprise visibility
• Using performance insights to inform contract adjustments, development priorities and strategic relationship decisions

MODULE 05
Supplier Development, Collaboration and Capability Building
• Identifying development opportunities that deliver mutual value through process improvement, innovation, capacity expansion or sustainability enhancement
• Designing and implementing structured supplier development programmes including training, joint projects, knowledge transfer and capability-building initiatives
• Establishing collaborative improvement mechanisms, joint performance reviews and shared gain-sharing arrangements that incentivise continuous improvement
• Managing the interface between internal improvement initiatives and supplier operations to prevent sub-optimisation and maximise end-to-end value
• Building long-term partnership approaches with strategic suppliers that foster trust, transparency and joint strategic planning
• Measuring and demonstrating the return on supplier development investment through tracked performance improvements and value creation

MODULE 06
Risk Management, Compliance and Ethical Governance in Supplier Relationships
• Identifying and assessing the full spectrum of risks arising from supplier relationships including operational, financial, reputational, regulatory and sustainability risks
• Developing integrated risk management frameworks, mitigation strategies and contingency plans tailored to different supplier categories and relationship types
• Establishing compliance monitoring, audit and assurance processes that verify supplier adherence to contractual, regulatory and ethical requirements
• Managing ethical considerations including labour standards, human rights, environmental practices and anti-corruption expectations across the supply base
• Integrating supplier risk and compliance considerations into broader organisational risk, business continuity and corporate responsibility frameworks
• Building risk-aware cultures and behaviours that encourage proactive identification, transparent reporting and collaborative mitigation with suppliers

MODULE 07
Contract Administration, Governance and Issue Resolution
• Establishing robust contract administration processes that maintain alignment between contractual obligations and day-to-day relationship management
• Designing governance forums, escalation protocols and decision rights that enable timely resolution of issues while preserving relationship health
• Managing contract variations, performance adjustments and change processes in ways that protect value and strengthen partnership over time
• Developing structured issue resolution and dispute prevention approaches that address root causes and prevent recurrence
• Integrating contract performance data with relationship management activities to ensure commercial terms support strategic objectives
• Building organisational capability in contract interpretation, negotiation of adjustments and commercial management of supplier relationships

MODULE 08
Data Analytics, Digital Tools and Performance Visibility
• Assessing current data quality, system capabilities and technology maturity to identify opportunities for enhanced supplier performance visibility
• Applying analytics to identify performance trends, predict emerging issues and prioritise high-impact improvement opportunities across the supplier portfolio
• Evaluating and integrating digital tools for supplier performance dashboards, real-time monitoring, collaborative platforms and automated alerting
• Establishing data governance, master data management and integration requirements that support reliable supplier performance decision-making
• Using predictive indicators and advanced analytics to move from reactive performance management to proactive relationship optimisation
• Building organisational capability to interpret supplier performance data and translate insights into targeted relationship interventions

MODULE 09
Sustainability, ESG and Responsible Supplier Practices
• Integrating environmental, social and governance criteria into supplier relationship management strategies, selection and performance frameworks
• Developing supplier sustainability assessment, improvement and reporting processes that align with organisational ESG commitments and stakeholder expectations
• Establishing collaborative approaches with suppliers to reduce environmental impact, improve labour practices and enhance responsible sourcing across the supply chain
• Managing sustainability-related risks, opportunities and compliance requirements within supplier relationships
• Measuring and communicating the sustainability performance of the supplier base to internal and external stakeholders
• Embedding responsible supplier practices into standard relationship management processes, contracts and continuous improvement activities

MODULE 10
Strategic Leadership, Continuous Improvement and Relationship Excellence
• Developing the leadership capabilities required to guide supplier relationship transformation and sustain high performance under complexity and change
• Building organisational capability, skills and cultures that embed high-performance supplier relationship management across procurement and supply chain functions
• Anticipating emerging trends in supplier markets, technology, sustainability requirements and geopolitical factors to evolve relationship strategies proactively
• Establishing knowledge management, lessons learned and capability development processes that protect and enhance supplier relationship expertise
• Positioning supplier relationship management as a strategic contributor to organisational competitiveness, resilience and responsible performance
• Creating actionable roadmaps for advancing supplier relationship management maturity aligned with organisational capacity and strategic priorities

sourceRecord.courseOverview: Many organisations fail to realise the full strategic value from their supplier base because relationships remain transactional, performance oversight is fragmented and development opportunities are missed. This supplier relationship management training equips practitioners with integrated frameworks to design, govern and optimise supplier relationships that deliver measurable commercial, operational and sustainability outcomes. Participants develop practical capabilities in segmentation, performance measurement, collaborative development and risk governance while embedding data-driven decision-making and continuous improvement. The vendor performance course emphasis enables organisations to move beyond compliance monitoring towards genuine partnership models that enhance resilience, innovation and long-term value creation. This course can be facilitated in London, Dubai, Kuala Lumpur, Nairobi, and other major business centres on client-preferred dates.
